Artificial constructs, projections, or possibly beings based on a human template but heavily modified (195, 196). Polder Dossman is identified or suspected to be one (175, 195, 196, 203). Hector Bogus is an "Eidolon Lord" (180) or "eidolon-chief" (194) who creates miniature, tortured eidolons (181–183). The term is linked to the Media Lords (180). A sequence of nine eidolons, progressing from stone to "rapture-flesh," is described, which turn on their creator (196). James Morey fears becoming a "mere eidolon of an eidolon" following a cult figure (101).
Eidolon-Godlings
Hector Bogus's dismissive term for potentially powerful but artificial figures like Polder Dossman (197).
Eidolon-Masters
Creators or manipulators of eidolons, like those who experimented on Polder Dossman (212) or Hector Bogus (209).
Enclaves
Distinct alternate worlds or realities often characterized by peculiar biological or social rules, such as those where boy children are born with beards or females fully formed (17), or where young adult males are seasonally horned and hoofed (17). Pilger Tisman's failed death performance might have been analyzed differently using more sophisticated equipment found in "other enclaves" (2).
End of Pyrotechnics
A phrase denoting the moment of Pilger Tisman's apparent death (the cessation of vital signs and the extinguishing of aura and tone), which lasts only three seconds before his successful worldjump and the reappearance of his aura and tone (9).
Environs
Used generally to refer to specific alternate worlds or settings, such as the one recalled by Pilgrim Dusmano where males are horned and hoofed (17), or the location ("that environs") where Cyrus Evenhand feels diminished by Pilgrim's attack (25). Pilgrim plans for generational support across various environs (30).
Eschatological Things
The four final realities or concepts, for which Prime World serves as the "base and anchor" (21). The laughter directed at Polder's bogus-gold tooth plug comes from "creatures of every eschatological case" (200).
Fate
Personified by or equivalent to the High Seven Dice Throwers; their collective dicing determines outcomes (201). Polder Dossman's destiny is said to ride on a coin flip (209). "Fair fate" is questioned for not granting Cyrus Evenhand an uneventful first day as Consul (81).
Fetish Hands
Hairy, gripping appendages associated with Prime World, imagined to emerge from the earth and seize victims with bone-crushing strength (21).
Fetishistic
An adjective used by Pilgrim Dusmano to describe the meticulous, "crabbed," and irrational "ultimate accounts" kept on Prime World (20). Noah Zontik uses it to characterize prime people, should they mirror Prime World's logic (22).
Fever
A quantifiable physiological reaction to visual stimuli; the Daylight Museum prohibits art causing more than a four-point rise (59). Prime World is described as inducing "miasmic fever" (21), and Noah Zontik calls the hypothetical original Pilgrim "fevered" (23).
Fifteen-Year Leap
The possible illusion of a time interval created by Pilger Tisman's world-jump "to upstream cliffs," potentially explaining the time elapsed between his death and the main narrative events (12).
Final Things
Used in several contexts: 1. The four eschatological realities anchored by Prime World (21). 2. Absolute conclusions or ends, which Pilgrim claims to avoid "forever" (131). 3. The ultimate events unfolding during the narrative's climax, as noted by Doctor Judas Raffels (108). 4. The nature of time and direction, which Pilgrim insists are never final (75). 5. Death, described by Dusmano as seldom final (17), although Cyrus Evenhand's killing must be final (26). 6. Outcomes in the Narrow Corner, which the Holy Knacker declares are final (130, 132).
Folk Ocean
An alternative name for the Group Unconscious, the underlying psychic medium where testaments can be published (142).
Frame of Mind
The mental state required for successful world-jumping: apprehensive, nervous, determined, daring, creative, defiant, and open (39). Pilgrim reminds the Pyms of this before their dispatch (39).
Freedom of Entry
A right asserted by the militia under Media Lord authority, overriding physical barriers in the name of "Total Freedom" (114).
Fringies
A category of people (along with nonscientists, pseudos, etc.) who correctly intuited that alternate worlds occupy the same local space (14).
Fury-Child
An alternate designation for the hostile, shape-shifting child entity encountered in the Narrow Corner (124, 160).
Gestes
The narrative or legendary accounts of a cult; Pilgrim Dusmano feels his clumsy killing must be heavily revised before entering the gestes of his own cult (25).
Ghost Worlds
Horrendous counterworlds erected by tricky departing cult figures that impinge, sometimes physically, on the real world, causing dislocation, disturbance, erosion, and fright (4). Contrasted with the less harmful "after-appearances" or "harmless ghosts" of earlier times (3–4).
Ghosts
Relatively harmless "after-appearances" resulting from individuals carrying only minimal personal baggage (memory, identity, consciousness) forward from the "death drama" in earlier times (3). Distinct from the later, more malevolent "ghost worlds" (4).
Giants
Dimwitted inhabitants of the lowering sky over Prime World, considered the "pride of prime" (24). Also, a term used for powerful figures, like the "money giants" who lust after fortunes (95) or "good giants" whose toppling brings rich satiation (50).
Gout (of Water)
A drop or portion; Albert Fineface promises Pelion that his testament will be published in every gout of water from the Folk Ocean (142).
Grain of Sand
Used by Pilgrim Dusmano to illustrate the infinitesimal probability of encountering Prime World ("as small as a grain of sand compared to a solar system medium in size") (20). Noah Zontik retorts that even a grain of sand is a nuisance in a giant's shoe (20).
Grays
One of the nonchromatic colors noted in Pilger Tisman's unique aura (7).
Gripping Hands (Sinewy)
Characteristic of Prime World and its inhabitants; hairy, fetish hands that emerge from the earth to grip ankles with bone-crushing strength (21). Prime people are those "with the sinewy, gripping hands" (22).
Group Unconscious
An alternative name for the "Folk Ocean," the underlying psychic medium containing collective testaments and memories, into which Pelion Tuscamondo buys the right to publish his image (142, 144).
Guilt
Considered an illusion, unreal, according to Pilgrim Dusmano's amoral philosophy derived from the existence of alternate worlds (16). Also used regarding the coroner's feeling when certifying world-jumpers as simply 'dead' (11).
Gyne Peribebleene-ton-Helion
An archetype described as "Woman Wrapped-in-the-Sun," listed alongside Hermes, Homunculus, Moloch, Fisherman, Huracan, and Beggar-King (155).
Hand of Heaven
A meteorological manipulation, apparently contractable, which points down at its designated subject (161, 163, 168). Polder Dossman uses a visible version, paid for with gold (168), activates it to impress locals (163), modifies it (161), and puts it on standby (161). It possesses a genuine, invisible counterpart with a cloudy subscript (“Protect this least of mine”) specifically intended for Og Scath as protector (168). Hector Bogus, as an Eidetic Lord, can modify the Hand’s phenomena, adding thunder, lightning, gold sparkle, and specific scents (184), but later uses it impulsively to seize Polder and dip him in corrosive sublimate (190–191), an action deemed unethical (191). Polder adopts its pointing gesture (168). The Hand is destroyed by Polder's mountain-moving feat (206), an event attributed to Polder having broken it (207).
Heads Will Roll
A contemporary song hit whistled with grim humor by Jude Ravel (Doctor) after Tisman’s successful world-jump prompts the brigadier of police to threaten repercussions (10). Judas Raffels (Doctor) also whistles the tune while leading the militia toward Pilgrim, anticipating an execution (114).
Hell
Presented as one of only two ways off the dreaded Prime World, paradoxically considered the more bearable option by Pilgrim Dusmano (21). It is the potential destination for the tenth part of Polder Dossman that does not reside in the Nine Worlds (208), and Polder fears Prime World partly because it is rumored to be one of Hell's gates (208). Og Scath is fated to follow Polder there if necessary (207), and Hector Bogus maliciously wishes Polder there (208). It is also depicted as a potential location ("out in the Southgate complex") for experiencing extreme sensations (59), and as a place where certain pottery is fired (60). The Legacy's opening promise of pleasure before hell is qualified by the later account of nine timeless aspects that continue enjoying themselves (133, 146, 208). The Polder-sliver provides a good imitation of a soul screaming eternally in hell (214, 215).
High Seven Dice Throwers
An esoteric, high-status group associated with Fate, possessing seven positions (201). A vacancy exists due to the disappearance of Merope (197). Moira Morey asserts that it must be believed Polder Dossman has become one of the seven, regardless of the truth (198), a status Polder later claims (201, 203).
Horned and Hoofed
A temporary physical state adopted by young male adults during the rutting season in a particular alternate environs recalled by Pilgrim Dusmano (17).
Identity
One of the potentially weighable aspects (along with memory and consciousness) that dying persons might carry forward with them (3). Pilger Tisman succeeds in taking his identity when he world-jumps (10). Pilgrim Dusmano asserts that the apparent celestial locations of galaxies are merely notes in cipher, as there isn't enough room to write down all their identities in one place (15). The public identity of the assailant Mut is recalled by Pilgrim after waking from the attack (48). Revealing the identity of a Consul is a catalyst for destruction (58, 68).
Identity and Fragmentation
A recurring theme concerning the unstable, composite, and often artiﬁcial nature of the self. The central protagonist exists under numerous names (Pilger Tisman; Pilgrim Dusmano; Pelion Tuscamondo; Palgrave Tacoman; Paladin Tajiman; Polycletus Tasman; Palmas Thasomen; Paulus Theissmand; Pilatus Dosmens; Philemon Dorsetmoon; Philip Dusselmon; Polder Dossman) suggesting a fractured or sequential identity across different realities or "complexes" (146). Noah Zontik argues that Dusmano is a "derivative," a "projection" originating from another's imagination, akin to substanceless "swamp gas" (23), though Dusmano insists he is an "authentic original" (23). Dusmano uses the metaphor of being a "bundle of sticks," a million parallel selves with no single dominant identity (77). This fragmentation extends to consciousness and memory, which are "weighable" substances potentially carried forward after death (3) but are often lost or unreliable (10–11, 160). The concept of Eidolons further complicates identity, suggesting beings (including potentially Polder Dossman) are artiﬁcial constructs built on a human base or entirely fabricated (175, 178, 183, 196). The narrative repeatedly questions the idea of a single, stable self and presents identities that are fluid, multiple, projected, or manufactured.
Illusions
Pilgrim Dusmano contends that recompense, debt, guilt, punishment, and death are merely illusions within the framework of multiple alternate worlds (16). The mountain-moving feat performed by Polder Dossman is stated not to be an illusion (205).
Imago Dei
An archetype mentioned alongside Orpheus, Child Hero, and Kore as having a "new arrival" counterpart (154).
Inconsiderate
The police brigadier's judgment of Pilger Tisman for taking an inconveniently long time to die (5).
Instrumental Guess
The term used for the death-monitors' tentative conclusion, based on their measurements, that memory, identity, or consciousness are the probable "weighable substance" carried forward by jumpers (3).
Integers, Correspondence
Parallel versions or representations of individuals existing on corresponding worlds or "orbs" (30). Pilgrim Dusmano believes his different integers aid one another (30).
JUDAS
Invoked by the curator regarding the betrayal of the Consul's identity (68). Pilgrim Dusmano gleefully embraces the term, praising the "red-murder rapture and the self-murder exultation that the real Judas-goat knew!" (68).
JUGLANS, CEREBRAL
The "remembering acorn"; a small nodule within the brain identified as the storage location for compressed memory "abridgments" and essences (5). Described as a composite of chemical fixes and electrical charges inhabiting patterned wrinkles and grooves (5), it is monitored and "marred" by Dr. Funk during Tisman's death-weighing (5). Its contents are extracted or "stolen" shortly after Tisman's physical death, causing the structure to collapse (9).
JUMP / JUMPER
See World-Jumper / World-Jumping.
Kangaroo (Sentence By)
A method of sentencing apparently available to Cyrus Evenhand, mentioned as an option for dealing with Pilgrim Dusmano, implying an irregular, perhaps summary or predetermined, judgment ("Even if we sentence him by kangaroo, it must be a fair trial and a fair sentence.") (26).
Law, Dunlunk's Fifth
States: "Any action in any world will inevitably set up parallel actions in parallel worlds" (30). It is invoked to explain how shaping younglings on one world affects their counterparts elsewhere (30) and potentially explains Og Scath's sense of prior connection to Polder Dossman (175).
Law, Older
An unspecified law suggested by Og Scath as potentially predating Dunlunk's Fifth Law, possibly explaining the sense of recognition between individuals across parallel existences (175).
Logic
Associated strongly with Prime World, where it takes the form of "absolute logic of total delirium," permitting no deviation (21). Noah Zontik suggests prime people might be logical and dull (22), and calls the original Pilgrim "logical" (23). Pilgrim Dusmano professes to love "antilogy" and blinds himself to logic (117).
Lords of the Zodiac
A group of powerful archetypes. Og Scath asserts Polder Dossman has become one (197). Polder later claims this status (201, 203). Hector Bogus questions its validity (197). Polder considers becoming a "double Lord" representing the reconstituted signs of the camel and the boar (174).
Lords, Eidetic
See Eidetic Lords.
Lords, Wiggly-Word
Polder Dossman's mocking term for Hector Bogus, grouping him with Eidetic, Media, and Advocate Lords (185).
Louden Devil
A figure cited by Pilgrim Dusmano for the saying, "'It is more pleasure to kill one good man than a hundred indifferent men'" (67).
Man-Tone
An alternative term for person-tone, specifically referring to Pilger Tisman's unique, powerful sonic signature (7).
Media
The all-encompassing communication systems, linked by Og Scath to the Eidetic Lords (175) and the Media Lords (80). Polder claims expertise in modifying the "larger media flow" via his own unnamed medium (181). Noah Zontik asserts the Media represent the anti-intellect and anti-illumination (107). Defined by Bogus as including scatter-ray, focus-ray, ether-tinsel, and solid-light transmission, existing only in the "obscenity sort" (184). Responsible for the destruction of Consuls and predicted to destroy Pilgrim (108).
Media Lords
Figures who hold power through control of the Media (107). Associated with the Eidetic Lords (175). Considered by Noah Zontik to be the true Lords of Unreason and Darkness (107). They rule implicitly by election of the populace in the absence of formal officials (107). They attack purpose and hate authority (107), ritually destroy unmasked Consuls (108), and are predicted to destroy Pilgrim in the end (108). Their militia enforces their will (111, 114–115). Hector Bogus is identified as one (180, 185). Og Scath considers them allied with Polder (175). See also Lords, Media.
Media Lords and Eidolons
A linked group of themes concerning the manipulation of reality and identity through communication channels and artiﬁcial constructs. The Media Lords hold the real power in the postanarchic age, displacing formal government (107). Described by Noah Zontik as the "true Lords of Unreason and Darkness," representing the "anti-intellect" and "anti-illumination" (107), they derive power from collective projection rather than formal election (107). They attack purpose, hate authority (107), and ritually destroy ﬁgures of authority like the Consul when unmasked (108). Their tools include pervasive media (scatter-ray, focus-ray, ether-tinsel, solid-light transmission, all classiﬁed by Hector Bogus as "obscenity") (184) and armed Militia (111, 114). Closely allied are the Eidetic Lords (175, 181), seemingly involved in the creation and control of Eidolons, artiﬁcial beings or constructs often built on a human base (195, 196). Polder Dossman is repeatedly suggested or revealed to be such an eidolon (175, 183, 192). Hector Bogus, also an Eidolon Lord (180), demonstrates the power to create, animate, torture, and disanimate miniature eidolons (181–183) and links this to what Polder may be (182–183). The complex joins the novel's concerns with artiﬁciality, the manipulation of reality, the power that comes from controlling information and perception, and the possibility that central ﬁgures are manufactured.
Memory
Considered one of the primary "weighable" substances that can be carried forward after death, along with identity and consciousness (3). Its continuity requires attention during the death transition (17). Pilger Tisman successfully takes his memory with him (10). The knacker warns Pilgrim that his memory might not survive the transition to his new state (92). The Nine Worlds, existing outside time, leave no memory trace (160). Polder's own memory is depicted as unreliable or incomplete regarding past events (173) and details of contracts (161) or faces (175). The pan-morphic cultist in the Narrow Corner is described as being injured in mind and memory (123).
Memory Center
The physical locus of memory within the brain, specifically identified as the cerebral juglans or "remembering acorn," containing memory "abridgments and essences" (9). Pilger Tisman's is still intact immediately after death but is then "stolen" from (9).
Merope
Named as one of the Seven Sisters of the Pleiades (197). Also identified as one of the High Seven Dice Throwers, whose recent disappearance (nearly a decade prior) has created a vacancy in that group (197). Og Scath notes that within his "type-memory," Merope has manifested variously as female (seven times), hermaphrodite (seven times), and male (six times) (197). Merope's return to the sky is noted on the night Polder's cult peaks (198).
Metacosmosis
Pilgrim Dusmano's term for the transmigration or travel between alternate worlds (16).
Meteorological Manipulation
The technical term for phenomena like the Hand from Heaven, which Polder Dossman contracts for and activates (163, 168). Polder also attacks the hecklers using meteorological means (whirlwind, plasma explosion) (202).
Miasmic Fever
An atmospheric and physical condition attributed to Prime World (21). Prime people are likewise potentially "miasmic" (22).
Mockery
A characteristic expression of Pilgrim Dusmano, described as "curling and pleasant" on his mouth (115, 203). Pilger Tisman's resurrected person-tone is also said to possess a "biting mockery" (9).
Moloch
An archetype mentioned in a list including Hermes, Homunculus, and Fisherman (155).
Monster
What Polder Dossman realizes he has become within the "many-monstered interior ocean" of the collective unconscious (170).
Muck
A defining characteristic of Prime World (21). Prime people are described as potentially "mucky" (22).
Mud
The characteristic substance of Prime World (21). Also part of the debris left of Pilgrim Dusmano after he is torn apart by horses (118). Polder Dossman, after achieving clarified form, wonders despairingly if he is still "made out of mud" (130).
Multi-Media Productions
The name appearing on a small advertisement attached to the pointing finger of the Hand From Heaven ("Sky-Signs and Prodigies by Multi-Media Productions. Call us!"); Polder finds this detail displeasing (170).
Murk
The defining atmospheric quality of Prime World (21). Prime people are likewise potentially "murky" (22). Moira Morey suggests filling the eyes of the watchers above the Narrow Corner with murk to render them invisible (122).
Needle, Eye of the
Referenced in relation to the biblical edict concerning the rich, camels, and the kingdom of heaven (121, 133). The Narrow Corner is sometimes called "the Camel's Eye," linking it to this fable (124).
Nets
Metaphorical tools used by the death-monitors (Wilcove Funk; Austin, Jon; Jude Ravel; etc.) in their attempt to capture the escaping consciousness, memory, or identity of dying individuals like Pilger Tisman (7, 11). Tisman successfully evades or escapes these nets (7, 11).
Nodule (Containing)
Refers to the cerebral juglans, which contains the memory patterns and seems "always on the nervous edge of explosion" (6).
Nonchromatic
Describes colors within Pilger Tisman's aura (specifically "a hundred nonchromatic colors") (7). Also used to describe an aspect of Tisman's call-tone, which is translated into audio (6).
Nonsuches
A category of people (along with fringies and pseudos) who correctly understood alternate worlds to occupy the same local space (14).
Notes (on Hand from Heaven)
Refers to the small advertisement ("Sky-Signs and Prodigies by Multi-Media Productions. Call us!") visible on the pointing finger of the Hand from Heaven activated by Polder Dossman; Polder finds the note displeasing and considers having it removed (170).
Ocean
A vast, underlying psychic medium or repository composed of the personal testaments of devils (143). It infuses every mind, memory, creature, and manifestation (142, 144). Pelion Tuscamondo pays to publish his "flame and image" into this ocean (142, 144). Polder Dossman becomes an archetype within this ocean (197), which is also described as the "many-monstered interior ocean" (170).
Orbs, Corresponding
Parallel worlds which contain "correspondenceintegers" or parallel selves (30).
Pallidness, Pulsating
One of the unusual visual effects noted in Pilger Tisman's complex aura (7).
Paraclete
A term used by Pilgrim Dusmano for the replacement or alternate self he can send after himself when he departs a world (77). Lord Fairfronter ironically questions if Pilgrim is a Christus to be sending a Paraclete (104).
Parallel
Used to describe worlds, actions, persons, selves, and bodies existing concurrently but usually separately across different dimensions or aspects (30, 55, 77, 104). Dunlunk's Fifth Law posits that actions inevitably create parallel actions (30). Pilgrim shapes "correspondence-integers" on parallel orbs (30). He considers his "sticks" to be parallel persons (77) and claims nothing of himself will be lost as he can be recognized in another parallel (78). Such existences may be linked by laws older than Dunlunk's (175). The concept explains shared or reflected memories between individuals like Dusmano and Noah Zontik, or Polder and Og Scath (32, 175).
Pattern
A term used in several contexts: 1. The underlying structure or template of memory contained within the cerebral juglans, holding power even when empty of detail (6). Taking these patterns is like stealing holes or tunnels (6). Pilger Tisman's memory deposit collapses when its pattern is removed (9). 2. The formative principle for commodities arriving at the trading floor; a student theorizes half the pattern must come from the ambient and half from another world via displacement (41–42). 3. The specific brainwave patterns (delta) emitted by Pilger Tisman during his death (8).
Person
Defined circularly by Pilgrim Dusmano as one of the "persons of these wide-eyed groups" who believe in alternate worlds (14). Also used as a fundamental unit subject to limitation (the "prime count") in some beliefs (14). The nature of a person is questioned regarding the Tisman/Dusmano complex (146).
Person-Tone
The unique sonic signature of an individual, equivalent to call-tone (4, 6). Pilger Tisman's is powerful and complex (6). Its reappearance outside the body signifies successful world-jumping (7, 9).
Personal Baggage
Minimal items (memory, identity, consciousness) carried forward from death by some individuals, historically leading to harmless ghost appearances (3).
Personal Spectrum
The unique range of colors translated from an individual's aura; Pilger Tisman's is considered unprecedentedly complex and unique (7).
Plasticene-Gray Clay
Material, born of swamps and fired in Hell, used to make expensive, passionate, and powerful mood-piece crockery observed by Pilgrim in Sheol Shuckins or the Dismal Den (60).
Poltergeists
Referenced metaphorically by Noah Zontik to describe the slow movement of objects on Prime World (23).
Pseudos / Pseudoscientists
Groups who, along with "fringies and nonsuches," correctly believed alternate worlds occupy the same local space (14).
Purpose
The quality attacked by the Media Lords (107). Noah Zontik claims the Media Lords serve no purpose (107). Polder argues the whole purpose of power is to be abused (186). The cerebral juglans' purpose had only lately been discovered (5).
Python
One of the forms assumed by the demented Pym child entity in the Narrow Corner as it destroys the ariel (128). Also listed as an archetype residing in Domdaniel, alongside Corn-Mother, FenrisWolf, and Hermaphrodite (154).
Reals
A term used by Hector Bogus to denote actually existing entities or phenomena, contrasting them with the artificial or eidetic (192).
Remembering Acorn
See Juglans, Cerebral (5).
Residue
A "new and compensating thing," often "fast-spreading," left behind by departing individuals (especially cult figures) who take something with them in death (3). Wilcove Funk (Doctor) potentially steals and suppresses the residue left by Pilger Tisman (10).
Resurrection Thirst
The characteristic, intolerable thirst experienced upon being raised from the dead, exemplified by Lazarus (141) but, according to Hector Bogus, not suffered by reanimated eidetic contrivances (192).
Rutting Season
Occurs in a specific alternate environs recalled by Pilgrim Dusmano, during which young male adults become horned and hoofed for a six-week interlude of intense activity ("Oh, that season!") (17). Pilgrim also promulgates "dynamic rutting as a fine art," contributing to his status as a Lord Spiritual (73).
SATTERFIELD
The public identity associated with Mut, one of Evenhand's henchmen (74). Known for personas like "Strength-inSerenity" and "Strength-in-Purity" (74).
SCRIVENER (DEVIL)
A category of "testifying devil" whose works constitute the collective unconscious or mass media (143). Initially identified by letters ('a,' 'b,' 'c'), later requiring the Tarshish Syllabary and elemental symbols for classification (143). Nine new scrivener or media devils were discovered concurrently with nine new physical elements (143).
SEVEN SISTERS OF THE PLEIADES
Merope, one of the High Seven Dice Throwers, is identified as one of this group (197).
SHEOL SHUCKINS
A location (perhaps a museum or shop) where one could observe expensive crockery made from swamp-born clay fired in hell (60).
SHININGS
Visible emanations noted in Pilger Tisman's complex aura, some "cut loose from any color at all" (7).
SIGNATURE
Doctor Jude Ravel's term for Pilger Tisman's unique call-tone or person-tone (6).
SKY-SIGNS AND PRODIGIES
The services advertised on the note attached to the pointing finger of the Hand From Heaven, offered by "Multi-Media Productions" (170).
SOUL(S)
Its existence is questioned or debated. Pilger Tisman is said to have had his "soul" escape capture when his memory center was emptied (9, cf. 101). Belief systems differ on soul count: billions per world, or a fixed prime count (approx. 3.5 billion) with others being reflections or "shadow souls" (14). Hector Bogus studies a "soul in hell" via his tortured animation (182). Pilgrim claims that the knacker's soul is trapped forever inside the golden knacker-statue (101). Ravenous, toothclattering spirits in the Narrow Corner eat souls (125). The Pym child seeks the "life and soul" of the climbing polymorph (124). Noah Zontik intends to save the "lives and souls" of both Pilgrim and Evenhand (86).
SOUND-FOSSILS
Doctor Ravel's term for the recorded traces left in the brain, comparing their erasure after a successful world-jump to finding an old record or tape wiped clean (10).
SOUTHGATE COMPLEX
Location of the "hell" museum/experience where one can encounter "hot and dizzy and nauseous stuff" (59).
SPIRIT(S)
An aspect of being. Judas Raffels professes disbelief in any spirit, focusing instead on Pilgrim's medical body (106). The ariel is said to have had her flight, balance, and spirit destroyed by the Pym child entity (129). Invisible, tooth-clattering spirits with frosty breath inhabit the chasms of the Narrow Corner, ravening to eat souls (125). The "spirit moves" is invoked by Lorica regarding creative opportunity (148). Polder Dossman feels the bottom fall out of his spirits after the mountain-moving (206).
STEALING HOLES (OR TUNNELS)
Doctor Funk's metaphor for taking away the fundamental patterns of memory from the cerebral juglans; considered impossible, yet "often done nowadays" (6).
STICKS (BUNDLE OF)
Pilgrim Dusmano's metaphor for his composite self, comprising a million parallel persons (sticks) bundled together, none individually significant (77).
SUBSCRIPT, CLOUDY
The text accompanying the invisible Hand from Heaven ('Protect this least of mine.'), specifically intended for the protector Og Scath (168).
Tarshish Syllabary
An extensive script system employed for classifying the numerous "testifying devils" whose works constitute the collective unconscious, used when the conventional alphabet proved inadequate (143).
Testaments (of Devils)
The personal creative outputs (literary or eidetic) of a group of "devils" which collectively form the substance of the mass media or group unconscious (143). Most are without excellence, but a few hundred achieve "group-unconscious publication" (143).
Testaments (Personal)
An individual's unique expression or essence. Palgrave Tacoman realizes his "cranky testament," associated with a new unstable element and the boar motif, has become part of the collective unconscious (154). Albert Fineface facilitates Pelion Tuscamondo publishing his "personal flame and image" or "testament" into this same underlying ocean (142, 144).
Thrones and Powers!
Og Scath's exclamation upon witnessing the Hand from Heaven deposit the dead Polder Dossman in an ash-box (190).
Thunder
Associated with the Hand from Heaven (Polder desires the echo and memory of it) (184) and the moving of Shining Mountain (accompanied by unnatural lightning) (205). Also produced metaphorically by Polder's voice (171) and the charge of the King Boar ("royal swinish thunder") (156). The body-smith emits an "apish voice like high-pitched thunder" in the Narrow Corner (126).
Tone
See Call-Tone / Person-Tone / Man-Tone.
Tragos-Goat
The "goat" element in "tragedy," identified by the curator as the evil force behind the Consul's destruction, calling it "the devil" (68).
Transmigration (of Souls/Worlds)
The jumping from death to life in another body or world, a central belief related to the existence of multiple worlds (14). Pilgrim Dusmano refers to it as "metacosmosis" and suggests it can be studied and controlled (16).
Transworld Impetus
A quality possessed by "spook-arrivals" from other worlds, like the anticipated alternate Pilgrim, giving them an advantage (95).
Tree-Worlds
An alternative term used by "fringies and nonsuches" for the interconnected alternate worlds occupying the same local space, implying a branching structure (14).
Under-Minds
The deepest layer of consciousness shared by all beings ("glowworm or giant"), containing the collective unconscious or "Folk Ocean" (142). Pelion Tuscamondo pays a heavy toll to gain access and publish his "flame and image" permanently within these under-minds (144). Archetypal motifs, like Palgrave Tacoman's "humpback-flesh camel motif," become active in the under-minds of even inanimate objects like grass (154).
Vat
A container used for extreme processes: holding molten gold for plating the eviscerated knacker into a cult statue (91, 100), and holding corrosive sublimate into which the Hand from Heaven dips Polder Dossman to kill him (190).
Weighable Substance
The metaphorical or literal "material" (such as memory, identity, or consciousness) that certain tricky individuals manage to carry forward with them when dying (3). The capacity to take such substance is linked to cult figures (3) and successful world-jumpers like Pilger Tisman (10). Its transfer is difficult for death-monitors to prevent (3).
Worlds (Alternate, Counter-, Ghost, Nine, Prime, Shadow)
Multiple realities existing concurrently. Alternate Worlds may be scattered through space or co-exist locally (13, 14); Pilgrim Dusmano claims billions exist "right here right now" (15) allowing for controllable World-Jumping (16). Counterworlds or Ghost Worlds are "horrendous" realms erected by tricky departing souls that impinge disruptively on the real world (4). Shadow Worlds are indistinct realms associated with dying world-jumpers (11). Prime World is a feared, hypothetical foundational reality characterized by absolute logic, inescapable materiality, and links to Hell (20–22, 206, 208). The Nine Worlds to La Spezia constitute a special afterlife Legacy for the rich, existing outside time and offering extreme pleasure (133, 134, 140, 146, 157). These various conceptualizations often overlap or are debated within the narrative.

Objects & Rituals (113 entries)

"Narrow Valley"
The cited source of an epigraph offering a pragmatic, alternative explanation for the camel passing through the needle's eye (121).
Adonis
An archetypal figure (154). Palgrave Tacoman makes a "very good Adonis" in his ritual death (157). Albrecht Fairbrow is judged not to make a very good one (155). Polder Dossman is told his secondary totem person is Adonis (169).
Animals (Wise-in-Death)
Creatures, unlike the "frustrated-in-death" Pilger Tisman, possessing a clear death-accepting ritual; Dr. Jude Ravel relates his father's belief that such an animal, even if released from fatal circumstances after acceptance, would proceed to die anyway (2). Knackers are respected by animals (93, 99).
Animation(s)
Lifelike figures or processes. Hector Bogus creates small, animated figures ("effigies or dolls") capable of experiencing pain eternally, which he keeps in a cigar box or tortures in a cabinet (181–183). These are differentiated from "real life," though Bogus questions the distinction (183). Bogus also implies Polder might be such an animation (182). The term also refers to the elaborate, liveaction dramas performed at the Cannes Perpetual Animation Festival (134, 135, 137, 140, 141). The Marshal of Animations oversees the use of actors or automatons (134, 137).
Aphacan Boar
A type of wild boar. Palgrave Tacoman makes a very good one in his ritual death (157). Albrecht Fairbrow's killer, the scurrying boar, is deemed not a very good one (155). The King Boar encountered by Palgrave Tacoman is the boar "of all Aphaca" (156).
Assailant, Intense
The unnamed, powerful man (later identified as Mut) who attacks Pilgrim Dusmano on the commodity arrival floor (45). He handles Pilgrim easily (45), performs a ritual killing by opening a throat vessel with a knife and collecting blood in a five-pint tankard (46), yet seems strangely distracted, allowing Pilgrim to steal his wallet (47). His public identity is remembered by Pilgrim as "Mr. Holiness-through-Strength" (48).
Ballyhoo Boar!
An insult shouted at Polder Dossman by local children, conflating him with his secondary totem animal (169).
Blood-Drinking
Mut, one of Cyrus Evenhand's henchmen, consumes five pints of Pilgrim Dusmano's blood from a tankard during a ritual killing, stating "I do sometimes" drink blood (51).
Body Beautiful Object
Polder Dossman's self-assessment, considering himself superior in this regard to the "knobby" and "bulky" Mut, whom he plans to turn into a cult statue (91).
Body-Smith
An entity identified with the Holy Knacker and the flesh-smith, encountered by the pan-morph Pilgrim in the Narrow Corner; it attempts to trap the pan-morph in a single, final form named "Change-No-More" (126, 127). Polder recognizes the flesh-smith man he destroys as the Holy Knacker (131).
Bosch, Hieronymus
Referenced as the painter of Thirst (147) and the inspiration for the drama "Adoration of the Boar" presented in Oraioi Polloi (157).
Bread-Casting
Pilgrim Dusmano's practice of cultivating young followers ("plastic younglings," "young grain") as an investment ("casting bread on waters") expected to yield future support and resources ("hundredfold bread") across multiple worlds and eventualities (30–31).
Bucket, Glowing
The vessel, presumably containing molten gold, used by James Morey to fill the eviscerated knacker, transforming him into a cult statue (99). It is withdrawn after completing its work (100).
Camel
An animal frequently referenced, often in metaphorical or symbolic contexts. Polder Dossman is derided as a "paper camel," "hot-air camel," and "paint-picture camel" (169). It is established as Polder's primary totem animal (169). A local lad details its status as "second-best in everything": steed, pack animal, draft animal, etc. (164). Its by-products (stomach for bagpipes, bones for buttons, thorax for whistles, buttermilk, cheese, eyeball for warding evil eye, felt, fleece, hair, lamp oil, flesh-meat, liver, marrow-soup, parchment, rawhide, cordovan, vellum, manure for fuel) are extensively compared, often favorably, to those of other creatures (164–167). Polder considers riding his favorite camel on Prime World (206). It is also Polder's "last creature contact" before his final decline (206–207). The "flesh of the camel" is mentioned as a gamy totem material contrasting with spirit-flesh (144). Passing "huge camels to the stool" while straining at gnats is cited in the "Song of the Golden Shovel" (72). The difficulty of a camel passing through a needle's eye is referenced (121), and contrasted with the "giant camel-eye" cavern entrance (124).
Camel's Eye
A name sometimes given to the Narrow Corner, associated with the fable of the camel and the needle's eye, though the actual feature is a "giant camel-eye" cavern (124). Also the location of a "smoky memory" for the unwinged ariel where she may have encountered a body-smith or knacker (160).
Camel's Revenge, The
A group identified by a leather and hair badge found embedded in the neck of the spy Trenchant (85). They are one of the groups outraged by Pilgrim's behavior and predicted to kill him (85). Their bravos later battle the militia of the Media Lords (111).
Chasm
The abyss over which world-jumpers, like Pilger Tisman, make their "grand jump" during gateway deaths (8). Also, the howling, bottomless void flanking the knife-edge precipice of the Narrow Corner (125), into which Polder falls (132).
Climax
The dramatic peak. The riddling in the Jezebel animation builds to it (137). Polder feels he cannot avoid being destroyed as climax in the boar hunt animation (151). The charge of the king boar and Palgrave represents a grand climax allowing no second presentation (156). Pilgrim proclaims himself "anticlimax" (117), and the narrative concludes that the whole affair was "anticlimax without climax" (120).
Coursing
The act of hunting, specifically the boar hunt undertaken by Palgrave Tacoman and the elites on Oraioi Polloi (150, 152, 153, 156).
Cracked-Glass Eyes
The appearance of Pilgrim Dusmano's eyes after being attacked by Mut (60). Also the type of jewel forming the eyepieces in Pilgrim's ritual mask (69). The pan-morphous figure in the Narrow Corner has these or jeweled eyes (122).
Cream (of the Cream)
Part of the answer given by the third Jehu Companion in the Jezebel drama, referring to the "illumined flesh and the ghosts supreme" (136).
Death Drama
The event of dying, from which those who carry forward minimal personal baggage might historically produce harmless ghosts (3).
Demon(s), Gold-Symbol
A classification including Aurelion, the 79th recording spirit, who facilitates entry into the "underlay" cartel (148).
Doctors Medical
A title or professional category. Judas Raffels and John Augustine hold this title (103). They question their presence in the cult (106), discuss Pilgrim's medical body and mask-like face (106), and consider collecting stipends for pronouncing people dead (117).
Don Quixote in His Library
The title of a Doré illustration used as the basis for a drama on Cannes World, noted to be a misnomer for God in the throes of Creation (140).
Doors (Between Worlds)
Metaphorical openings between different situations or worlds, opened in peculiar, non-obvious ways (like the messenger ritual) that cannot be widely known or easily remembered (55). Apprehension is described as a key that fits many such doors (38). Iron doors are mentioned metaphorically as being slammed shut by the Body-Smith's vaunts (127).
Doré Day
A day at the Cannes Perpetual Animation Festival dedicated to dramas based on illustrations by Gustave Doré (134, 138). On this day, the Marshal of Animations failed to provide a live actress for the role of Jezebel, leading to scandal (138).
Dray
A large, sturdy vehicle used by Mary Morey and James Morey, empowered by the knacker's numinosity, to transport the vast quantity of Mut Cult gold (92, 94, 95).
Durandarte, Mourners of
The subject of a Doré illustration, forming the basis of a drama on Cannes World (140).
Elites
The privileged class inhabiting certain worlds or participating in specific events. They pass lifetimes on Cannes World enjoying the Perpetual Animation Festival (135, 137). On Oraioi Polloi, they engage in the ritual boar hunt (150–153), have spokesmen (Albert Fineface, Whitebread, Leslie) (141, 155), and maintain a close association with parrot flocks (151). Pilgrim Dusmano refers to the "intense elite" who understand how to wield power (187), while Hector Bogus dismisses the "brittle elites" (187).
Faith Sufficient
A prerequisite state or quality attributed to Pelion Tuscamondo, along with station and connections, allowing him to successfully request mountains for his animation backdrop (141).
Five-Pint Tankard
An "old period piece" container with a flip lid, used by the assailant Mut to collect Pilgrim Dusmano's blood during a ritualistic attack (46). Mut later drinks the collected blood (51).
Flesh-Smith
The entity encountered in the Narrow Corner, also identified as the Holy Knacker and body-smith (126). Described as having an ape-shape and rank flesh (131), it battles the clarified Polder (128), smells of molten gold fluxed with lime (131), and attempts to fix Polder into a final form before being killed and thrown into the abyss (126, 131).
Glob (of Flesh-Meat)
A great roasted portion served to Pilgrim Dusmano at the Media Club, identified as the flesh of the henchman Blut (87). It is served without condiment, bread, or wine, being "its own everything" (87).
Gnu, Bushman
The source of gelatin considered "nonpareil," slightly superior to the camel-derived equivalent (165).
Goad, Camel
An attribute held in the left hand by Polder Dossman when he performs the mountain-moving miracle (205).
Goat-Kid
A small, recently dead goat whose body Mary Morey brings into the All-Effects Hall (99). She places it before the dying knacker's face just as James pours molten gold into his cavity (99). The kid's body seemingly understands the knacker's final compassionate expression and is given "care and disposal" by Mary (100).
Golden Shovel Pip
A rare mantle brooch worn by Lord Fairfronter, signifying his membership in Pilgrim Dusmano's cult and his work establishing the Pilgrim image (75).
Golden Shovel, Song of the
The source of the epigraph for Chapter 6 (72). Noah Zontik wears the pin of the Golden Shovel (84).
Golden Straw
A drinking implement disdained by Judas Raffels (Doctor) when he seizes the grace cup during the cult meeting (113).
Gothic Mountains
Part of the mountainous backdrop ordered by Pelion Tuscamondo for the Resurrection of Lazarus animation, characterized by steepness, menace, and spires twinkling blue (141).
Grace Cup
A ritual vessel containing quince wine, part of the cult meeting ceremony (112). Judas Raffels (Doctor) seizes it and drinks directly, disdaining the golden straw (113).
Greek Katastrophy
Pilgrim Dusmano's term for the ritual destruction of the Consul, which he describes as more vital and dramatic than Roman arena games or Greek tragedy (69–70). He details its classic form involving the prolonged torture and dismemberment of a virgin victim by the entire community (70–71).
Green Camel Milk
One of the beverages (along with water and whey) brought to Polder Dossman after his reanimation, which he drinks nervously (192). Also offered as a drink by someone during Polder's arrival on the stark world (159).
Grotesque Act
Pilgrim Dusmano's remembered assessment of the ritual method used to dispatch messengers (40). He later refers to the method used on the Pyms as grotesque (53).
Guardian (over Property / Prophetic)
Role assumed over derelict property (89). Also, the role the Moreys are documented as by the knacker, posing as "prophesied guardians" returning from the grave to claim the Mut Cult gold (93).
Humpbacked Flesh
A term associated with several concepts: the "order of the humpbacked flesh," linked to the 'Camel's Revenge' group (85); the "old humpback-flesh camel motif" incorporated into Palgrave Tacoman's archetypal testament (154); and a cryptic reference by Hector Bogus to a troublesome "plastic, less-than-human substratum" (195).
Iris Umbrella
The personal insignia of Noah Zontik, which Pilgrim Dusmano quickly affixes to his own mantle as a sign of being under Zontik's protection when Noah approaches (84).
JEHU'S COMPANIONS FINDING THE REMAINS OF JEZEBEL
A drama based on Doré illustrations, performed repeatedly at the Cannes Perpetual Animation Festival (135). It involves four companions interacting with four pieces of Jezebel's mutilated body (hand, foot, head, other hand), which ask riddles (135–137). The climax involves a revelation that one hand is the true head and the previous answers were wrong (137). The use of an automaton for Jezebel in one performance causes a major scandal (134, 137).
JEZEBEL
The central figure in the drama Jehu's Companions Finding the Remains of Jezebel (135). Her dismembered body parts (hand, foot, head, hand/true head) ask riddles after being injected with vita-flow (135–137). The role requires a live actress, and the substitution of an automaton (134), later replaced by the Marshal of Animations' unwilling daughter (138), causes significant disruption.
JUMP-NO-MORE
Name mockingly given to the clarified man (Polder) by the flesh-smith/Holy Knacker in the Narrow Corner, signifying the entity's intention to end Polder's ability to change or escape (130).
Katastrophy, Greek
Defined by Pilgrim Dusmano not as a tragedy but as a ritual "assault, the sack, the rape, the ruin, the destruction" (70). He describes its classic form involving the extended torture and eventual dismemberment of a virgin victim by the entire community, considering it more vital and dramatic than Roman games (70–71). He equates the killing assaults on unmasked Consuls to this practice, calling them "national solidarity acts" and "ritual murders to renew our blood" (71).
Killing, Ritual
A recurring motif performed with specific methods and significance. Mut performs one on Pilgrim Dusmano, using a ritual knife to bleed him into a five-pint tankard (46), which Pilgrim recognizes as a "ritual killing" that affords him time to prepare for a world-jump (45). Pilgrim later uses a ritual stone knife to dispatch the Pym family as messengers to Supply (53–55). The killing of an unmasked Consul is described by Pilgrim as a necessary "ritual murder" for national renewal (71). Polder Dossman views the consumption of Blut's flesh as a "rich red ritual roast meat" (87).
King Boar
A champion boar, heralded by trumpeting sounds from the cedared mountains, that arrives to challenge Palgrave Tacoman after the lesser "scurrying boar" is killed (153, 156). It stands tall and emanates a red-brown fire against the blue foothills (156). Its tusks flash like white and gold fire in salute before charging down the coursing alley to meet Palgrave in a climactic clash (156). It kills Palgrave, kneeling beside the body in a pose resembling adoration (157).
Knife, Ritual
A slender, sharp blade wielded by the assailant Mut during his attack on Pilgrim Dusmano; used to open a vessel in Pilgrim's throat for the purpose of collecting his blood in a tankard (46).
Knife, Ritual Stone
A very large stone knife provided, seemingly by workmen, along with stone couches, for the ritual dispatch of the Pym family (53). Pilgrim uses it to cut the throats of Aubrey Pym (53), his wife (54), the elder child (54), and, with difficulty due to the child's struggling, the younger child (55). The knife is removed by workmen after the ritual (56).
Knife, Rubber
The derogatory nickname used by the genuine younger Lords Spiritual for Trenchant, the false Lord and spy, implying his ineffectiveness or lack of substance (79, 85).
Lifting Fingers
Components of a large hoist in the All-Effects Hall, used by James Morey to gently lift the knacker's gold-filled body (100).
Lime Flux
A substance used in melting gold; the distinctively foul odor associated with it is inexplicably present on the flesh-smith/Holy Knacker encountered by Polder in the Narrow Corner (131).
Mask
Worn literally by Cyrus Evenhand when operating publicly (26, 49) and required for the office of Consul to ensure anonymity (69). The Consul's mask includes an eyepiece (69) and necessitates a "glottle" to disguise speech (69). Unmasking a Consul leads to certain destruction (70, 80). The term is used metaphorically by Judas Raffels, suggesting Pilgrim is a ruler masked by his followers (105) and that John Augustine (Doctor) has his own figurative mask (106). Pilgrim Dusmano eventually adopts a ritual mask instead of a face (69).
Micromurder
Pilgrim Dusmano's term for the ritual drowning of the wooden statuette containing his former eyes, an act he views with "almost leprous interest" as a symbolic precursor or "sauce" for the grander destruction of the Consul (67). He prays never to weary of such pleasures (64).
Militia (of Media Lords)
The armed force serving the Media Lords. They battle the bravos of the Camel's Revenge (111). They enforce "Freedom of Entry" and "Freedom to Arrest" using a "flesh-and-blood warrant" (114). Led by a clear-voiced young commander (114), they pursue Pilgrim Dusmano based on Judas Raffels' betrayal (114), apprehend him (115), and execute him by trampling and dismemberment with horses (118). A sergeant from the militia interacts with Mary Morey and Noah Zontik regarding their desire to follow Pilgrim in death (119).
Mountains
Pelion Tuscamondo orders various types (Gothic, Doré, menacing, Anti-Lebanon, Hermon, Hauran) as backdrops for his Resurrection of Lazarus animation (141). Polder Dossman claims the power to move mountains if public opinion is first manipulated (187). See Mountain-Moving and Shining Mountain.
Mourners of Durandarte
The subject of a Doré illustration used as the basis for a drama presented on Cannes World (140).
Musk Ox
Its hair is noted for unequaled fineness, though camel hair was used first for brushes; its hide is also mentioned (165).
Mustard (Gas)
An "old ritual gas," also known as Yperite, used in executions designed to cause discomfort (2). Pilger Tisman is executed using this gas (2).
Mutilated
Jezebel's body is presented as such in the Cannes drama (135). The good man Longram is mutilated "in a dozen painful ways" by mobs before serving as Polder's proxy (211). Mary Morey mutilates the knacker's body while eviscerating it (97).
National Solidarity Acts
Pilgrim Dusmano's term for the ritual killing assaults on unmasked Consuls, viewing them as acts that renew the collective blood (71).
Neat's-Foot Oil
Compared unfavorably to the "old second-place camel oil" by the local lad in Camel Town (166).
Paint-Picture Camel!
An insult shouted by local children at Polder Dossman, mocking his perceived artificiality (169).
Panther in the Desert, The
The title of a drama based on a Doré illustration, performed on Cannes World (140).
Paper Camel!
An insult shouted by local children at Polder Dossman, implying he is artificial or lacks substance (169).
Parchment
Fine split lambskin is considered paramount, but camel parchment has been used by holy prophets (166).
Parting Cup
A ritual vessel, filled with quince wine, used in the Dusmano cult meeting ceremony (112). Judas Raffels (Doctor) drinks from it directly, bypassing the ritual serving (113).
Pasteboard Pig!
An insult shouted by local children at Polder Dossman, identifying him with his secondary totem animal, the boar (169).
Perilous Pass, The
Subject of a Doré illustration, elements of which are said to have influenced the depiction of the Narrow Corner (140). Basis for a drama performed on Cannes World (140).
Perpetual Animation Festival
See Cannes Perpetual Animation Festival.
Plugs By Suggs
The stamp appearing on the bogus-gold plug Polder Dossman uses to fill a cured tooth, indicating the item came from a local dental supply house (200).
Pluralized
The state of having realized and enriched one's concentric aspects and personalities; the inhabitants of Camel Town's world have not pluralized themselves (163).
Regressed Flesh
A type of primordial or devolved flesh, possibly synonymous with "camel flesh" or "humpbacked clay," identified by Vonk (Doctor) as one of the components mixed with human flesh and eidolon fiber in Polder Dossman's body (212).
Rennet
Camel rennet is noted by the Camel Town lad as being highly regarded by housewives, second only to cow-calf's stomach rennet (166).
Ritual
Formalized acts structure death, transit, cult membership, and public spectacle. Examples include death-weighing, the Pyms' dispatch, the destruction of the Consul, the golden knacker, cult bread and wine, and the Adonis-like boar hunt. These acts combine symbolic authority with actual suffering (1–2, 46, 53–55, 67–71, 97–101, 112–113, 152–157, 210–215).
Ritual Hounds
Pilgrim Dusmano's term for the collective forces of a nation aroused to hunt down and destroy an unmasked Consul (67).
Ritual Killing
A recurring motif performed with specific methods and significance. Mut performs one on Pilgrim Dusmano, using a ritual knife to bleed him into a five-pint tankard (46), which Pilgrim recognizes as a "ritual killing" that affords him time to prepare for a world-jump (45). Pilgrim later uses a ritual stone knife to dispatch the Pym family as messengers to Supply (53–55). The killing of an unmasked Consul is described by Pilgrim as a necessary "ritual murder" for national renewal (71). Pilgrim Dusmano views the consumption of Blut's flesh as a "rich red ritual roast meat" (87).
Ritual Mask
Elaborate masks worn by Consuls to ensure anonymity while performing their duties (69). Mary Morey notes that Pilgrim Dusmano now wears a ritual mask (with cracked-glass jewel eyepieces) instead of a face (69).
Ritual Stone Knife
A very large stone knife provided, seemingly by workmen, along with stone couches, for the ritual dispatch of the Pym family (53). Pilgrim uses it to cut the throats of Aubrey Pym (53), his wife (54), the elder child (54), and, with difficulty due to the child's struggling, the younger child (55). The knife is removed by workmen after the ritual (56).
Rock-Shrew Joke (Malodorous)
Pilgrim Dusmano's dismissive term for Noah Zontik's analogy comparing Pilgrim to swamp gas, contrasting it unfavorably with an "upside-down eagle joke" (24).
Rubber Knife
The derogatory nickname used by the genuine younger Lords Spiritual for Trenchant, the false Lord and spy, implying his ineffectiveness or lack of substance (79, 85).
SCULPTOR-STATUE
An analogy used by Hector Bogus: an old sculptor carves a statue of a sculptor, putting too much of himself into it; this statue then carves a more sophisticated one, and so on for nine iterations, ending in "rapture-flesh" eidolons who turn on the original sculptor (196).
SECOND-BEST
The defining characteristic of Camel Town and of the camel, according to the local lad Oak Scath; they are reportedly second-best in every possible category but best in none (164).
SHIELD
A protective influence or entity. Noah Zontik is designated by God as Pilgrim Dusmano's friend and shield (27) and later refers to his protective sigil, the Iris Umbrella (84). Oak Scath identifies himself as Polder Dossman's shield (168, 203), linking this role to holding the umbrella over the Ark (172). Hecklers possess shields that deflect Polder's lightning (201) and protect against electrical and meteorological attacks (202).
SHINING MOUNTAIN
The specific mountain looming above Camel Town, which the hecklers challenge Polder Dossman to move (205). Polder successfully moves it in a cataclysmic event, after which it stands briefly over the gathering, kills the hecklers with falling boulders, and moves off to the south and east (205).
SHOWY DEATH
The kind of death expected from a cult figure, which Pilger Tisman planned but failed to deliver due to the shock and pain of his execution (2).
STATUE
Pilgrim Dusmano states his intention to make himself look like a statue, but not a statuette (63). Refers also to the HOLY KNACKER statue (100, 101) and the sequence of SCULPTORSTATUES (196).
STONE COUCHES
Four long benches brought by workmen for the Pym family to lie on during the ritual dispatch to Supply (52, 53). Removed after the ritual (56).
STONE KNIFE, RITUAL
See KNIFE, RITUAL STONE.
SUBLIMATE, CORROSIVE
A substance kept in a vat by a processor in an industrial yard; Hector Bogus dips the suffering animation (183) and later Polder Dossman (190) into it to kill them.
SUGGS
Proprietor of a local dental supply and plug house, whose name is stamped on the bogus-gold plug used by Polder Dossman (200).
SWAMP GAS
Noah Zontik's dismissive analogy for Pilgrim Dusmano, suggesting that he is ionized, luminescent gas, a projection of the "most dismal swamp" and not a substantial being (23).
Tankard (Five-Pint)
An old, flip-lidded vessel used by the assailant Mut to collect Pilgrim Dusmano's blood during the ritual attack (46). Mut later drinks the five pints of blood from it in one draft (51).
Thirst
A significant motif, especially in the afterlife or states adjacent to it. Lazarus experiences authentic thirst upon resurrection (140, 141), an element central to the drama (140, 142). Polder Dossman suffers terrible "resurrection thirst" after being reanimated (192), contrasting with Hector Bogus's assertion that eidetic contrivances do not (192). Polder also experiences horrible thirst upon awakening on the ragged hillside after his jump (159).
Token
Something potentially left behind by a successful world-jumper like Pilger Tisman, possibly hidden (11). Also refers to the leather and hair badge of "the Camel's Revenge" found embedded in the spy Trenchant's neck (85).
Token Lust / Token Murder
Pilgrim Dusmano's terms for the ritual drowning of the wooden statuette, viewing it as a symbolic act or "sauce" for the larger destruction of the Consul (67, 71).
Tongs
Used by Mary Morey to ritually place particled walnut bread on the tongues of cult members (112).
Tower (Crashing)
The simile used to describe the fall of the combined construct of impaled boar, horse, and rider (Lorica) during the hunt on Oraioi Polloi (153).
Trade
Lorica is described as being "in trade," specifically selling worlds and systems (147, 148). Hunting boar is considered a fine pleasure, unless one lives by it "as a trade" (152).
Trap
Pilgrim Dusmano plans to lure the "Camel's Revenge" group into a trap where they will kill him, fulfilling his desire to be "done to death by mad Camels" (85).
Umbrella
A recurring symbol of protection. Noah Zontik is known as "the Umbrella" for his protective services (28, 103). Og Scath holds a huge umbrella over the Ark on his coat of arms, representing his fated duty to shield Polder Dossman (168, 172, 177, 207). This protective umbrella is later described by Og as having a hole large enough for a mountain to pass through after Polder accepts the mountain-moving challenge (204). Noah Zontik states Polder will need his umbrella shielding him wherever he goes after death (119). Lorica is repeatedly, and dismissively, referred to as an "umbrella peddler" or "umbrella salesman" (147, 148, 149, 153, 204).
Umbrella Man
A nickname for Noah Zontik, reflecting his protective role (103).
Virgin
The required state (male or female) of the victim in the classic form of a Greek Katastrophy, necessary for the "pleasure" of the ritual destruction to be sufficiently "rich" (70–71).
Vita-Flow
A substance injected into the dismembered pieces of Jezebel's body in the Cannes World drama to keep them "alive enough to talk" for the purpose of asking riddles (137).
Yogurt
Mentioned in a comparison of camel products; yogurt from the khudi-cow is considered best in strength and authority, with camel-milk yogurt being second-best (167).
Yperite
An "old ritual gas," also known as Mustard gas, used in executions designed to inflict death "with discomfort" (2). Pilger Tisman is executed using this method (2).

The Eight Henchmen (9 entries)

Blut
The code name for one of Cyrus Evenhand's eight henchmen, signifying blood or family (48, 89). He is killed and torn to pieces by the populace early in the campaign against the Consul's associates (73, 74). Later, Polder Dossman consumes his roasted flesh ("It's Blut.") at the Media Club (87).
Brut
The code name for one of Cyrus Evenhand's eight henchmen, signifying the brood or spawn (48, 89). His fortune becomes part of the assets targeted by Pilgrim's knacker (89).
Flut
The code name for one of Cyrus Evenhand's henchmen, signifying flood or overflowing (48). He is one of the three initially targeted by the Media Lords (73). His fortune is designated for collection by the knacker (89).
Glut
The code name for one of Cyrus Evenhand's eight henchmen, signifying blaze or flame (48). His fortune is designated for collection by Pilgrim's knacker (89).
Gut
The code name for one of Cyrus Evenhand's eight henchmen, signifying property (49). He is one of the three initially targeted by the Media Lords (73). His fortune is designated for collection by Pilgrim's knacker (89).
Hut
The code name for one of Cyrus Evenhand's henchmen, representing the harbor, shelter, or hat (38, 49). Pilgrim Dusmano selectively kills him first, viewing the act as an opening move ("ante") in his conflict with Evenhand's organization (38, 49). Hut's fortune is later targeted by Pilgrim's knacker (89).
Mut
The code name for one of Cyrus Evenhand's eight henchmen, signifying "courage (but not, apparently, the carefulness)" (49). He is the powerful assailant who attacks Pilgrim Dusmano, performs a ritual bleeding, collects the blood in a five-pint tankard (45–47), but Pilgrim secretly takes his wallet (47–48). He later reports to Cyrus Evenhand, offers to procure tissue samples from Pilgrim Dusmano, drinks the collected blood (50–51), and is revealed to have the public identity of Satterfield ("Strength-in-Serenity," "Strength-in-Purity," "Mr. Holiness-through-Strength") (48, 74). His immense fortune and associated cult (Mut Cult) are subsequently plundered by Pilgrim and the knacker (90, 91, 92, 96). Pilgrim Dusmano plans to have Mut killed and his body turned into a gold-plated cult statue (91).
Mut's wallet
"My blood for drachmas" (48).
Wut
Code name for one of Cyrus Evenhand's eight henchmen, signifying "rage or mania" (49). His substantial fortune (96) is targeted by Pilgrim's knacker in anticipation of his death (89, 94), though the knacker is killed before processing it (96–98). He appears in the Narrow Corner afterlife as an "intelligent, calculating, canny, relentless, unforgetting, unforgiving man" possessed by "rage and mania" (125). He battles the hound (James Morey) fiercely, eventually falling into the abyss after the hound tears out his throat (128–129). His rage terrifies the horses used by the militia, resulting in his being killed by simple garrote instead (120).

Sources & Epigraphs (2 entries)

Arithmetic Book
Cited by Mary Morey as the source for the principle that rational odds don't prevail in random anachronicities (19).
Woolly Camel Book of Nursery Rhymes
The cited source of the epigraph for Chapter 12 ("I'll tell you a story about Mary Morey. . .") (158).

All Terms (899 entries)

del Mar, Maria
A young, taut-faced follower who mourns Pilger Tisman at his burial; her brother Jacob also mourns from a distance. They anticipate Mary and James Morey in the later narrative (12).
"Narrow Valley"
The cited source of an epigraph offering a pragmatic, alternative explanation for the camel passing through the needle's eye (121).
Abominations
Pleasurable acts or consumables enjoyed by Pilgrim Dusmano (87) and Polder Dossman (207). Also used by Hector Bogus to describe actions attributed to Polder by rumor which, if performed, would lead to Polder's destruction (185).
Abridgments
Concentrated essences of memory stored within the cerebral juglans or "remembering acorn" (5). Pilger Tisman's memory center, filled with these, is still intact immediately after death but collapses shortly thereafter as its content is stolen (9).
Absolute Logic
The defining characteristic of Prime World, described by Pilgrim Dusmano as the "absolute logic of total delirium," the most fearful thing to be found anywhere (21).
Accounts, Ultimate
Records kept meticulously on Prime World, associated with logic, compensation, and a narrow, one-dimensional sequence; Pilgrim Dusmano expresses fear of having to "pay" them (20).
Acorn, Remembering
See Juglans, Cerebral (5).
Adept
One skilled, particularly in the act of dying and worldjumping, like Pilger Tisman (11). Tisman is buried, possibly under the designation "Adept at dying" (12). Lorica is also described as an adept (147).
Adonis
An archetypal figure (154). Palgrave Tacoman makes a "very good Adonis" in his ritual death (157). Albrecht Fairbrow is judged not to make a very good one (155). Polder Dossman is told his secondary totem person is Adonis (169).
After-Appearances
Ghostly manifestations, often harmless in earlier times, resulting from individuals carrying minimal personal baggage (memory, identity, consciousness) forward from death (3). Contrasted with the more disruptive "horrendous ghost worlds" erected by later, trickier departing cult figures (4).
Afterglow / After-Sound
Lingering traces of a person after death, specifically the person-tone, which the brigadier of police does not want to perceive after Pilger Tisman's execution (6, 7).
Agent(s) to Supply
Messengers sent, typically one per week, to the mysterious entity or location known as Supply (37). Pilgrim Dusmano finds it difficult to send more than one weekly (37). Families, particularly those of typical size and shape for Supply's location, are preferred, as the family members act as "strings" or "built-in hostages" (34, 36). The process is considered "squeamish" (36) and involves a "very grotesque act" often performed ritualistically with a stone knife and requiring a specific "frame of mind" (39, 40, 53). The sending involves hazards like potential memory failure due to routine (52) and a necessary haziness surrounding the method (40, 52). Aubrey Pym and his family are dispatched as agents (38, 53–55). Spurgeon was once such an "outre messenger" (36).
Agglutinative
A potential quality of proto-protein sourced from Supply, possibly too much or too little so (36).
Agitators, Instant
Wild, ravening, dialectical experts who serve Pilgrim Dusmano's purposes by pouring words, instigations, and enlivening action into the people, becoming their "churning blood," "deviled brains," and "spastic spleens" (68).
Air, Incandescent Blue
The medium through which Pilgrim Dusmano ascends in slanting, soaring flight after leaving the Personage Club (24).
Airquake
One of the phenomena accompanying the miraculous moving of Shining Mountain by Polder Dossman (205).
Alessandro
Creator of three Chicago-period wood-texture paintings viewed by Pilgrim Dusmano at the Daylight Museum (66).
Alexander
An archetypal figure mentioned alongside Simon Magus, Baubo, Demeter, Adonis, Broom-Witch, and Leviathan (154).
All-Effects Hall
An armored and secluded facility behind the Golden Grotto of the Pilgrim Cult, used for the "knacker business of harvesting fortunes" (90). Mary Morey and James Morey work there, overseeing furnaces for golden images and machinery (90). It has a bright light (100), ponderous doorways connecting to the Grotto (100), and a skylike height where the gilded knacker statue is hung (100). The knacker demands the Mut Cult gold be brought there (92), and the Moreys use a dray to transport it (94, 95). The final transformation and display of the knacker statue occur within or just outside it (99–101).
Alternate Worlds
Multiple, co-existing realities theorized by various groups. Scientists posited billions scattered through space (13), while "fringies and nonsuches" correctly believed they occupied the same familiar local space as "tree-worlds" or "branch-worlds" (14). Pilgrim Dusmano reconciled these views, claiming billions exist "right here right now," viewable through a "tri-mental view," with distant galaxies being mere marginalia (15). These worlds allow for "world-jumping" or "transmigration" (16), potentially controllable to repeat or select specific life experiences or ages (16–17), including unusual environs (17). Dusmano claims they are only "about as real as the world we're in now" (17). Some are considered parallel (30, 77, 78, 104). They can be broken "like eggs" by passage through them (104).
Alternate Worlds / Multiplicity of Reality
The narrative's basic metaphysical assertion, positing the co-existence of countless realities. Initial theories range from billions of worlds scattered through conventional space (13) to billions occupying the same local space ("tree-worlds," "branch-worlds") (14). Pilgrim Dusmano synthesizes these, claiming billions exist "right here right now," perceivable through a "tri-mental view," rendering distant galaxies mere marginalia (15). This multiplicity enables WorldJumping or "transmigration," potentially allowing selection of desired realities or life stages (16–17), and underpins Dusmano's philosophy where conventional morality, consequence, and even death are rendered illusory (16). These worlds possess varying degrees of reality ("about as real as the world we're in now") (17) and include specialized environs (17) and the distinct afterlife sequence of the Nine Worlds to La Spezia (133–134). Set against this multiplicity is the single, dreaded Prime World, the potential anchor of reality and feared gateway to damnation (20–21). Much of the novel's speculation turns on movement among these realities, whether by jumps or by psychic leakage (32), and on their uncertain status.
Amalgamated Camel Enterprises
The only aspect of Polder Dossman's affairs that Og Scath admits to promoting (174).
Ambient
The surrounding environment or medium from which, according to one student's theory, the vast quantities of material arriving at Pilgrim Dusmano's commodity floor might be transformed, powered by the slight displacement of two coincident worlds (41). Pilgrim questions whether the "pattern" for this transformation might also originate there, but the student insists half must come from elsewhere (41–42).
Amorality
Stated by Pilgrim Dusmano to be a "total thing" implicit in his claim regarding alternate worlds, rendering recompense, debt, guilt, punishment, and death mere illusions (16).
Amorphous Ocean
The primordial, unformed state from which the name Polder indicates reclamation into a stable form (131). See also Ocean and Group Unconscious / Folk Ocean.
Amplification
The process applied to a person's call-tone or persontone to make it audible (6). Pilger Tisman's tone hardly needs it (6), and if he successfully jumps, his resurrected tone will not require it (7, 9). The brigadier forbids tampering with the amplification during Pilger Tisman's execution (6). Hector Bogus possesses amplification capable of turning an animation's screams into a town-shocking sound (182), but cannot amplify the Polder-sliver's scream (214).
Anachronicities, Random
Realms where, according to Mary Morey citing an arithmetic book, rational odds do not prevail, and the possibility exists for a single bad outcome to outweigh billions of good ones (19).
Anchor (of Final Things)
Prime World is described as the base and anchor of the four final or eschatological things (21).
Animals (Wise-in-Death)
Creatures, unlike the "frustrated-in-death" Pilger Tisman, possessing a clear death-accepting ritual; Dr. Jude Ravel relates his father's belief that such an animal, even if released from fatal circumstances after acceptance, would proceed to die anyway (2). Knackers are respected by animals (93, 99).
Animation(s)
Lifelike figures or processes. Hector Bogus creates small, animated figures ("effigies or dolls") capable of experiencing pain eternally, which he keeps in a cigar box or tortures in a cabinet (181–183). These are differentiated from "real life," though Bogus questions the distinction (183). Bogus also implies Polder might be such an animation (182). The term also refers to the elaborate, liveaction dramas performed at the Cannes Perpetual Animation Festival (134, 135, 137, 140, 141). The Marshal of Animations oversees the use of actors or automatons (134, 137).
Animosity
The slightest edge of this quality is detected in the live monkey or kobold eyes of the wooden statuette by Groben (63).
Anomalies
Abrupt and stubborn inconsistencies characterizing Pilgrim Dusmano's import business, such as not knowing where his goods came from or if he paid for them (33).
Ante
Pilgrim Dusmano's term for his killing of Hut, considering it his opening stake in the "game" or war against Cyrus Evenhand and his associates (38).
Anticlimax
Pilgrim Dusmano declares himself this, contrasting it with the non-existent hero (117). The entire sequence of events surrounding the deaths of Pilgrim's associates and rivals is described as anticlimax without climax (120).
Antihero
Pilgrim Dusmano's self-description ("I am antihero. But there is no hero anywhere."), adopted just before his final decline (117). He looks less like one as his fear increases (118).
Antilife
A concept valued by the Putty Dwarf, analogous to how life "happened to matter once"; transcendence is now happening to life (148–149).
Antilogy
Loved by Pilgrim Dusmano, in contrast to logy or logic, which he blinds his eyes to (117).
Antimatter
Recognized by Pilgrim Dusmano, though he claims never to have seen matter (117).
Antithesis
Known by Pilgrim Dusmano, while thesis is not (117).
Ape-Man
An aspect or description of the Holy Knacker/fleshsmith/body-smith encountered in the Narrow Corner (126, 127, 131).
Aphacan Boar
A type of wild boar. Palgrave Tacoman makes a very good one in his ritual death (157). Albrecht Fairbrow's killer, the scurrying boar, is deemed not a very good one (155). The King Boar encountered by Palgrave Tacoman is the boar "of all Aphaca" (156).
Apparatus, Secret
The powerful organization headed by Cyrus Evenhand, with which Pilgrim Dusmano goes to war (27).
Apprehension
A state cultivated in underlings and particularly messengers by Pilgrim Dusmano, considered a key fitting many doors between worlds (38). The Pym family exhibits it before being sent to Dongola (38). Pilgrim advises the Pyms not to let go of their apprehension even while embracing happiness and trust (53). Required for the "jump" (39).
Archery League
Aubrey Pym's wife attends this on the morning he is selected as a messenger (34).
Archetype
A fundamental pattern or figure. Palgrave Tacoman becomes one of the "archetypical devil-angels" upon the billionfold multiplication of his testament (154). Polder Dossman claims this status (201, 203), along with being a Zodiac Lord and High Dicer (203). Og Scath affirms Polder has become one, located in the underlying ocean of minds (197), but Hector Bogus dismisses him as merely a "little green eidolon-godling" (197). Palgrave is initially reluctant to become one (147). The term is also linked to the "communicating gods of the atomic numbers" (154).
Arena
The setting for the three-tiered conflict in the Narrow Corner after death (125). Also mentioned regarding Roman games (70). The arena, village, and world are identical in Adobe Pueblos (147).
Ariel
The post-death manifestation or companion role of Mary Morey, later Moira Mara, paired with her brother James (the hound), as servitors to their cult figure (122, 149, 159, 213). She appears initially as a freckled, brilliant girl in sunlight (150), having lost her wings at the Narrow Corner (129, 160). In the Narrow Corner, she battles the child fire-drake (126) before being destroyed and falling into a pit (129). Also appears with the hound to Palgrave Tacoman (149, 157).
Arithmetic Book
Cited by Mary Morey as the source for the principle that rational odds don't prevail in random anachronicities (19).
Ark
The central image on Og Scath's coat of arms, depicted as a large, covered boat, poorly designed, unsteerable, and lacking masts or oarlocks (177). Og Scath claims to be the large man depicted sitting astride its roof ridge holding an umbrella over the open main hatch (177–178).
Arkhê
Greek term for rule or principle, invoked by Pilgrim Dusmano regarding the postanarchic age where any rule, masked or not, is considered a bad omen (80).
Arrival Floor / Area, Commodity
A vast, shimmering, enigmatic area in Pilgrim Dusmano's business headquarters where immense quantities of diverse goods (fuel, clothing, food, building materials, metals, minerals, chemicals, machinery, vehicles, tonics, talismans) appear constantly without visible means of transport (41, 42). Theories suggest the material is transformed from the ambient (41) via "One Smooth Operation" (42). The floor seems to be an electric or magnetic field force nexus, possibly with gravitational properties, though instrumentation denies these (42). It produces a shimmering effect, perhaps from "Bi-location kickback" (42). Aubrey Pym and his family wait here (38); Pilgrim is attacked here (44, 47); he cleans himself at fountains on its edge (47). Pilgrim walks along its edge (41). Doctor Judas Raffels indicates Pilgrim Dusmano is hiding near this area (114).
Article of Death
The state in which Pilger Tisman (1) and later Polder Dossman (210) lie while being attended by doctors and others for the purpose of "weighing" their death.
Artificial
A descriptor applied to various entities and concepts. Pilgrim Dusmano suggests the ancient pleasures are lost and modern organized rituals are artificial (71). He claims his parallel selves ("sticks") are artificial personalities (77).
