Polder Dossman is suspected of being artificial, potentially a "made-thing" of the Eidetic Lords (175), an "artificial contrivance," a "stuffed sausage of a puppet" (178), or an "experimental contrivance" (192). Hector Bogus asserts that life is artificial (183) and creates artificial animations (181–183). The scattered pieces of Jezebel in the Cannes animation are revealed to be artificial (137).
Aspect World
A type of alternate reality, distinct from outer worlds, suggested by Mut as the origin of Pilgrim Dusmano (50). Messages are sent to other aspects via messenger families (55). Pilgrim Dusmano speaks of parallel Dusmanos on alternate worlds or aspects (89).
Assailant, Intense
The unnamed, powerful man (later identified as Mut) who attacks Pilgrim Dusmano on the commodity arrival floor (45). He handles Pilgrim easily (45), performs a ritual killing by opening a throat vessel with a knife and collecting blood in a five-pint tankard (46), yet seems strangely distracted, allowing Pilgrim to steal his wallet (47). His public identity is remembered by Pilgrim as "Mr. Holiness-through-Strength" (48).
Assassinated
Rulers had been killed so swiftly prior to the maskedConsul system that rule itself had disappeared (69).
Associate
Term used for Noah Zontik in relation to Pilgrim Dusmano (20, 27), and for Cyrus Evenhand's henchmen (38). Also refers to Pilgrim's business associate Spurgeon (35). Doctor August, Hans examines Polder with his associates (195). Palgrave Tacoman has associate aspects pleasuring themselves across the Nine Worlds after his death (157).
Atrium Theater
Location in Oraioi Polloi where the "living theaters" of the Nine Worlds to La Spezia are presented (147). The "Adoration of the Boar" is performed there (157).
Attribute
An object held or associated with a figure, signifying identity or power. Polder Dossman holds a camel goad as an attribute before moving the mountain (205). Polder Dossman's surviving hand holds a camel's flem as an attribute after death (213).
Aura
The electrical shell surrounding a person, translatable into light and color (7). Pilger Tisman's aura is described as dazzling, containing a hundred nonchromatic colors, grays, silvers, brasses, pulsating pallidness, shinings, shimmers, writhing blackness, and areas of light that cannot be fractured (7). It is dimmed but not extinguished during his execution (4), goes out upon death (9), but then reappears dazzlingly at a distance before flicking out of the world (9).
Aurelion
A "gold-symbol demon," the seventy-ninth recording spirit, who pushes applications for membership in the "underlay" cartel controlling power and influence beneath the worlds (148). Membership requires a huge payment, insisted upon by Aurelion (149). Palgrave Tacoman orders the sum paid (149).
Austin, Jon (Doctor)
One of the three "outstanding doctors" attending Pilger Tisman's death-weighing (1). He expresses dislike for Tisman as a "hulk" (4) and questions how Tisman could be loved (4). He notes Tisman leaves behind only one powerful friend and enemy, and wonders about the cult members left behind (6). He is fascinated by the unique colors and light of Tisman's aura, calling the man "a dazzle!" (7). He asks Doctor Funk what Tisman was an adept at (11). He is later listed as one of the cult members present during the final events, referred to as "John Augustine" (103). As Dr. John Augustine, he discusses the nature of Pilgrim's death with Dr. Judas Raffels (117), collaborates in declaring Dusmano dead to collect stipends (118), and makes his way out of life by private conveyance after the others are killed (120). Also appears as "Doctor August" attending Polder Dossman's death (210, 215) and as "Doctor Hans August" analyzing Polder's body (212).
Authentic Cult Figure
What Noah Zontik wonders if Pilgrim Dusmano's "scruffy little handful of tricks and miracles" are sufficient to make him (24). Zontik later notes Pilgrim is becoming one (28).
Authentic Original
Pilgrim Dusmano's insistent self-description, contrasted with Noah Zontik's accusation that he is a "derivative" (23).
Authority
The quality most hated by the Media Lords (107). Polder Dossman questions whether the abdication of authority in the world applies to Og Scath (204).
Avidity
The curator notes the nation's intense eagerness for the destruction of a Consul (66).
Back-Brain
A distinct neurological feature noted for its unusual size in both Wilcove Funk (Doctor) (5) and the dying Pilger Tisman, whose skull seemed internally larger than its exterior dimensions could accommodate (5).
Ballad, World-Jumper's
A short verse serving as an epigraph, contemplating mortality and the precarious nature of existence on a world from which one might abruptly depart (1). Also quoted by Polder Dossman near his end (210).
Ballyhoo Boar!
An insult shouted at Polder Dossman by local children, conflating him with his secondary totem animal (169).
Basham
The place of origin claimed by Og Scath, which he states cannot be located in modern geography (177).
Baubo
An archetypal figure mentioned in a list including Simon Magus, Demeter, Adonis, Alexander, Broom-Witch, and Leviathan (154).
Bed (of Og Scath)
An unusually large iron bed, sofa, or divan, fifteen feet long and six feet wide, located in Og Scath's spacious dwelling; it appears ancient and valuable (176).
Beggar-King
An oceanic companion archetype mentioned alongside Huracan and Gyne Peribebleene-ton-Helion (155).
Beneficence
A quality personified by the "dripping hands" of Pilgrim Dusmano (115), Pelion Tuscamondo (139), and Polder Dossman (203), suggesting a bestowal of grace or favor.
Betrayed-in-Death Cult Figure
Wilcove Funk (Doctor)'s description of Pilger Tisman, characterizing him as a cult leader who failed to deliver a promised spectacular death, thus frustrating his followers (2).
Bi-Location
The condition of existing in multiple places simultaneously. Pilgrim Dusmano discusses the problem of bilocation regarding alternate worlds (16). The floor of his main business terminal is believed by some to smell of it (33). Its "kickback" is suggested as a cause for the shimmering effect at the commodity arrival area (42).
Black-Wings
Entities encountered in the afterlife, whose buffets are felt by Polder Dossman as he traverses the narrow path of the Narrow Corner (131).
Blake, Mad
William Blake, cited as one of the historical/literary figures whose projections and shaping influenced the nature of the Narrow Corner (127).
Blissful Permit
The method by which the saintly Cyrus Evenhand conducted his off-world commerce, a method Pilgrim Dusmano ascertains he cannot use, even when controlling Evenhand's assets, due to interworld rules (90).
Blood-Drinking
Mut, one of Cyrus Evenhand's henchmen, consumes five pints of Pilgrim Dusmano's blood from a tankard during a ritual killing, stating "I do sometimes" drink blood (51).
Blood-Magnet
A powerful, perhaps morbid, attraction to which the museum curator finds himself drawn while observing Pilgrim Dusmano's interaction with the Consul's eyepiece (70).
Blood-Meat Bodies
The corpses of the dead, described as objects of intense lust for Pilgrim Dusmano, surpassing even the desire of "money giants" for the associated fortunes (95).
Blues, Resurrection
A state of sickness and fatigue suffered by world-jumpers upon arrival in a new world, experienced by Polder Dossman (159).
Blut
The code name for one of Cyrus Evenhand's eight henchmen, signifying blood or family (48, 89). He is killed and torn to pieces by the populace early in the campaign against the Consul's associates (73, 74). Later, Polder Dossman consumes his roasted flesh ("It's Blut.") at the Media Club (87).
Board Meeting
Defined specifically within Pilgrim Dusmano's commerce as any occasion where he sits down "to board" with three or more of his employees (34). Spurgeon and other leaders attend these (35, 47, 51).
Body Beautiful Object
Polder Dossman's self-assessment, considering himself superior in this regard to the "knobby" and "bulky" Mut, whom he plans to turn into a cult statue (91).
Body-and-Blood Giant
An archetypal figure mentioned alongside the Leper and the Boogerman, whose company Palgrave Tacoman joins upon achieving cult status (155).
Body-Jumper
John Augustine (Doctor)'s term for Pilgrim Dusmano's earlier mode of existence before becoming a world-jumper, involving sequentially inhabiting and slaying bodies (106).
Body-Smith
An entity identified with the Holy Knacker and the flesh-smith, encountered by the pan-morph Pilgrim in the Narrow Corner; it attempts to trap the pan-morph in a single, final form named "Change-No-More" (126, 127). Polder recognizes the flesh-smith man he destroys as the Holy Knacker (131).
Bogus Lords
The meaning ascribed by Hector Bogus to his family name, implying a playful, non-serious participation in the power structures ("Lord play, the big-man play") that only becomes evil when taken seriously (188).
Bogus, Hector
An Eidolon or Media Lord described as technically proficient (180). He engages Polder Dossman in philosophical debate, reveals his power to animate and torture small effigies (181–183), asserts Polder's artificiality (183, 189), modifies the Hand from Heaven (184), and later uses it to kill Polder by dipping him in corrosive sublimate (190). He oversees Polder's final moments, fills the office of brigadier of police (211), and witnesses the analysis of Polder's body (212–214), engaging in a final, contemptuous dialogue with the dying Polder-sliver (214).
Boondocks World
Hector Bogus's dismissive term for Prime World (213) and the world where Polder's final death occurs (214).
Bosch Day, Hieronymus
The thematic designation for the day's events at the Atrium Theater in Oraioi Polloi when Palgrave Tacoman is present (147).
Bosch, Hieronymus
Referenced as the painter of Thirst (147) and the inspiration for the drama "Adoration of the Boar" presented in Oraioi Polloi (157).
Bottoming-Earth
A descriptive term for Prime World, evoking its foundational nature and connection to muck and bottomless sloughs (21).
Brackets
Pilgrim Dusmano's metaphor for the structures provided by art, onto which the "trammels" (complexities or hindrances) of life can later be hooked (59).
Branch-Worlds
An alternative term used by "fringies and nonsuches" for the interconnected alternate worlds occupying the same local space (14).
Bread-Casting
Pilgrim Dusmano's practice of cultivating young followers ("plastic younglings," "young grain") as an investment ("casting bread on waters") expected to yield future support and resources ("hundredfold bread") across multiple worlds and eventualities (30–31).
Bridge, Invisible
A high, potent structure exerting a "powerful charm," envisioned by the Pym family as their means of crossing to another world or aspect, facilitated by Pilgrim Dusmano's ritual (53).
Brigadier of Police
An official present at Pilger Tisman's death-weighing (1). He displays impatience (5), expresses personal hatred for Tisman possibly influenced by Tisman's powerful enemy (7), demands the silencing of Tisman's mocking post-mortem tone (7), and angrily denounces the proceedings as "bungled" when Tisman successfully world-jumps (10). Hector Bogus later holds this office during Polder Dossman's death (211).
Bright Young People
Pilgrim Dusmano's term for his students at Rampart University, to whom he preaches that "Everything is allowed" (18).
Broom-Witch
An archetypal figure mentioned in a list with Simon Magus, Baubo, Demeter, Adonis, and Alexander (154).
Brut
The code name for one of Cyrus Evenhand's eight henchmen, signifying the brood or spawn (48, 89). His fortune becomes part of the assets targeted by Pilgrim's knacker (89).
Bucket, Glowing
The vessel, presumably containing molten gold, used by James Morey to fill the eviscerated knacker, transforming him into a cult statue (99). It is withdrawn after completing its work (100).
Buckling, Parallel Worlds
Described as a "wide tangle" from which Pilgrim Dusmano habitually derived or found advantage (32).
Bundle of Sticks
Pilgrim Dusmano's self-metaphor, representing his existence as a composite of a "million long and skinny sticks bundled together," each stick being a parallel self, none individually constituting a large part of the whole (77).
Busts
Pilgrim Dusmano's term for his own maladroit actions or failures, which he believes are "written plainly on the air itself for everyone to read" and require revision or redacting before entering his cult's narrative (25).
Cabinet, Torture
A device used by Hector Bogus into which he places small animated effigies, applies white-hot fire, and observes their eternal suffering (182).
Call-Tone
An audible signature, a nonchromatic aspect of the body corona, unique to an individual (4, 6). Pilger Tisman's is rough, rambunctious, complex, and powerful, hardly needing amplification (6). Jude Ravel (Doctor) considers it a "signature" but not a complete résumé of the man (6). The brigadier demands to hear it extinguished simultaneously with Pilger Tisman's life (6). It is the last thing to potentially "jump" forward after death, and its reappearance outside the body, possibly seeming to mock, signifies a successful escape (7). Pilger Tisman's tone sounds again triumphantly and mockingly after his death, even taking up the tune "Heads Will Roll" (9, 10).
Camel
An animal frequently referenced, often in metaphorical or symbolic contexts. Polder Dossman is derided as a "paper camel," "hot-air camel," and "paint-picture camel" (169). It is established as Polder's primary totem animal (169). A local lad details its status as "second-best in everything": steed, pack animal, draft animal, etc. (164). Its by-products (stomach for bagpipes, bones for buttons, thorax for whistles, buttermilk, cheese, eyeball for warding evil eye, felt, fleece, hair, lamp oil, flesh-meat, liver, marrow-soup, parchment, rawhide, cordovan, vellum, manure for fuel) are extensively compared, often favorably, to those of other creatures (164–167). Polder considers riding his favorite camel on Prime World (206). It is also Polder's "last creature contact" before his final decline (206–207). The "flesh of the camel" is mentioned as a gamy totem material contrasting with spirit-flesh (144). Passing "huge camels to the stool" while straining at gnats is cited in the "Song of the Golden Shovel" (72). The difficulty of a camel passing through a needle's eye is referenced (121), and contrasted with the "giant camel-eye" cavern entrance (124).
Camel Town
A location described by a local lad as the "second-best town in the world in every way," best in nothing but second-best in everything, like the camel (163–164). Polder visits it upon arrival in a sharp-lined, simple world (163).
Camel's Eye
A name sometimes given to the Narrow Corner, associated with the fable of the camel and the needle's eye, though the actual feature is a "giant camel-eye" cavern (124). Also the location of a "smoky memory" for the unwinged ariel where she may have encountered a body-smith or knacker (160).
Camel's Revenge, The
A group identified by a leather and hair badge found embedded in the neck of the spy Trenchant (85). They are one of the groups outraged by Pilgrim's behavior and predicted to kill him (85). Their bravos later battle the militia of the Media Lords (111).
Cannes
One of the nine locations constituting the Nine Worlds to La Spezia, part of the Legacy of the rich (134, 146).
Cannes Perpetual Animation Festival
An ongoing event on Cannes World requiring the constant use of live actors for its ten thousand daily dramas (135). Elite lifetimes are measured by the cycle of these dramas (135). Features dramas based on Doré illustrations, including Jehu's Companions Finding the Remains of Jezebel (135).
Canny
A quality attributed to world-jumpers who might leap "upstream" or "downstream" rather than straight across (8), and to the string-pulling involved in Pilgrim's and the knacker's documentation schemes (95). Also a quality of the "intelligent, calculating, relentless, unforgetting, unforgiving man" (Wut) encountered in the Narrow Corner (125).
Carrying-Forward
The act by which certain tricky individuals, particularly cult figures, take something (often memory, identity, or consciousness) with them upon dying (2, 3). This substance is weighable (3, 10). The process involves individual tricks, cataloged by death-monitors (3), and often leaves a "compensating thing" or "residue" behind (3, 10). Tisman succeeds in this (10).
Catalogue of Tricks
A list, numbering over a hundred, documenting the individual methods used by dying persons to achieve "carryingforward" (3).
Catch, The
The potential negative consequence or drawback inherent in Pilgrim Dusmano's promise of endless world-jumping; Mary Morey persistently demands he name it (18). Dusmano acknowledges an "extremely improbable failure," a "narrow foul chance" linked to Prime World (18, 19, 20), but initially refuses to elaborate (19).
Centrality
A state battled for in the Narrow Corner, where the establishment of one's eyes as the controlling center dictates the reality of the field (122). The pan-morphous cult figure initially wins this advantage (122).
Cerebral Juglans
A small nodule in the brain, the "remembering acorn," containing compressed memory essences (5). It is a composite of chemical fixes and electrical charges in patterned wrinkles (5). Wilcove Funk (Doctor) monitors and "mars" Pilger Tisman's juglans during the death-weighing (5). Though initially intact after Pilger Tisman's death, its "fat content" (memory, identity, consciousness) is stolen shortly after, collapsing the structure (9).
Certified Cult Figure
A status acknowledged by the knacker as helpful and providing "blue chip" interworld standing, though he notes Pilgrim Dusmano doesn't meet the expected moral minimum (90).
Challenge
Demanded of Polder Dossman by the hecklers, involving a test of power and faith that cannot be faked (202). Polder accepts, declaring he can do anything imaginable (203). The hecklers demand "Mountain-moving!" (204).
Change-No-More
The name given by the body-smith to the final, straitened, single form he intends to impose on the pan-morphous Pilgrim in the Narrow Corner (126).
Chaos
Suggested by Rhinestone Suderman as the operative principle for the Pilgrim Dusmano cult, providing "more scope" (19).
Chaotic Man
Rhinestone Suderman's preferred description of Pilgrim Dusmano, positioning him as a figure through whom great things might be brought forth, analogous to mythological creation from chaos (19).
Chasm
The abyss over which world-jumpers, like Pilger Tisman, make their "grand jump" during gateway deaths (8). Also, the howling, bottomless void flanking the knife-edge precipice of the Narrow Corner (125), into which Polder falls (132).
Chef
The functionary at the Media Club who serves Pilgrim Dusmano the roasted flesh-meat of Blut (87).
Chicago-Period
Designation for wood-texture paintings by Alessandro displayed at the Daylight Museum (66).
Child
Frequently appears in significant or strange roles. Aubrey Pym's younger child speaks unexpectedly ("The hard way," "Showy, but not cover much") (40, 41), shows insight ("You have jeweled eyes. . . Maybe somebody will kill you") (53), has snake-like or basilisk eyes with agate fire (54), defies and threatens Pilgrim ("I'll knock you clear into hell") (54), and its hate-filled, child-sized eye is the last part seen riding the effluvium of the people-grinder (56). This same child later manifests after death as a "demented and furious child," a "fury-child," a "firedrake," a "crackling-voiced buzzard," or a "python," showing open lust for Pilgrim's soul (122, 124), attacking both Pilgrim and the ariel in the Narrow Corner (126, 128) before being recognized by the clarified Polder as Aubrey Pym's younger son (129). Children (specifically "the damnable young of the damnable local humans") also mock Polder Dossman with insightful insults (including paper camel, paint-picture camel, and pasteboard pig) (169), and one is killed by Polder (170). The killing of children by Polder is cited as a reason for the hecklers' anger (202). Small children are required participants in the torture phase of a Greek Katastrophy (70). Boy children are born with beards and moustaches in one alternate enclave (17).
Chimeras
Confusing entities present alongside persons and players in the "three-tiered arena" of the Narrow Corner (125).
Chin
Wilcove Funk (Doctor)'s is rendered "unnecessary and impossible" by his protruding muzzle (5). Vonk (Doctor) also has this feature (211).
Christ in Matthew
Cited as one of the projections that shaped the Narrow Corner (127).
Christus
Referenced ironically by Fairfronter regarding Pilgrim Dusmano sending a Paraclete (104). Polder Dossman stands "like a Christus" while proclaiming himself antihero (117). Pelion Tuscamondo raises Lazarus in the manner of a Christus (140).
Chthonic
Related to the underworld or primal earth forces. Pilgrim Dusmano describes the "genuine chthonic roots" of ancient pleasures as shriveled (71). A "chthonic demiurge" is mentioned in a saying about idle hands (46).
Chung and Ching
A major worldwide wholesaler firm possessing its own "One Smooth Operation" for receiving supplies (42).
Cigar-Store Indian
An anomalous and "woodenly vital" carving by Finnegan, displayed in the Daylight Museum's reserved room; it holds real cigars (65). It is the "only moral person there" during Pilgrim's destructive revelry (70).
Clarified Man
The state achieved by the pan-morphic cultist (Pilgrim/Polder) after beginning to emerge from his "ocean of forms" in the Narrow Corner (128, 129). This involves settling into a human form (130) but still being mentally "fuzzy and witless" with superimposed outlines affecting his perception (130). He recognizes Wut (129) and the child attacker (129) and eventually remembers his own name, Polder (131).
Climax
The dramatic peak. The riddling in the Jezebel animation builds to it (137). Polder feels he cannot avoid being destroyed as climax in the boar hunt animation (151). The charge of the king boar and Palgrave represents a grand climax allowing no second presentation (156). Pilgrim proclaims himself "anticlimax" (117), and the narrative concludes that the whole affair was "anticlimax without climax" (120).
Cloud-Capper
Og Scath uses this term, likely referring to the Hand from Heaven (190).
Clouds
Associated with freckled daylight behind Mary Morey (104). A "fearful scurry of clouds" accompanies the mountain-moving (205). Wraith-like clouds accompany the fall of Shining Mountain's roots (205). Also described as hot during Polder's arrival in the stark world (160).
Clutter-Buck
The source, distinct from a bull, of the basic ingredient for mock-pizzle pie (75).
Coat of Arms (of Og Scath)
A giant-sized coat of arms hanging in Og Scath's dwelling (176). It bears the name O'Basham (177) and its central image is the Ark with Og riding the roof ridge, holding an umbrella over the main hatch (177).
Cognomen(s)
Code names or nicknames used for associates, such as Hut for one of Cyrus Evenhand's henchmen (38, 122), or the set used for all eight (Blut, Brut, etc.) (48, 89). Given for Evenhand's men, but their real names are withheld (26).
Coincident Worlds
Two worlds whose slight displacement generates incredible force, suggested as the power source for the transformation of materials at the commodity arrival floor (41). The theory posits that half the "pattern" must come from one world, half from the other (42).
Color
A quality potentially absent or illusory in certain worlds (162). Pilger Tisman's aura contains a hundred "nonchromatic colors" (7). The paintings of van Gregory Ghi are suffused with an unworldly, ghostly orange color (66). Colors in the Daylight Museum must be "chaste" and viewable without inducing fever or high unease (59). Polder finds the sharp-lined world lacks the true quality of color, specifically red (162).
Commerce
Pilgrim Dusmano engages in a "fabulous import business" characterized by abrupt anomalies, such as forgetting where he got his goods or whether he paid for them (33). He harvests "past plantings" (33). His main terminal features a shimmering floor (33). This involves interactions with associates like Spurgeon (35) and requires sending messengers to "Supply" (35–36). He also engages in "off-the-world commerce," as does Cyrus Evenhand (89). Polder Dossman is also involved in extensive and profitable commercial affairs, seemingly handled by others or decided in minds other than his own (172). Palgrave Tacoman and Albert Fineface have followed "unusual commerces" (142).
Commodity Arrival Floor / Area
See Arrival Floor / Area, Commodity.
Compensating Thing
A new item or residue seemingly left behind by those who succeed in "carrying-forward" something from death (3). Cult figures often leave a "fast-spreading residue" (3). Pilger Tisman is presumed to have left one, which Wilcove Funk (Doctor) likely steals and suppresses (10).
Complex
Used in the sense of a psychological or existential composite. All persons sharing a "set" (like the various Dusmano/Tisman figures) are part of the same complex, which can contain vastly different persons (e.g., a saint among sinners) (146).
Compulsion, Blind
The force cited by Rhinestone Suderman as the necessary impetus for the founding of all cults (19). Howard Praise questions the source of this compulsion (19). Og Scath feels compelled to watch over Polder (162), and Moira Morey and James Morey feel compelled to do so with self-denial (162).
Condenser
A device with two opposing brass balls used by Hector Bogus to administer a galvanic shock to small effigies (181). Polder Dossman is later subjected to a giant version used by a shock-plastic manufacturing company (191).
Consciousness
Considered, along with memory and identity, as one of the weighable things that can be "carried forward" after death (3, 10). It is often taken by unconscious persons making the leap (3). Pilger Tisman takes the "container for his consciousness" with him (10). Hector Bogus devises an artificial consciousness for his tortured animations based on an "ingenious resonating circuit" (182).
Consul
A high, anonymous, masked office held sequentially by absolutely good men who head governments and make decisions from behind a veil (69). They must use a "glottle" to disguise their speech (69). If a Consul's face or Consul-name is revealed, he is marked for destruction by devils (70) and public "ritual hounds" (67). The destruction is a national "devil-revel," a pleasure hardly occurring twice a generation (66–67). Cyrus Evenhand is revealed to be the Consul (58, 66), with the code name Rut (49, 76, 89, 94). Pilgrim Dusmano claims being unmasked is an evil omen for a Consul (80) and actively works to bring about Cyrus Evenhand's destruction (50, 66). Pilgrim was once considered for the office but rejected (49). The "masked-Consul system" had previously stabilized rule after a period of assassinations (69).
Consul-Name
The secret name associated with the office of Consul; its revelation leads to the Consul's destruction (70).
Container for Consciousness
One of the weighable things, along with memory and identity, that Pilger Tisman successfully takes with him when he world-jumps (10).
Continuity of Memories
Requires attention during the act of dying to ensure successful world-jumping (17).
Contrivance
Polder Dossman realizes he is an artificial one (178) and is later described by Hector Bogus as an "experimental contrivance" (192).
Cordcutter
A young Lord Spiritual communicator at the Media Club who informs Pilgrim about the pursuit of Blut, Gut, and Flut, presents a piece of Blut, and seeks more "activating information" from Pilgrim (73–74). He is present at the final cult gathering (103).
Corner, Narrow
See Narrow Corner.
Corona Spectrum
An aspect of a person that can be measured or observed; Pilger Tisman's is dimmed but not extinguished during his execution (4).
Coroner
An official present at Pilger Tisman's death-weighing (1). He explains to the brigadier that dying is a series of reactions, not an instant event (8). He feels guilty writing "dead" for jumpers and suggests categories like "Dead, subject to continuance" or "Not so dead as all that" (11). Og Scath later fills the office of coroner for Polder Dossman's death (210).
Corporate Good
The justification or outcome Pilgrim Dusmano envisions for consolidating Cyrus Evenhand's fortunes with his own, suggesting it will nourish his parallel selves (89).
Corporate Murder-Pleasure
The intense, collective satisfaction derived from destroying a Consul, described by Pilgrim Dusmano as a ritualistic national event, especially rich if the Consul is spotless, like Cyrus Evenhand (67, 71). Pilgrim anticipates it regarding Cyrus Evenhand's death (50).
Corpse(s), Twitching
The result of Polder Dossman's response to hecklers; the heckler movement loses momentum as many practitioners are turned into these (201).
Correspondence-Integers
Parallel aspects or representations of individuals existing on corresponding orbs (30). Shaping younglings on one orb shapes these integers elsewhere according to "distance in attitude and space and time" (30).
Corresponding Orbs
Parallel worlds where correspondence-integers exist (30).
Corresponding Persons
Pilgrim Dusmano's term for his parallel selves on other worlds or orbs; he believes he is well-organized regarding them and that the different "integers" of him aid one another (30).
Counterpart (Without Prime-Part)
What Pilgrim Dusmano proclaims himself to be speaking of, along with counterworlds and counterculture, denying the existence or necessity of originals or theses (117).
Counterworlds
Horrendous ghost worlds erected by tricky departing cult figures that impinge upon the real world, causing dislocation, disturbance, erosion, and fright (4). Pilgrim Dusmano claims to speak of these "with no first world" (117).
Courage (Mut)
The quality represented by Mut, one of Cyrus Evenhand's henchmen, specifically courage without carefulness (49).
Coursing
The act of hunting, specifically the boar hunt undertaken by Palgrave Tacoman and the elites on Oraioi Polloi (150, 152, 153, 156).
Cracked-Glass Eyes
The appearance of Pilgrim Dusmano's eyes after being attacked by Mut (60). Also the type of jewel forming the eyepieces in Pilgrim's ritual mask (69). The pan-morphous figure in the Narrow Corner has these or jeweled eyes (122).
Cream (of the Cream)
Part of the answer given by the third Jehu Companion in the Jezebel drama, referring to the "illumined flesh and the ghosts supreme" (136).
Creative Cults
Hector Bogus refers to the "impelling level" of these, which must be achieved for a world to be strong (186).
Creature
Used to refer to various beings: Pilgrim Dusmano is called this by Cyrus Evenhand (25) and by Mut (50); Polder Dossman is called a "small creature" by Hector Bogus (185); the pan-morphous cultist figure in the Narrow Corner (122, 123); the apelike being (Holy Knacker) in the Narrow Corner (123, 126, 130, 131); the fury-child/firedrake in the Narrow Corner (124).
Cult / Cult Figure / Cult Members
A central element. Pilger Tisman is a "betrayed-in-death cult figure" whose followers expected a showy death (2). He has few followers left (2, 6), including del Mar, Maria and del Mar, Jacob (12). Cult figures are tricky, often taking things with them in death and leaving residues (3). They are loved, have devoted followings and magnetic effects (4). They can erect "horrendous ghost worlds" (4). Pilgrim Dusmano intentionally forms a cult (19, 21), recruiting students like Mary Morey, James Morey and Rhinestone Suderman, and Howard Praise (19, 103). His cult involves specific pleasures (62) and requires adherents (32). He manipulates minds, especially the young (31), and shapes followers through "brain scions" (30) and "bread-casting" (30–31) to prepare helpers in other worlds (30). His followers become ashamed of their devotion (28). The cult has a "Golden Grotto" (90) and an "All-Effects Hall" (90). It is associated with an "unpleasant sort of happiness" (28) and potentially evil (103). Dusmano is called a cult figure by Noah Zontik (28, 78, 84) and Judas Raffels (115), and referred to as such by the knacker (90). He seeks to make his image ("ideated self") (59, 64) and uses the Daylight Museum for this (59, 61). He eventually uses a ritual mask instead of a face (69). Palgrave Tacoman achieves swift status as a cult figure (155). Polder Dossman continues the cult (166, 170), seeks to make it thrive (173), considers becoming a Lord of the Zodiac for it (173), promotes the "Laughing God" title (189), experiences its dissolution after the mountain-moving (206), and is the focus of a final cult meeting (112). Cults are strong in the current decade, "absolutely blue chip" interworld (90), and are started by blind compulsion (19). Their combination is surprisingly easy (90). A deficiency of cults indicates a weak world (186).
Cultishness
Polder Dossman's cult appeal, which Hector Bogus dismisses as amounting to little on this world (187).
Cults (Combining/Deficiency of/Inept)
The knacker notes that combining cults is easier than expected (90). Pilgrim/Polder notes a "startling deficiency" of cults on the new world, even "inept cults" being absent (186).
Curator (Daylight Museum)
Clarence Music (103). He interacts with Pilgrim Dusmano and the Moreys, discussing Pilgrim's shadows and sanity (61), explaining the museum's rules (59), revealing items from the Duffy Walk-In Bijou (63), handling the Jezebel note (66), expressing bewilderment at the persecution of the Consul (66–67), and referring to the Consul's eyepiece (69). He is initially described as fearful but drawn to the "blood-magnet" (70) and later as "straight corned mutton" for his naive view of the populace (68).
Dark Contingency
Pilgrim Dusmano's term for the possibility of Prime World's existence and the associated dangers (21).
Darkness
Associated with Prime World (21) and the private state imposed on the watchers in the Narrow Corner by the pan-morph's vision (122). The Media Lords are identified by Noah Zontik as the true Lords of Unreason and Darkness (107). Frosty breath of unseen spirits is visible against the darkness in the Narrow Corner (125).
Daylight Museum
A museum favoring art that is "uncompromised and untrammeled," featuring "plain abundance" and no "dark corners" or "dark concepts" (59). It emphasizes clear representation and chaste colors, with rules against art inducing fever or excessive unease (59). Pilgrim Dusmano frequents it, partly to create his own "special image" (59). It houses works by Groben (63), van Gregory Ghi (66), Alessandro (66), Scanlon, Adam (65), Finnegan (65), and a triptych by "Joe Smith" (65). The curator is Clarence Music (61). Pilgrim has a report about Cyrus Evenhand delivered outside it (58) and later discusses art and the Consul with the curator and the Moreys inside (60–71).
Dazzle
A quality attributed to Pilger Tisman, whose aura makes him "a dazzle!" (7). Also part of the "shimmer" associated with Pilgrim Dusmano (37, 115, 203), and his "dripping hands" (115). Pilgrim Dusmano cannot become such a dazzle if he is merely derivative swamp gas (23).
Dead (Special Categories)
The coroner suggests that standard "alive" and "dead" are insufficient for world-jumpers, proposing alternatives like "Dead, subject to continuance" or "Not so dead as all that" (11).
Death (of Pilger Tisman)
An execution for "shockingly murderous and irresponsible deeds and behaviors" (1–2). Tisman is sentenced "to die with discomfort" via Yperite or Mustard gas (2). His death is attended by doctors, aides, a coroner, and police, not to save him, but to "weigh his death" using sophisticated and ingenious equipment (1). Tisman is expected to provide a "showy death" as a cult figure but fails, instead experiencing a "death delirium" (2). He successfully "world-jumps," taking his memory, identity, and consciousness-container with him (9–10), leaving behind a mocking, resurrected person-tone (9).
Death (of Polder Dossman)
Attended by Doctor Vonk, Hans August, and Judah Raphaelson, Og Scath (acting coroner), and Hector Bogus (acting brigadier of police) (210). Polder has a "light companion" in death, the proxy Longram (210–211). He is subjected vicariously to Longram's torments (211). His body is analyzed, revealing eidolon fiber, human flesh, and regressed or camel flesh (212). His final moment is the cessation of a "fluttering sliver" of his heart kept active by Bogus (214–215). He is heard screaming eternally from a deep distance, presumed to be in Hell (215).
Death Drama
The event of dying, from which those who carry forward minimal personal baggage might historically produce harmless ghosts (3).
Death's-Hand
A metaphorical grip or claim left on fortunes by the dead, often harder to remove than a living hand (95). Pilgrim plans to leave this on the fortunes of Cyrus Evenhand and his associates (95).
Death-Coma
A state described as a "pleasant coma" experienced on the Nine Worlds, characterized by awareness, emanating power, and influence; a "vital and sparkling repose" (157).
Death-Monitors / Death-Weighers
Officials, including doctors, aides, a coroner, and police, tasked with observing and measuring the process and phenomena of death, particularly in executions like Pilger Tisman's (1, 3). They use specialized equipment (1) and attempt to catalogue the tricks used for "carrying-forward" weighable substance (3). They fail to prevent Pilger Tisman's escape (9–11). Doctors Vonk, Hans August, and Judah Raphaelson fulfill this role for Polder Dossman (210).
Death-Scraps
Lesser doctors who might seek stipends for pronouncing persons dead, a role Doctors John Augustine and Judas Raffels consider usurping (117).
Declared Thing
Pilgrim Dusmano's doctrine of existence without opposites: high without low, light without dark, inside without outside, etc. (116). Noah Zontik questions if it has meaning (116).
Delectable
One of the nine locations making up the Nine Worlds to La Spezia (134, 146).
Delirium (Death)
The state Pilger Tisman enters after being gassed, during which he tries and fails to recall his planned heroic last words and gestures (2).
Delirium (Total)
The state of mind prevalent on Prime World, characterized by absolute logic that permits no deviation; considered the most fearful thing anywhere (21). Those on Prime World have "delirious minds" (22).
Delta Pattern
A brain impulse pattern of about three counts per second emitted by Pilger Tisman during his death throes, considered unusual for an unconscious person or a world-jumper, indicating a personal trick for gauging his jump (8).
Demeter
An archetypal figure mentioned alongside Simon Magus, Baubo, Adonis, Alexander, Broom-Witch, and Leviathan (154).
Demetriades, Anastasia
A figure who recounted the "prophetic frightfulness" of the Narrow Corner to Finnegan, Count, who then projected it back onto the location via visualization (127).
Demiurge, Chthonic
Invoked in the saying, "a chthonic demiurge will find work for idle hands" (46).
Demon(s), Gold-Symbol
A classification including Aurelion, the 79th recording spirit, who facilitates entry into the "underlay" cartel (148).
Demons
Mentioned in the dog-foot verse recited in the smoky passageway leading to the Narrow Corner: "Demons, demons, spew and spree! / Gouge your eyes out. Count them three" (124).
Derivative
A person or entity considered secondary, a reflection or projection rather than an original. Noah Zontik insists Pilgrim Dusmano is a derivative, possibly originating from the imagination of a dull prime person, comparing him to shimmering but substanceless swamp gas (23). Pilgrim denies being a derivative (23). Pilgrim later speaks of derivatives in the context of counterculture, claiming there are no originals anywhere (117).
Derivative People
The multitude of beings considered secondary or reflected, contrasted with the few "prime people" (14, 21, 22). Pilgrim acknowledges room for them in his presumption (22).
Devil
The curator identifies the force driving the destruction of the Consul as the "tragos-goat himself. . . the devil" (68).
Devil-Angels, Archetypical
The "unstable-hundred company" which Palgrave Tacoman joins upon the universal acceptance of his testament (154).
Devil-Revel
Pilgrim Dusmano's term for the collective, murderous pleasure derived by a nation from the destruction of a Consul (66).
Devils
A group whose personal testaments constitute the "ocean" of the group unconscious or mass media (143). They are distinguished by literary/eidetic styles and assigned identifiers (letters, Tarshish Syllabary signs, elemental symbols) (143). There are believed to be as many such publishing devils as there are elements (143). Nine new media devils have been discovered concurrently with nine new elements (143). They also possess the power to seize and dismember an unmasked man (70).
Dialectical Experts
Synonymous with "instant agitators" and "slashing wolves" who help incite the populace for Pilgrim Dusmano (68).
Dice Throwers, High Seven
An elite group associated with Fate, also called the "High Seven" (197, 198) or simply "High Dicers" (200). Their dicing is another name for Fate (201). Membership confers the highest status (197). A vacancy exists due to Merope's disappearance, and there is speculation Polder might fill it (197). Moira Morey declares it must be believed Polder is one of them (198).
Dimwits
The original people of the Prime World, described as giants who are the "pride of prime" (24).
Dingy Moment
The duration Og Scath will spend following Polder into the "shallow and dingy ditch" instead of Hell (213).
Discomfort
Pilger Tisman is sentenced to "die with discomfort," a punishment described as cruel but not unusual (2). Polder Dossman is also sentenced to this, with Hector Bogus having "private ideas" on how it might be achieved (211). Longram must add Polder's discomforts to his own suffering (211).
Dismal Den
A museum on Third Street specializing in "unruly pictures or statuary or transfixes," an alternative to the Daylight Museum (59). Also a place where one might observe expensive crockery made of swamp-born clay fired in Hell (60).
Displacement (of Worlds)
The slight shift between two coincident worlds, theorized by a student to generate the "incredible force" responsible for transforming ambient materials into commodities and for powering creativity (41–42).
Distraction
A term used by Pilgrim Dusmano regarding things that must be ignored during death to ensure memory continuity (17). Also used by Judas Raffels to describe the original meaning of "distract" (to draw asunder) when Pilgrim fears being torn apart by horses (118). The knoll where Pilgrim delivers his final sermon and is killed is referred to as the "knoll of the distraction" (119).
Divinity Glow
A radiance acquired by Mary Morey and James Morey after being imbued with numinosity by the knacker, making them seem like transcendent "cloud-walkers" (93).
Doctors Medical
A title or professional category. Judas Raffels and John Augustine hold this title (103). They question their presence in the cult (106), discuss Pilgrim's medical body and mask-like face (106), and consider collecting stipends for pronouncing people dead (117).
Dog (Companion)
The form taken by James Morey/Jake as a companion to Pilgrim/Polder (122, 159). Appears as a human-form dog, somber, silent, faithful, dwelling in shadow (150). He assembles hound-form dogs for hunting (151). He is present with the ariel when they come to Palgrave Tacoman (149). After death, he fiercely battles Wut in the Narrow Corner (128) before being destroyed and falling into the abyss, howling (129).
Dolls
Small effigies manipulated by Hector Bogus (181).
Domdaniel
A castle under the ocean, cited as a location where new archetypes (like Python) take up lodging (154).
Don Quixote in His Library
The title of a Doré illustration used as the basis for a drama on Cannes World, noted to be a misnomer for God in the throes of Creation (140).
Dongola
The specified destination for the messenger Aubrey Pym and his family (39, 40). Mrs. Pym recalls the Hemsteds went there earlier (39). Commerce exists between the Present World and such places (55).
Doors (Between Worlds)
Metaphorical openings between different situations or worlds, opened in peculiar, non-obvious ways (like the messenger ritual) that cannot be widely known or easily remembered (55). Apprehension is described as a key that fits many such doors (38). Iron doors are mentioned metaphorically as being slammed shut by the Body-Smith's vaunts (127).
Dorsetmoon, Philemon
One of the names listed as part of the Tisman/Dusmano/Tacoman/Tasman/Theissmand/Dosmens/Dusselmon/Dossman complex (146).
Doré Day
A day at the Cannes Perpetual Animation Festival dedicated to dramas based on illustrations by Gustave Doré (134, 138). On this day, the Marshal of Animations failed to provide a live actress for the role of Jezebel, leading to scandal (138).
Doré, Gustave
Gustave Doré (1832–1883), the French artist and illustrator known for his engravings of the Bible, Dante's Inferno, Don Quixote, and other works. His illustrations provide the basis for dramas performed at the Cannes Perpetual Animation Festival, including The Strange Nations Slain by the Lions of Samaria, Babylon Fallen, The Giant Antaeus, The Perilous Pass, The Mourners of Durandarte, Don Quixote in His Library (actually God in the throes of Creation), The Panther in the Desert, and The Resurrection of Lazarus (135, 140).
Dosmens, Pilatus
One of the names listed as part of the Tisman/Dusmano/Tacoman/Tasman/Theissmand/Dorsetmoon/Dusselmon/Dossman complex (146).
Dossman, Polder
The final name/identity assumed by the central character after his jump from the Nine Worlds (159). He arrives thirsty and disoriented on a stark, sharp-lined world (159, 161), accompanied by Moira Mara (ariel) and Jake Mara (dog) (159). He establishes commercial success rapidly but struggles with his cult (172–173). He claims high status (Archetype, Zodiac Lord, High Dicer) (201, 203) and performs miracles and wonders (200), including moving a mountain (205), but his power then wanes (206). He is revealed/suspected to be an artificial eidolon-construct (175, 178, 183). He confronts Hector Bogus (180–189) and is subsequently killed via the Hand from Heaven and corrosive sublimate (190), reanimated by galvanic shock (191), and finally dies after a confrontation with hecklers (201–215).
Dotty
The title of a "breath-flubbing" triptych displayed at the Daylight Museum, showing a girl clothed, unclothed, and visceral; signed "Joe Smith" on two panels (65).
Double Vision
Afflicts the clarified man (Polder) in the Narrow Corner, causing superimposed outlines in his mind (130). The panmorphous creature appears as if seen by double, triple, or dozen vision (122).
Doxies
Female followers or members of Pilgrim Dusmano's cult (103).
Drachmas
Currency mentioned by Pilgrim when finding cash in Mut's wallet (47–48).
Drag-World Gravity
One of the forces seemingly, but not actually, present at the commodity arrival floor (42).
Dray
A large, sturdy vehicle used by Mary Morey and James Morey, empowered by the knacker's numinosity, to transport the vast quantity of Mut Cult gold (92, 94, 95).
Dripping Hands
A characteristic attribute of Pilgrim Dusmano (115), Pelion Tuscamondo (139), and Polder Dossman (168, 203). The hands are said to drip light, dazzle, grace, gift, seed, solace, healing, and death (115, 203).
Drowning (of Statuette)
A "micromurder" performed by James Morey at Pilgrim Dusmano's urging (63–64, 67). The small wooden statuette with live eyes (Pilgrim's former eyes) is held underwater in an ornate crock until it is "drowned" (63–64). The act is considered a "token lust and token murder," a sauce for the anticipated destruction of the Consul (67, 71). The statuette struggles, screams underwater (67, 69), and its wooden limbs become displaced and deformed (71).
Duffy, Melchisedech
Owner of the "Walk-In Bijou in New Orleans," from which several strange art objects (Groben's statuette, van Gregory Ghi's paintings, Alessandro's paintings, the Dotty triptych) are on loan to the Daylight Museum (63, 66). He apparently keeps the best items hidden away (66).
Dummies (on a World)
From the "World-Jumper's Ballad," one of the stances humans take: "We stand like dummies on a world / Or be like sharpies jumping off it" (1).
Dunlunk's Fifth Law
“Any action in any world will inevitably set up parallel actions in parallel worlds” (30). Pilgrim systematically applies this law in his teaching and manipulation of selected minds; his worlds are not isolated from the consequences of one another.
Durandarte, Mourners of
The subject of a Doré illustration, forming the basis of a drama on Cannes World (140).
Dusmano, Pilgrim
The central character for much of the narrative. An enigmatic figure who lectures on alternate worlds and controllable world-jumping (15–18), advocating amorality and selective suicide (16–17). He forms a cult, attracting students like the Moreys, Rhinestone Suderman, and Howard Praise (19). He is associated with Noah Zontik (his "powerful friend") (20, 32) and opposed by Cyrus Evenhand (his "powerful enemy") (25). He possesses unusual abilities like flight (24) and passing through walls (24, 25), performs "small miracles" with a scarf (21, 23), and engages in vast, anomalous commerce (33, 41). He manipulates minds (31) and politics (32). He is described as potentially a derivative projection (23, 103), possibly shallow (23), but also an "authentic original" (23). His earlier counterpart Tisman has a distinctive call-tone and aura (6–7); Pilgrim has the familiar dripping hands (115). He kills Hut (38), ritually dispatches the Pym family as messengers (53–55), confronts the spy Trenchant (79–83), and is later revealed as the target for destruction by the Media Lords (108) before being pursued and killed by militia and horses (114–118). (See also Dossman, Polder for his later identity).
Dusselmon, Philip
One of the names listed as part of the Tisman/Dusmano/Tacoman/Tasman/Theissmand/Dosmens/Dorsetmoon/Dossman complex (146).
Dwarf, Putty
An interlocutor with Lorica and Albrecht Fairbrow, advocating the embrace of "valued antilife" and urging Palgrave Tacoman to become part of the "great creative ocean" at the "bottom" of existence (148, 149).
Eagle Joke (Upside-Down)
A metaphor used by Noah Zontik to describe a type of disorienting, "soaring joke" that momentarily inverts perception, like an eagle rolling onto its back in flight, making the world seem to disappear because the eagle sees only sky (22). Pilgrim Dusmano later dismisses Noah's subsequent argument as a "malodorous rock-shrew joke," not an upside-down eagle joke (24).
Earthquake
Occurs in the Western Sierras on the day Cyrus Evenhand becomes Consul, cited by Pilgrim Dusmano as an "evil omen" despite its statistical normality (80). Also, one of the phenomena accompanying the moving of Shining Mountain (205).
Ecumens
Alternate term for inhabited worlds or planes of existence; Pilgrim Dusmano seldom enters new lives, earths, or ecumens unprepared (30).
Eidetic Life
A state of existence, possibly created by Media, which Hector Bogus contrasts with "real life" but suggests can still exist (192).
Eidetic Lords
Powerful entities associated with the Media Lords (175, 181) and possibly involved in the creation or manipulation of beings like Polder Dossman (175). They are served by individuals like Hector Bogus (181, 185) and potentially represent forces of unreason and darkness (175). Polder refers to Hector Bogus as an Eidetic Lord (185). They seem to possess or control specific types of power or reality (181, 186).
Eidolon Fiber
A non-flesh component identified in the analysis of Polder Dossman's body, mixed with human and regressed flesh (212).
Eidolon(s)
Artificial constructs, projections, or possibly beings based on a human template but heavily modified (195, 196). Polder Dossman is identified or suspected to be one (175, 195, 196, 203). Hector Bogus is an "Eidolon Lord" (180) or "eidolon-chief" (194) who creates miniature, tortured eidolons (181–183). The term is linked to the Media Lords (180). A sequence of nine eidolons, progressing from stone to "rapture-flesh," is described, which turn on their creator (196). James Morey fears becoming a "mere eidolon of an eidolon" following a cult figure (101).
Eidolon-Godlings
Hector Bogus's dismissive term for potentially powerful but artificial figures like Polder Dossman (197).
Eidolon-Masters
Creators or manipulators of eidolons, like those who experimented on Polder Dossman (212) or Hector Bogus (209).
Electric Man
A popular press designation attributed to charismatic figures like Pilgrim Dusmano (37), Pelion Tuscamondo (139), and Polder Dossman (203).
Element(s)
Fundamental components of reality, possibly numbering over one hundred (143). Also used symbolically in literary criticism to identify the styles of "media devils" (143). The discovery of nine new elements coincides with nine new media devils (143). Palgrave Tacoman becomes associated with a new, unstable element announced by the post boy (152, 154). The term also refers to the materials present "in the ambient" at the commodity arrival floor (41).
Elites
The privileged class inhabiting certain worlds or participating in specific events. They pass lifetimes on Cannes World enjoying the Perpetual Animation Festival (135, 137). On Oraioi Polloi, they engage in the ritual boar hunt (150–153), have spokesmen (Albert Fineface, Whitebread, Leslie) (141, 155), and maintain a close association with parrot flocks (151). Pilgrim Dusmano refers to the "intense elite" who understand how to wield power (187), while Hector Bogus dismisses the "brittle elites" (187).
Enacian
A large type of human, possibly a giant; one of the forms the pan-morphous creature in the Narrow Corner might resemble (122).
Enclaves
Distinct alternate worlds or realities often characterized by peculiar biological or social rules, such as those where boy children are born with beards or females fully formed (17), or where young adult males are seasonally horned and hoofed (17). Pilger Tisman's failed death performance might have been analyzed differently using more sophisticated equipment found in "other enclaves" (2).
End of Pyrotechnics
A phrase denoting the moment of Pilger Tisman's apparent death (the cessation of vital signs and the extinguishing of aura and tone), which lasts only three seconds before his successful worldjump and the reappearance of his aura and tone (9).
Environs
Used generally to refer to specific alternate worlds or settings, such as the one recalled by Pilgrim Dusmano where males are horned and hoofed (17), or the location ("that environs") where Cyrus Evenhand feels diminished by Pilgrim's attack (25). Pilgrim plans for generational support across various environs (30).
Eschatological Things
The four final realities or concepts, for which Prime World serves as the "base and anchor" (21). The laughter directed at Polder's bogus-gold tooth plug comes from "creatures of every eschatological case" (200).
Evenhand, Cyrus
Pilgrim Dusmano's primary antagonist, designated his "one powerful enemy" (6, 25, 86). He is the leader of a powerful and secret organization (27) employing eight henchmen with code names (25, 48–49). Operating behind a mask (26), he holds the anonymous office of the Consul (58, 66), with the code name Rut (49). Accounted a good, spotless, and saintly man (25, 49, 66, 71), he conducts his off-world commerce via "blissful permit" (90). Pilgrim targets him for destruction despite his goodness (50), leaks his identity (58), inciting national hysteria (66–68). Cyrus Evenhand listens in on Pilgrim's conversations (76) and is later killed and dismembered by the Media Lords or the populace (108), his vast fortunes becoming derelict (89, 94).
Everything Is Allowed
The core message Pilgrim Dusmano imparts to his "bright young people" or students (18).
Fairfronter, Lord
An older, elegant Lord Spiritual and member of Pilgrim Dusmano's inner cult, recognizable by the rare "Golden Shovel Pip" and "Pilgrim Staff" he wears (75). He expresses anxiety about Dusmano leaving the world, praises his advancement of posthuman personality, questions the timing, and asks about a replacement leader (75). He pledges to incorporate Dusmano's sayings into the cult (78) and inquires about arrangements for Dusmano's desired death (78). He later cautions Dusmano to be careful, calling him their only cult figure (78). Present at the final cult gathering (103), he questions whether Dusmano is a Christus sending a Paraclete (104), disputes Judas Raffels' claim about green-thorn time being out of season (112), and cautions Judas Raffels about the subjectivity of his visions (106).
Fairbrow, Albrecht
An elite companion of Palgrave Tacoman and Jeanie on Oraioi Polloi (147). Though described by the narrator as one of the "deeply evil men" (148), he compliments Lorica on killing the first boar (153). He is assigned by Palgrave to hunt the second, dangerous "scurrying boar" (154), but his horse's legs are broken, and he is killed by the boar while fighting on foot (155). His death scene matches an image previously displayed on the post boy's horn, and his dead face resembles Palgrave's (155).
Faith Sufficient
A prerequisite state or quality attributed to Pelion Tuscamondo, along with station and connections, allowing him to successfully request mountains for his animation backdrop (141).
False Lord Spiritual
The designation applied to the spy Trenchant, implying he held credentials but lacked the true essence or status of a Lord Spiritual (79, 184). Identified as such by Pilgrim (83), he is seized by genuine Media Lords and killed by Pilgrim (83). His leftover pieces are later collected (84).
Familied Men
Pilgrim Dusmano's preferred messengers, chosen because their families serve as "built-in hostages," ensuring the completion of missions (34). Aubrey Pym fits this criterion (34). Pilgrim attempts to send families matching the "typical size and shape" of the destination world (36).
Fate
Personified by or equivalent to the High Seven Dice Throwers; their collective dicing determines outcomes (201). Polder Dossman's destiny is said to ride on a coin flip (209). "Fair fate" is questioned for not granting Cyrus Evenhand an uneventful first day as Consul (81).
Fear
A prominent emotion. Pilger Tisman's attendants fear his humor (5). Pilgrim is attacked by Mut, realizing his peril in "balanced panic" (45). Pilgrim later feels "clammy fear" seeing the horses intended to kill him (118). The Pym family is apprehensive (38). Polder experiences fear when asking about the coin toss outcome (208) and about being damned to Prime World (207). The elites feel fear from the scurrying boar (154). Crowds experience fear and trembling before Polder (200). Pilgrim Dusmano is white-eyed and twitching with fear (115).
Fetish Hands
Hairy, gripping appendages associated with Prime World, imagined to emerge from the earth and seize victims with bone-crushing strength (21).
Fetish World
Pilgrim Dusmano's term for Prime World, emphasizing its oppressive materiality where metaphors are concrete, reality is rigidly literal, and "compensation is calculated and extracted" (21).
Fetishistic
An adjective used by Pilgrim Dusmano to describe the meticulous, "crabbed," and irrational "ultimate accounts" kept on Prime World (20). Noah Zontik uses it to characterize prime people, should they mirror Prime World's logic (22).
Fever
A quantifiable physiological reaction to visual stimuli; the Daylight Museum prohibits art causing more than a four-point rise (59). Prime World is described as inducing "miasmic fever" (21), and Noah Zontik calls the hypothetical original Pilgrim "fevered" (23).
Field Force Nexus
A possible scientific description of the commodity arrival floor, suggesting it operates via electrical forces (42).
Fifteen-Year Leap
The possible illusion of a time interval created by Pilger Tisman's world-jump "to upstream cliffs," potentially explaining the time elapsed between his death and the main narrative events (12).
Final Place
The feared final destination beyond the world-jumper's escapes. Bogus threatens Polder with it, while Noah's commission requires him to accompany Pilgrim even if hell is his final place. The timeless Nine Lives are not described as exhausted before this happens (27, 185, 208).
Final Things
Used in several contexts: 1. The four eschatological realities anchored by Prime World (21). 2. Absolute conclusions or ends, which Pilgrim claims to avoid "forever" (131). 3. The ultimate events unfolding during the narrative's climax, as noted by Doctor Judas Raffels (108). 4. The nature of time and direction, which Pilgrim insists are never final (75). 5. Death, described by Dusmano as seldom final (17), although Cyrus Evenhand's killing must be final (26). 6. Outcomes in the Narrow Corner, which the Holy Knacker declares are final (130, 132).
Fineface, Albert
Spokesman and captain of the elites on Cannes World. He investigates the Jezebel performance, wounds the Marshal's tongue, and acts as broker for Pelion Tuscamondo's publication in the Group Unconscious (137–144). Albrecht Fairbrow and later Leslie Whitebread occupy related roles on Oraioi Polloi.
Finnegan
An artist known for carving uniquely vital cigar-store Indians (65) and possibly the mentor of van Gregory Ghi (66). Finnegan, Count is also mentioned as having projected Anastasia Demetriades's visions of the Narrow Corner onto the place (127).
Fire-Drake
One form assumed by the demented Pym child in the Narrow Corner afterlife, characterized by rage and destructive power (124). It engages in battle with the ariel (126, 128).
Fire-Flesh Person
Pilgrim Dusmano's term for himself, implying a nature immune to harm from ordinary ("common and camelous clay") sources (85).
First World
The originating or primary reality in a series of worlds. Pilgrim Dusmano speaks of counterworlds having "no first world" (117).
Fish Eggs, Prime
What a drowning man gourmandizes in an illustrative anecdote, representing a desperate seizing of opportunity even in catastrophe (46).
Five-Pint Tankard
An "old period piece" container with a flip lid, used by the assailant Mut to collect Pilgrim Dusmano's blood during a ritualistic attack (46). Mut later drinks the collected blood (51).
Flesh-Meat Bodies
The physical corpses sought by Pilgrim Dusmano with intense lust, valued as much as, or more than, the fortunes associated with them (95).
Flesh-Smith
The entity encountered in the Narrow Corner, also identified as the Holy Knacker and body-smith (126). Described as having an ape-shape and rank flesh (131), it battles the clarified Polder (128), smells of molten gold fluxed with lime (131), and attempts to fix Polder into a final form before being killed and thrown into the abyss (126, 131).
Flickering Mind
The unstable mental state of Pilger Tisman during his death delirium, from which Wilcove Funk (Doctor) wishes they could retrieve his last thoughts (2). Pilgrim's mind is also described this way when distracted during Mut's attack (47). Pilgrim extinguishes the "flickering life" in the spy Trenchant's heart (83).
Flight
An ability possessed by Pilgrim Dusmano, allowing him to pass through walls (24, 25) and ascend into the air with a finesse surpassing birds (24).
Floor, Commodity Arrival
See Arrival Floor / Area, Commodity.
Flut
The code name for one of Cyrus Evenhand's henchmen, signifying flood or overflowing (48). He is one of the three initially targeted by the Media Lords (73). His fortune is designated for collection by the knacker (89).
Fluttering
Describes the motion of the last sliver of Polder Dossman's heart, kept animate by Hector Bogus in a torture cabinet (214). Its fluttering grows more intense in agony before ceasing, signifying Polder's final end (214–215).
Folk Ocean
An alternative name for the Group Unconscious, the underlying psychic medium where testaments can be published (142).
Folk-Knitting
Pilgrim Dusmano's term for the creation of "red history," specifically through the collective, ritualistic destruction of a figure like the Consul (67).
Fool
Pilgrim Dusmano deems the spy Trenchant a fool for attempting a double game and asserts that fools should not be allowed to live (83).
Fool's, Tom
A museum located "out along the parkway," offering an alternative experience to the Daylight Museum, perhaps specializing in the absurd or grotesque (59).
Footprints (of Brain Tracks)
A metaphorical trace or essence of mental patterns. Jude Ravel (Doctor) speculates whether Pilger Tisman took the footprints of his brain tracks with him when he worldjumped, or if such footprints could generate a new person (11).
Fortean World
Named by Noah Zontik as one aspect of the Prime World of prime people, alongside the uninfused, grubby, spiritualist, and quack aspects (23).
Fortune-Marrow
The essential wealth scraped from the "affairbones" (the metaphorical bones of their affairs) of the dead by a specialized knacker, as arranged by Pilgrim for Cyrus Evenhand and his associates (89).
Four Points
The maximum rise in the fever index permitted when viewing art in the Daylight Museum (59).
Four-Year-Old Child
See Child.
Frame of Mind
The mental state required for successful world-jumping: apprehensive, nervous, determined, daring, creative, defiant, and open (39). Pilgrim reminds the Pyms of this before their dispatch (39).
Freedom of Entry
A right asserted by the militia under Media Lord authority, overriding physical barriers in the name of "Total Freedom" (114).
Freedom to Arrest
Claimed as a "fundamental freedom" by the militia, justifying arrest based on their own strength and their Lords' power, superseding written warrants (114).
French Curve
An instrument, along with a straightedge, seemingly used to create the unnaturally sharp lines defining the stark world where Polder Dossman arrives (161).
Friend, Powerful
Considered a necessity for every man (27). Noah Zontik is Pilgrim Dusmano's "one powerful friend" (20, 27, 86). Pilger Tisman leaves behind only one such friend after his death (6, 12). Og Scath assumes this role, albeit reluctantly, for Polder Dossman (212–213).
Fringies
A category of people (along with nonscientists, pseudos, etc.) who correctly intuited that alternate worlds occupy the same local space (14).
Frog
One of the possible forms resembled by the pan-morphous creature in the Narrow Corner (122).
Frustrated-in-Death Man
Wilcove Funk (Doctor)'s diagnosis of Pilger Tisman, indicating Tisman did not achieve a satisfying or ritually complete death, unlike a "wise-in-death animal" (2).
Fugaro Vortex, Secondary
A magnetic phenomenon suspected, but not confirmed by instruments, at the commodity arrival floor (42).
Funk, Wilcove (Doctor)
One of the three physicians overseeing Pilger Tisman's death-weighing (1). He provides commentary on Tisman's state ("frustrated-in-death," "betrayed-in-death cult figure") (2), death-weighing procedures (3), Tisman's aura and call-tone (4), and his own large head and back-brain (4–5). He monitors Tisman's cerebral juglans (5), discusses afterlife topology (9), and potentially conceals the "compensating thing" Tisman leaves (10). Later appears as Doctor Vonk attending Polder Dossman's death (210), offering analysis (211–212) and confirming Og Scath's death (214).
Furnaces (in All-Effects Hall)
Equipment used for casting golden images, managed by the Moreys (90). James uses one, already fired by Pilgrim, to melt down the Mut Cult gold (97). A separate "flashfurnace" contains molten gold for plating the knacker's corpse (98, 100).
Fury-Child
An alternate designation for the hostile, shape-shifting child entity encountered in the Narrow Corner (124, 160).
Gateway Deaths
The moments of death for outlaw world-jumpers, characterized by spectacular leaps across dimensions, likened to mountain-climbing or abyss-leaping (9).
Gestes
The narrative or legendary accounts of a cult; Pilgrim Dusmano feels his clumsy killing must be heavily revised before entering the gestes of his own cult (25).
Ghost Worlds
Horrendous counterworlds erected by tricky departing cult figures that impinge, sometimes physically, on the real world, causing dislocation, disturbance, erosion, and fright (4). Contrasted with the less harmful "after-appearances" or "harmless ghosts" of earlier times (3–4).
Ghosts
Relatively harmless "after-appearances" resulting from individuals carrying only minimal personal baggage (memory, identity, consciousness) forward from the "death drama" in earlier times (3). Distinct from the later, more malevolent "ghost worlds" (4).
Giants
Dimwitted inhabitants of the lowering sky over Prime World, considered the "pride of prime" (24). Also, a term used for powerful figures, like the "money giants" who lust after fortunes (95) or "good giants" whose toppling brings rich satiation (50).
Gibberish, High
An unintelligible, convoluted language spoken powerfully and eloquently by Polder Dossman, particularly during his large evening meetings (199, 200, 203). It is initially impressive but eventually breeds resentment and heckling (199). Hecklers declare it easily faked and no sign of true power (202, 203).
Gift (Dripping)
One of the qualities said to emanate from the "dripping hands" of figures like Pilgrim Dusmano and Polder Dossman (115, 203).
Glaciers
Mentioned by the defiant Pym child as passageways where he will hide and trap Pilgrim during his future travels between worlds (54).
Gleam, Godly
A quality often seen in the eyes of cult figures (87). Pilgrim Dusmano possesses a new and mutated version (87).
Glob (of Flesh-Meat)
A great roasted portion served to Pilgrim Dusmano at the Media Club, identified as the flesh of the henchman Blut (87). It is served without condiment, bread, or wine, being "its own everything" (87).
Glottle
A device required to be held in the mouth by Consuls when speaking officially, serving to trammel the tongue and disguise the speech (69). Also, one of the body parts torn out during a Greek Katastrophy (71).
Glow (Divinity / Numinous / Auferous)
A special radiance imparted to Mary Morey and James Morey by the knacker via a "simple trick" known for millennia by his ancestors, making them appear as transcendent "cloud-walkers" (93). This "numinosity" is linked to exceptional strength (93) but fades after the knacker is mutilated (97, 100). The knacker, transformed into a golden statue, pulses with "golden incandescence" (100) and a "glow beyond the glow of gold" (101). Polder exhibits a "nervous glow" before attempting mountain-moving (204).
Glut
The code name for one of Cyrus Evenhand's eight henchmen, signifying blaze or flame (48). His fortune is designated for collection by Pilgrim's knacker (89).
Glutting, Final
The concluding stage of Pilgrim Dusmano's killing process, characterized by "quick joy" in the destruction (83).
Gnat Lords
One of the categories of Lords (along with Pressmen, Forum, Articum, Tinsel, Spiritual, and Media) who have declared "permanent revolution" (81). Pilgrim Dusmano admits to being a member (81).
Gnats
Metaphorically, minor transgressions, inconsequential details, or bad omens used to attack opponents when lacking substantial cause (80, 81). Contrasted with the "great and ungainly camels" that are overlooked or "swallowed whole" (72, 81). The Media Lords and others are adept at "straining at gnats" (72, 108). Trenchant dismisses certain apparent omens against Cyrus Evenhand as mere gnats, "the little gnats of the age of unreason" (81).
Gnats-Weight
A minuscule amount of evidence, which the young Lords Spiritual can always find or manufacture against any man to declare ruination (74).
Gnu, Bushman
The source of gelatin considered "nonpareil," slightly superior to the camel-derived equivalent (165).
Goad, Camel
An attribute held in the left hand by Polder Dossman when he performs the mountain-moving miracle (205).
Goat-Kid
A small, recently dead goat whose body Mary Morey brings into the All-Effects Hall (99). She places it before the dying knacker's face just as James pours molten gold into his cavity (99). The kid's body seemingly understands the knacker's final compassionate expression and is given "care and disposal" by Mary (100).
Goatish Gonads
Along with deviled brains and spastic spleens, one of the metaphorical organs representing the base, reactive nature of the populace when stirred up by "instant agitators" (68).
God (Laughing God)
A title Pilgrim/Polder attempts to promote for his cult, based on a perceived local leaning toward such a name (189). Hector Bogus asserts Polder is not the "god type" and incapable of real laughter (189).
God of Ears
An entity invoked by Jude Ravel (Doctor) when remarking on the uniqueness of Tisman's call-tone ("No other person, thank the god of ears, could ever sound that sound.") (6).
God-Goop
Slang used by Hector Bogus for the substance or influence that animated Polder Dossman, suggesting it was bestowed long ago for utilitarian purposes (191).
Godlet
Noah Zontik's term for a cult figure like Pilgrim Dusmano, suggesting perhaps he is the "correct godlet for the postanarchic age" (105).
Golden Grimoire
The source of the epigraph for Chapter 8 (102).
Golden Grotto
The ornate front section or public face of the Pilgrim Cult headquarters, located before the armored All-Effects Hall (90, 94). The gilded knacker statue is rolled out into the Grotto for display (100), and James Morey frequently stands in its shadows (101).
Golden Shovel Pip
A rare mantle brooch worn by Lord Fairfronter, signifying his membership in Pilgrim Dusmano's cult and his work establishing the Pilgrim image (75).
Golden Shovel, Song of the
The source of the epigraph for Chapter 6 (72). Noah Zontik wears the pin of the Golden Shovel (84).
Golden Straw
A drinking implement disdained by Judas Raffels (Doctor) when he seizes the grace cup during the cult meeting (113).
Gonads, Goatish
See Goatish Gonads.
Good and Evil
Pilgrim denies guilt and accountability, while Polder argues that evil supplies motion against a static Good. These are the protagonist's arguments, not settled laws of the narrative. Evenhand's goodness attracts destructive hatred; Longram's goodness makes barren land flourish. Bogus's cruelty toward artificial persons raises a further question: whether denying a sufferer's reality can excuse inflicting pain (16, 67–71, 182–188, 211–215).
Gooney
How Pilgrim Dusmano intends to handle Mut when arranging his death, implying awkwardness or foolishness (91).
Goop, Galopading
Hector Bogus's term for the animating substance instilled in figures like Polder, suggesting it's a concept believed by peasants but perhaps not by manipulators like himself (191).
Gore-Mass
The piece of Wut's throat torn out by the dog in the Narrow Corner; the dog likely loses it before finding its voice again (129).
Gothic Mountains
Part of the mountainous backdrop ordered by Pelion Tuscamondo for the Resurrection of Lazarus animation, characterized by steepness, menace, and spires twinkling blue (141).
Gout (of Water)
A drop or portion; Albert Fineface promises Pelion that his testament will be published in every gout of water from the Folk Ocean (142).
Governor (over Property)
A role, along with guardian, that can be declared for a trustworthy and knowing man over the derelict property of declared traitors (89). Pilgrim Dusmano positions himself for this role regarding the assets of Cyrus Evenhand and his associates (89).
Grace (Dripping / Restraining)
One of the qualities said to drip from the "dripping hands" of cult figures like Pilgrim Dusmano (115, 203). Also, a quality Hector Bogus claims the Media Lords possess, allowing them to restrain themselves from depredations (187).
Grace Cup
A ritual vessel containing quince wine, part of the cult meeting ceremony (112). Judas Raffels (Doctor) seizes it and drinks directly, disdaining the golden straw (113).
Grain of Sand
Used by Pilgrim Dusmano to illustrate the infinitesimal probability of encountering Prime World ("as small as a grain of sand compared to a solar system medium in size") (20). Noah Zontik retorts that even a grain of sand is a nuisance in a giant's shoe (20).
Grand Jump
The final leap made by a world-jumper, like Pilger Tisman, "out over the chasm" during their gateway death (8).
Grays
One of the nonchromatic colors noted in Pilger Tisman's unique aura (7).
Greed
Blamed by Hector Bogus for the decision by Polder's nine pleasure-world selves to exclude the tenth self (Polder Prime) from sharing their experiences (208). The knacker asserts he has no greed, proposing an eight-to-one split of the confiscated fortunes (96).
Greek Katastrophy
Pilgrim Dusmano's term for the ritual destruction of the Consul, which he describes as more vital and dramatic than Roman arena games or Greek tragedy (69–70). He details its classic form involving the prolonged torture and dismemberment of a virgin victim by the entire community (70–71).
Greek Tragedy
The curator's comparison for the impending destruction of the Consul, seeing it as "stark evil coming on goat feet" (68). Pilgrim contrasts his preferred "Greek Katastrophy" as much more pleasurable (69).
Green Camel Milk
One of the beverages (along with water and whey) brought to Polder Dossman after his reanimation, which he drinks nervously (192). Also offered as a drink by someone during Polder's arrival on the stark world (159).
Green Scum
What Cyrus Evenhand imagines veins the giant insect form he perceives in Pilgrim Dusmano (25).
Green-Thorn Time
The specific budding stage of thorns in the thicket where Pilgrim hides; Judas Raffels (Doctor) sees this supernaturally, contradicting the autumn season, implying Pilgrim has altered time locally (112). Polder arrives on the stark world long past green-thorn time (159).
Grinder-Shredder / People-Grinder
A large machine appearing alongside stone benches before the Pyms' dispatch (52). Pilgrim expresses unease, noting its size seems appropriate for grinding people (52). He later stuffs the bodies of the Pym family into it for disposal (55–56). The machine is removed by workmen after use (56).
Gripping Hands (Sinewy)
Characteristic of Prime World and its inhabitants; hairy, fetish hands that emerge from the earth to grip ankles with bone-crushing strength (21). Prime people are those "with the sinewy, gripping hands" (22).
Groben
The artist who carved the little wooden statuette with live eyes, displayed at the Daylight Museum (63). The carving is considered mediocre, but the eyes are remarkable (63). It is judged one of the strangest carvings Groben ever did (71).
Grotesque Act
Pilgrim Dusmano's remembered assessment of the ritual method used to dispatch messengers (40). He later refers to the method used on the Pyms as grotesque (53).
Grotto, Golden
See Golden Grotto.
Group Unconscious
An alternative name for the "Folk Ocean," the underlying psychic medium containing collective testaments and memories, into which Pelion Tuscamondo buys the right to publish his image (142, 144).
Grubby World
One of the aspects of the Prime World of prime people, according to Noah Zontik (23).
Guardian (over Property / Prophetic)
Role assumed over derelict property (89). Also, the role the Moreys are documented as by the knacker, posing as "prophesied guardians" returning from the grave to claim the Mut Cult gold (93).
Guilt
