Considered an illusion, unreal, according to Pilgrim Dusmano's amoral philosophy derived from the existence of alternate worlds (16). Also used regarding the coroner's feeling when certifying world-jumpers as simply 'dead' (11).
Gut
The code name for one of Cyrus Evenhand's eight henchmen, signifying property (49). He is one of the three initially targeted by the Media Lords (73). His fortune is designated for collection by Pilgrim's knacker (89).
Guttering Brain
The state of Pilger Tisman's brain as monitored by Wilcove Funk (Doctor) during the death-weighing (5).
Gyne Peribebleene-ton-Helion
An archetype described as "Woman Wrapped-in-the-Sun," listed alongside Hermes, Homunculus, Moloch, Fisherman, Huracan, and Beggar-King (155).
Hand of Heaven
A meteorological manipulation, apparently contractable, which points down at its designated subject (161, 163, 168). Polder Dossman uses a visible version, paid for with gold (168), activates it to impress locals (163), modifies it (161), and puts it on standby (161). It possesses a genuine, invisible counterpart with a cloudy subscript (“Protect this least of mine”) specifically intended for Og Scath as protector (168). Hector Bogus, as an Eidetic Lord, can modify the Hand’s phenomena, adding thunder, lightning, gold sparkle, and specific scents (184), but later uses it impulsively to seize Polder and dip him in corrosive sublimate (190–191), an action deemed unethical (191). Polder adopts its pointing gesture (168). The Hand is destroyed by Polder's mountain-moving feat (206), an event attributed to Polder having broken it (207).
Hands, Dripping
A mysterious cultic term describing Pilgrim Dusmano’s hands, which are said to drip light, dazzle, grace, gift, seed, and solace (115). The spreading-out of these hands is considered a grand gesture (115). Polder Dossman emulates this, possessing dispensing hands that scatter manna and fishhooks which metaphorically catch onto the vulnerability of those encountered (170).
Happiness
An "unpleasant sort" of emotion specifically associated with the Dusmano cult and particularly affecting those peripherally involved (28). Also invoked by Pilgrim as essential, along with trust, for the Pym family before their dispatch, though qualified by the need for apprehension (53).
Heads Will Roll
A contemporary song hit whistled with grim humor by Jude Ravel (Doctor) after Tisman’s successful world-jump prompts the brigadier of police to threaten repercussions (10). Judas Raffels (Doctor) also whistles the tune while leading the militia toward Pilgrim, anticipating an execution (114).
Hecklers
Opponents who interrupt Polder's meetings. Polder kills some with lightning, leaving twitching corpses; the survivors acquire shields and intensify their attacks. Some are parents of children he has killed. They demand that he move Shining Mountain, and seven main groups are crushed by its falling boulders (199–205).
Hell
Presented as one of only two ways off the dreaded Prime World, paradoxically considered the more bearable option by Pilgrim Dusmano (21). It is the potential destination for the tenth part of Polder Dossman that does not reside in the Nine Worlds (208), and Polder fears Prime World partly because it is rumored to be one of Hell's gates (208). Og Scath is fated to follow Polder there if necessary (207), and Hector Bogus maliciously wishes Polder there (208). It is also depicted as a potential location ("out in the Southgate complex") for experiencing extreme sensations (59), and as a place where certain pottery is fired (60). The Legacy's opening promise of pleasure before hell is qualified by the later account of nine timeless aspects that continue enjoying themselves (133, 146, 208). The Polder-sliver provides a good imitation of a soul screaming eternally in hell (214, 215).
Hemsteds
A family name; Mrs. Pym recalls they went to Dongola earlier in the year before the Pyms were sent there as messengers (39).
Henchmen
The eight secret associates of Cyrus Evenhand (Rut), the Consul (49). Identified by the code names Blut, Brut, Flut, Glut, Gut, Hut, Mut, and Wut (48–49, 89), they are described as externalizations of Evenhand's own flaws or "spots" (51). Pilgrim kills Hut (38, 49), initiating conflict, and later identifies the others after obtaining Mut's wallet (48). These associates function partly through Evenhand's "murky headquarters" (25), utilizing voice-and-vision devices and psychic vehicles (26). After their anticipated deaths, Pilgrim engages a knacker to seize their substantial fortunes (89).
High Seven Dice Throwers
An esoteric, high-status group associated with Fate, possessing seven positions (201). A vacancy exists due to the disappearance of Merope (197). Moira Morey asserts that it must be believed Polder Dossman has become one of the seven, regardless of the truth (198), a status Polder later claims (201, 203).
Holiness-Through-Strength
The public persona attributed to Mut, one of Cyrus Evenhand's henchmen, noted for his formidable strength (48).
Holy Knacker
The name bestowed by Mary Morey upon the golden statue formed from the eviscerated and gold-filled body of the knacker (101). The statue captures the knacker’s final, paradoxical expression of "strangest compassion" (99). The term also refers to a hulking, apelike entity encountered in the Narrow Corner after death (122, 123). This being, identified as the flesh-smith and body-smith (126), smells inexplicably of molten gold treated with lime flux (131) and declares the finality of results in that realm (132) after being thrown into the pit by Polder (131).
Horned and Hoofed
A temporary physical state adopted by young male adults during the rutting season in a particular alternate environs recalled by Pilgrim Dusmano (17).
Hostages, Built-In
Pilgrim Dusmano's term for the families of messengers, believing their existence ensures the messenger will fulfill their dangerous task rather than fleeing or dying (34, 36).
Hound
The post-death manifestation or companion role of James Morey, paired with his sister Mary/Moira (the ariel), as servitors to their cult figure (122, 159, 213). He appears as a somber, faithful, human-form dog dwelling in shadow (150). He assembles hound-form dogs for hunting (151). After death, he battles Wut in the Narrow Corner (128) before being destroyed and falling into the abyss, his howls echoing from the depths (129).
Humpbacked Clay
According to Vonk (Doctor), a term for primordial flesh derived from Rimskanski, representing a debasement of the concept of 'vital fluid'. Samples exist on slides, and it is found mixed with eidolon fiber and human flesh in Polder Dossman (212).
Humpbacked Flesh
A term associated with several concepts: the "order of the humpbacked flesh," linked to the 'Camel's Revenge' group (85); the "old humpback-flesh camel motif" incorporated into Palgrave Tacoman's archetypal testament (154); and a cryptic reference by Hector Bogus to a troublesome "plastic, less-than-human substratum" (195).
Hut
The code name for one of Cyrus Evenhand's henchmen, representing the harbor, shelter, or hat (38, 49). Pilgrim Dusmano selectively kills him first, viewing the act as an opening move ("ante") in his conflict with Evenhand's organization (38, 49). Hut's fortune is later targeted by Pilgrim's knacker (89).
Hy-Brasail
One of the nine locations comprising the Nine Worlds to La Spezia, part of the exclusive Legacy of the rich (134, 146).
Hypnotic Man
A popular press designation attributed to charismatic figures like Pilgrim Dusmano (37), Pelion Tuscamondo (139), and Polder Dossman (203). Polder's eyebrows are also noted for their gently hypnotic effect (170).
Ideated Self
The self-conceived image that Pilgrim Dusmano actively works to create and project, partly through frequenting museums (59, 64).
Identity
One of the potentially weighable aspects (along with memory and consciousness) that dying persons might carry forward with them (3). Pilger Tisman succeeds in taking his identity when he world-jumps (10). Pilgrim Dusmano asserts that the apparent celestial locations of galaxies are merely notes in cipher, as there isn't enough room to write down all their identities in one place (15). The public identity of the assailant Mut is recalled by Pilgrim after waking from the attack (48). Revealing the identity of a Consul is a catalyst for destruction (58, 68).
Identity and Fragmentation
A recurring theme concerning the unstable, composite, and often artiﬁcial nature of the self. The central protagonist exists under numerous names (Pilger Tisman; Pilgrim Dusmano; Pelion Tuscamondo; Palgrave Tacoman; Paladin Tajiman; Polycletus Tasman; Palmas Thasomen; Paulus Theissmand; Pilatus Dosmens; Philemon Dorsetmoon; Philip Dusselmon; Polder Dossman) suggesting a fractured or sequential identity across different realities or "complexes" (146). Noah Zontik argues that Dusmano is a "derivative," a "projection" originating from another's imagination, akin to substanceless "swamp gas" (23), though Dusmano insists he is an "authentic original" (23). Dusmano uses the metaphor of being a "bundle of sticks," a million parallel selves with no single dominant identity (77). This fragmentation extends to consciousness and memory, which are "weighable" substances potentially carried forward after death (3) but are often lost or unreliable (10–11, 160). The concept of Eidolons further complicates identity, suggesting beings (including potentially Polder Dossman) are artiﬁcial constructs built on a human base or entirely fabricated (175, 178, 183, 196). The narrative repeatedly questions the idea of a single, stable self and presents identities that are fluid, multiple, projected, or manufactured.
Idol
What Pilgrim Dusmano states he is "in the way of becoming" (63). Mary Morey refers to his jeweled eyes as "idol-eyes" (63).
Idol-Thing
Referenced in the Museum-Munchers' Daybook epigraph as having "jewel eyes" (57).
Illusions
Pilgrim Dusmano contends that recompense, debt, guilt, punishment, and death are merely illusions within the framework of multiple alternate worlds (16). The mountain-moving feat performed by Polder Dossman is stated not to be an illusion (205).
Image
The representation or persona of an individual. Pilgrim Dusmano works to create a "special image" of himself, his "own ideated self" (59), partly through museum visits (61) and by cultivating his cult (75). This constructed image is contrasted with true personality (64). Albert Fineface offers to lodge Pelion Tuscamondo's "flame and image" in the collective unconscious (142, 144). The body of the knacker is transformed into an "authentic cult image" (100). Hector Bogus creates small animated images (182), and a sequence of nine eidolon images derived from a sculptor is described (196).
Imago Dei
An archetype mentioned alongside Orpheus, Child Hero, and Kore as having a "new arrival" counterpart (154).
Implosion House
A downtown museum catering to "unruly pictures or statuary or transfixes," providing an alternative to the Daylight Museum (59).
Impulse, Strange
The motivation behind Wilcove Funk (Doctor) concealing the "compensating thing" left behind by Pilger Tisman after his death (10).
Incandescence
A quality associated with powerful or numinous figures and objects. Pilger Tisman is described as an "incandescent cult figure" (6). Pilgrim Dusmano ascends into the "incandescent blue air" (24). The gilded statue of the knacker pulses with "golden incandescence" (100), and the molten gold from which it is made is "incandescently hot" (101).
Inconsiderate
The police brigadier's judgment of Pilger Tisman for taking an inconveniently long time to die (5).
Indian, Cigar-Store
See Cigar-Store Indian.
Indwellings, Cultish
Pilgrim Dusmano’s term for his rich and varied internal states or personal worlds, suggesting the external worlds might actually reside within him ("My personal and cultish indwellings are as varied as they are rich") (76).
Inner Being
The internal realm where Pilgrim Dusmano feels new worlds or life stages open like portals into rich suites of rooms (76).
Inner Circle
The roughly hundred scrivener or eidetic devils whose testaments gain publication throughout the Group Unconscious. Nine recently identified members correspond to nine recently identified elements; they are additions to the circle, not its entire membership (143–144).
Innocence
A quality required and certified for the office of Consul, possessed by Cyrus Evenhand (49, 66). Pilgrim Dusmano holds "no brief for innocence or goodness or spotlessness," considering them only of clinical interest (49). An "innocent victim," specifically a virgin, is deemed necessary by Pilgrim for the highest pleasure in destructive acts (67).
Instants
The subjective perception of time during moments of extremity. Pilgrim, while being attacked by Mut, finds the "final instants" are paradoxically "too long" compared to his previous experiences of dying (45).
Instrumental Guess
The term used for the death-monitors' tentative conclusion, based on their measurements, that memory, identity, or consciousness are the probable "weighable substance" carried forward by jumpers (3).
Integers, Correspondence
Parallel versions or representations of individuals existing on corresponding worlds or "orbs" (30). Pilgrim Dusmano believes his different integers aid one another (30).
Interworld
Pertaining to the routes, rules, and phenomena existing between different worlds. Interworld routes have specific rules enforced by non-human monitors (90). Cults hold significant ("blue chip") status in this domain (90).
Introspection Inn
A specialized museum located on Frankfort, catering to those with "a taste for his own bloody tongue" (59).
Intuition
A non-rational mode of perception or decision-making. Pilgrim Dusmano uses it to select Aubrey Pym as a messenger (33) and to determine the destination, Dongola (39). Cyrus Evenhand wrestles with his "dark intuition" regarding Pilgrim (25). Og Scath claims Polder's intuitive personality is the strongest element projected across worlds (199). Hector Bogus notes the Hand from Heaven possesses intuition, though its source is "otherwhere based" (190). Intuition is stated to be useless when confronting "amorphous stuff" like humpbacked flesh (195).
Intuitive Illogic
The paradoxical method employed by Pilgrim Dusmano and the knacker to rapidly process documents and set "deadfall traps" concerning the fortunes of Cyrus Evenhand's associates (95).
Intuitive Implementation
The process by which Polder Dossman's abdication commands are transmitted and arrive at their destinations across multiple worlds without conventional mailing or printing; it functions almost perfectly on his primary world but is less reliable across twelve billion worlds (199).
Iris Umbrella
The personal insignia of Noah Zontik, which Pilgrim Dusmano quickly affixes to his own mantle as a sign of being under Zontik's protection when Noah approaches (84).
Iron Meadows
An alternative name for the narrow province of the afterlife containing the Narrow Corner (121).
Iron Sky
The oppressive, low, metallic sky characteristic of the afterlife realm leading to the Narrow Corner (121, 123, 124, 128). It contains no sun (123).
Ivanova and McCresh
One of the great worldwide wholesaler firms mentioned as having its own "One Smooth Operation" for receiving world supplies (42).
JACOB DEL MAR
The brother of Maria del Mar and, like her, a follower of the cult figure Pilger Tisman (12). He mourns Tisman's death at the burial, keeping his distance but exhibiting silent, sobbing motion (12).
JAKE MARA
The name given to James Morey in the later stages of the narrative, after Polder Dossman's arrival in the stark, sharp-lined world (162). He is described as a "wan-wit young man" whose brains were scrambled during his time as a dog (162). He retains his loyalty to Polder, offering practical assistance like locating an "umbrella merchant" (Lorica) (167) and gathering intelligence on the hecklers (202). He expresses concern for Polder's well-being, protesting when doctors plan to disassemble him (195) and when the knacker proposes documenting his potential prophetic appearance (93).
JANIE
Pelion Tuscamondo's frequent companion on Cannes World (139). Possessing jeweled eyes and a jeweled mind (140), she is depicted with the "stereotyped perfection" of bright women within the Legacy (139). She precipitates a scandal at the Cannes Perpetual Animation Festival by exposing the use of an automaton instead of a live actress in the Jezebel drama (134, 137). She also acts as an intermediary, informing Pelion of a waiting visitor (145). See also JEANIE, JANIE-JEANIE.
JEANIE
Palgrave Tacoman's companion in a loge on Oraioi Polloi (147). She alerts Palgrave to the arrival of the ariel and the dog (Moira and Jake) (149). Seems to be the same character as JANIE.
JANIE-JEANIE
The paired form Janie-Jeanie marks the shift between the couch companions of Pelion and Palgrave at the opening of Chapter 11 (145).
JEHU'S COMPANIONS FINDING THE REMAINS OF JEZEBEL
A drama based on Doré illustrations, performed repeatedly at the Cannes Perpetual Animation Festival (135). It involves four companions interacting with four pieces of Jezebel's mutilated body (hand, foot, head, other hand), which ask riddles (135–137). The climax involves a revelation that one hand is the true head and the previous answers were wrong (137). The use of an automaton for Jezebel in one performance causes a major scandal (134, 137).
JEWELED EYES
A distinctive, non-human feature acquired by Pilgrim Dusmano after being attacked by Mut (54, 60); Mary Morey compares them to cracked glass or jewels (60), and the younger Pym child notes they are like a fly's eye "as big as a man" (54). Pilgrim acknowledges them as "idol-eyes" (63). They glitter when he contemplates bloodshed (65) and apparently allow Polder Dossman to see within people (79). The pan-morphous figure (Pilgrim/Polder) in the Narrow Corner possesses these or "cracked-glass eyes" (122). Pelion and Janie also have jeweled eyes, enabling them to watch multiple dramas simultaneously (140).
JEZEBEL
The central figure in the drama Jehu's Companions Finding the Remains of Jezebel (135). Her dismembered body parts (hand, foot, head, hand/true head) ask riddles after being injected with vita-flow (135–137). The role requires a live actress, and the substitution of an automaton (134), later replaced by the Marshal of Animations' unwilling daughter (138), causes significant disruption.
JOE SMITH
The inscribed signature on two of the three panels comprising the Dotty triptych (65).
JUDAS
Invoked by the curator regarding the betrayal of the Consul's identity (68). Pilgrim Dusmano gleefully embraces the term, praising the "red-murder rapture and the self-murder exultation that the real Judas-goat knew!" (68).
JUGLANS, CEREBRAL
The "remembering acorn"; a small nodule within the brain identified as the storage location for compressed memory "abridgments" and essences (5). Described as a composite of chemical fixes and electrical charges inhabiting patterned wrinkles and grooves (5), it is monitored and "marred" by Dr. Funk during Tisman's death-weighing (5). Its contents are extracted or "stolen" shortly after Tisman's physical death, causing the structure to collapse (9).
JUMP / JUMPER
See World-Jumper / World-Jumping.
JUMP-NO-MORE
Name mockingly given to the clarified man (Polder) by the flesh-smith/Holy Knacker in the Narrow Corner, signifying the entity's intention to end Polder's ability to change or escape (130).
Kangaroo (Sentence By)
A method of sentencing apparently available to Cyrus Evenhand, mentioned as an option for dealing with Pilgrim Dusmano, implying an irregular, perhaps summary or predetermined, judgment ("Even if we sentence him by kangaroo, it must be a fair trial and a fair sentence.") (26).
Katastrophy, Greek
Defined by Pilgrim Dusmano not as a tragedy but as a ritual "assault, the sack, the rape, the ruin, the destruction" (70). He describes its classic form involving the extended torture and eventual dismemberment of a virgin victim by the entire community, considering it more vital and dramatic than Roman games (70–71). He equates the killing assaults on unmasked Consuls to this practice, calling them "national solidarity acts" and "ritual murders to renew our blood" (71).
Kickback, Bi-Location
A phenomenon suggested as a possible cause of the constant, startling, shimmering effect observed at the commodity arrival floor (42).
Killing, Ritual
A recurring motif performed with specific methods and significance. Mut performs one on Pilgrim Dusmano, using a ritual knife to bleed him into a five-pint tankard (46), which Pilgrim recognizes as a "ritual killing" that affords him time to prepare for a world-jump (45). Pilgrim later uses a ritual stone knife to dispatch the Pym family as messengers to Supply (53–55). The killing of an unmasked Consul is described by Pilgrim as a necessary "ritual murder" for national renewal (71). Polder Dossman views the consumption of Blut's flesh as a "rich red ritual roast meat" (87).
King Boar
A champion boar, heralded by trumpeting sounds from the cedared mountains, that arrives to challenge Palgrave Tacoman after the lesser "scurrying boar" is killed (153, 156). It stands tall and emanates a red-brown fire against the blue foothills (156). Its tusks flash like white and gold fire in salute before charging down the coursing alley to meet Palgrave in a climactic clash (156). It kills Palgrave, kneeling beside the body in a pose resembling adoration (157).
Knacker
A specialist initially defined as dealing with animal carcasses (88), but the specific, talented individual engaged by Pilgrim Dusmano primarily processes the derelict fortunes, commerces, and affairs of the dead or soon-to-be-dead, such as Consul Cyrus Evenhand and his eight associates (88–89). This knacker, potentially a Lord Spiritual (89), uses advanced, possibly supernatural documentation techniques involving numinosity (93) and "intuitive illogic" (95) to consolidate these vast, multi-world assets (90, 94). He operates out of the All-Effects Hall (90) and claims descent from a lineage possessing secret knowledge (93). Asserting his claim ("It's all mine") to the Mut Cult's gold (96), he is betrayed by Pilgrim and killed by Mary Morey and James Morey, who eviscerate him and fill his body with molten gold; the gilded corpse becomes the HOLY KNACKER statue (97–101). He reappears post-death as an entity in the Narrow Corner (122).
Knife, Ritual
A slender, sharp blade wielded by the assailant Mut during his attack on Pilgrim Dusmano; used to open a vessel in Pilgrim's throat for the purpose of collecting his blood in a tankard (46).
Knife, Ritual Stone
A very large stone knife provided, seemingly by workmen, along with stone couches, for the ritual dispatch of the Pym family (53). Pilgrim uses it to cut the throats of Aubrey Pym (53), his wife (54), the elder child (54), and, with difficulty due to the child's struggling, the younger child (55). The knife is removed by workmen after the ritual (56).
Knife, Rubber
The derogatory nickname used by the genuine younger Lords Spiritual for Trenchant, the false Lord and spy, implying his ineffectiveness or lack of substance (79, 85).
Kobold Eyes
The type of small, brown, live eyes possessed by the wooden statuette carved by Groben; they are noted for their intense curiosity and slight edge of animosity (63).
La Spezia
The ninth named world of the Legacy, alongside Cannes, Oraioi Polloi, Hy-Brasail, Smart Set, Savona, Delectable, Theleme, and Luogo Perfetto. It is not a last chronological stage: the Nine Lives exist outside time and are never exhausted (133–146, 157).
Lad (in Camel Town)
A bright, young, local resident of Camel Town who engages Polder Dossman in a detailed conversation about the unique "second-best" status of camels and of Camel Town (163–167). He appears skeptical but impressed by Polder's Hand from Heaven display (163). He sells Polder his last camel (167) and reveals he has been "renovated," was likely an older man previously, and has been waiting for Polder (167). He identifies himself as Oak Scath (168).
Laughing God
The title Polder Dossman attempts to promote for his cult, based on a perceived local leaning toward the name (189). Hector Bogus dismisses Polder as incapable of the role, lacking real laughter and the "god type" (189).
Law, Dunlunk's Fifth
States: "Any action in any world will inevitably set up parallel actions in parallel worlds" (30). It is invoked to explain how shaping younglings on one world affects their counterparts elsewhere (30) and potentially explains Og Scath's sense of prior connection to Polder Dossman (175).
Law, Older
An unspecified law suggested by Og Scath as potentially predating Dunlunk's Fifth Law, possibly explaining the sense of recognition between individuals across parallel existences (175).
Lazarus
The subject of The Resurrection of Lazarus, one of the dramas performed on Cannes World based on Doré illustrations (140). In the drama he rises putrid and thirsty, with flesh falling off him, and stays that way (140). A cup of water is kept perpetually out of his reach by the audience-participation group mind (141, 142). He pays for the water with mortgage-gold derived from mortgaging his descendants' livings for seven generations (142). The cup eventually cracks from the gold coins, and Lazarus moans with his mouth in the sand (144). His "death thirst" or "hell thirst" continues even as the play and world change (146). Bosch, Hieronymus is noted perhaps not to have painted Lazarus's resurrection, but often painted Thirst (147).
Legacy
Specifically refers to the Nine Lives to La Spezia, a special compensation granted to the rich, permitting them nine additional lives of "almost hysterical" pleasure after death before potentially going to hell (133). This Legacy consists of Nine Moments (or momentums/powers), not segments of time (140), existing outside of time (160). The nine associated worlds (Cannes, Oraioi Polloi, HyBrasail, Smart Set, Savona, Delectable, Theleme, Luogo Perfetto, La Spezia) form a rivière or promontory shape (134). The "restrictive covenants" of the Legacy involve nine rich lives and worlds described as "pleasant little pieces of eternity" (132). Also mentioned is an "unusual Legacy" through which the pan-morph possesses nine special changes (127). Polder Dossman inherits a legacy via the Hand from Heaven gesture (168). Janie is described as one of the bright women who share in the Legacy (139).
Legion
Wilcove Funk (Doctor)'s description of the varied "topology of the other sides" encountered after death, implying vast and numerous potential afterlives or states (9).
Leper, The
An archetypal figure, whose company (along with the Boogerman and Body-and-Blood Giant) Palgrave Tacoman joins upon attaining cult status (155).
Leviathan
An archetypal figure mentioned alongside Simon Magus, Baubo, Demeter, Adonis, Alexander, and Broom-Witch (154).
Lifting Fingers
Components of a large hoist in the All-Effects Hall, used by James Morey to gently lift the knacker's gold-filled body (100).
Light Companion (in Death)
The role fulfilled by the good man Longram for Polder Dossman during the latter's final death process; Longram acts as Polder's proxy, absorbing some of the required spectacle and suffering (210–211).
Lime Flux
A substance used in melting gold; the distinctively foul odor associated with it is inexplicably present on the flesh-smith/Holy Knacker encountered by Polder in the Narrow Corner (131).
Live Eyes
The defining feature of the otherwise mediocre wooden statuette by Groben; described as small brown monkey or kobold eyes, snapped and crackled with curiosity and slight animosity (63). Mary Morey believes they are Pilgrim Dusmano's original eyes (63). They are extinguished ("drowned") when James Morey submerges the statuette in water (63–64, 71).
Lives (Nine Lives to La Spezia)
The rich's Legacy of nine lives or aspects of intense pleasure. These are nine Moments or powers without contact with time, not sequential lives that are exhausted. They persist even when another aspect of the person is in hell (133–146, 157, 208).
Loge
A private viewing box or area; Palgrave Tacoman enjoys leisure in one with Jeanie and Albrecht Fairbrow on Oraioi Polloi (147).
Logic
Associated strongly with Prime World, where it takes the form of "absolute logic of total delirium," permitting no deviation (21). Noah Zontik suggests prime people might be logical and dull (22), and calls the original Pilgrim "logical" (23). Pilgrim Dusmano professes to love "antilogy" and blinds himself to logic (117).
Longram
A good man to whom utterly barren land (Longram's Acres) had been ceded, which then flourished under his influence before being taken away again (206). He serves as Polder Dossman's "light companion" or proxy in death, having been "butchered by the mobs" and subjected to mutilation and torture gas, fulfilling the dramatic requirements Polder is too empty to meet (211). He is certainly dead before Polder's final end (213).
Lord of the Worlds
A divine or supreme entity. Apparently does not always know the best course regarding its own devices (20). Put tongues, fingers, styli, ethereal tinsel, ears, eyes, and the "perverse lobe" in humans for communication and subversion (107). Polder and Moira Mara seek means to convince the Lord of the Worlds of Polder's goodness (176).
Lords (Various)
Titles include Lords Temporal and Spiritual, Media and Eidetic Lords, Forum and Tinsel Lords, Lords of the Gnats, and Lords of the Zodiac. Their authority ranges from commerce and cult leadership to communication and archetypal influence. See the individual entries.
Lords of the Gnats
A group adept at finding minuscule faults ("gnats"). Pilgrim Dusmano admits membership but claims to be a "shouting of evil" rather than a whisper (81). They are part of the revolutionary coalition (81).
Lords of the Zodiac
A group of powerful archetypes. Og Scath asserts Polder Dossman has become one (197). Polder later claims this status (201, 203). Hector Bogus questions its validity (197). Polder considers becoming a "double Lord" representing the reconstituted signs of the camel and the boar (174).
Lords Spiritual
A title held by certain influential figures, seemingly connected to media, cults, and status (72). Pilgrim Dusmano is one (72, 73, 117). Lord Fairfronter is an "older and more elegant" one (75). Cordcutter is a "younger Lord Spiritual" (73, 74). The knacker is created one for his disposal services (94). Noah Zontik is one (84). Judas Raffels (Doctor) and John Augustine (Doctor) are Lords Spiritual (117). Trenchant is identified as a "false Lord Spiritual" (79, 83, 184). Polder addresses Hector Bogus as a "false Lord Spiritual" associated with Trenchant (184). They are part of the "permanent revolution against the people" (81).
Lords Temporal
A title held by Pilgrim Dusmano through his commerce and wealth (72). Noah Zontik also holds this title (84).
Lords, Eidetic
See Eidetic Lords.
Lords, Forum
Named by Trenchant as unable to find fault with Cyrus Evenhand (80) and part of the revolutionary coalition against the people (81).
Lords, Media
Powerful figures associated with mass media (143, 175). They are depicted as representing the anti-intellect and anti-illumination, the "true Lords of Unreason and Darkness" (107). They have become dominant in the absence of elected officials (107). They attack purpose, hate authority (107), and characteristically "rend and kill Consuls" (108). Their militia arrests Pilgrim (114–115). Noah Zontik predicts that they will destroy Pilgrim (108). They are unable to find fault with Cyrus Evenhand (80). Polder Dossman is allied with them (175), while Pilgrim is subject to their violence (108). They are part of the "permanent revolution against the people" (81). Hector Bogus is one (180). Polder addresses Bogus as Media Lord (185).
Lords, Tinsel
Young communicators associated with the Media Club (73). Unable to find fault with Cyrus Evenhand (80). Part of the revolutionary coalition (81).
Lords, Wiggly-Word
Polder Dossman's mocking term for Hector Bogus, grouping him with Eidetic, Media, and Advocate Lords (185).
Lorica
An adept and powerful man who sells worlds, systems, and galaxies, but is dismissed as an umbrella peddler (147–149). He warns Palgrave against buying archetypal membership in the infernal cartel and offers free participation in transcendence instead. Fairbrow and the Putty Dwarf undermine him. During the boar hunt he kills the first boar after his horse is impaled (152–153).
Lost Cantos (of Ovyde)
Clerk Ovyde constructed sheer heights of the Narrow Corner through the impetus of these works, which were subsequently burned as punishment for their "dangerous clarity" (127).
Louden Devil
A figure cited by Pilgrim Dusmano for the saying, "'It is more pleasure to kill one good man than a hundred indifferent men'" (67).
Luogo Perfetto
One of the nine worlds or states constituting the Nine Lives to La Spezia (134, 146).
Madness
Mentioned by Pilgrim Dusmano as the path of contemplating improbable failure (19). Noah Zontik refers to his own participation in the Dusmano cult as a "trivial madness" (84). The curator suspects Pilgrim is insane, though controllably so (61). Cyrus Evenhand refers to Pilgrim's perceived state near the end as "dingy madness" (76). Wut is possessed by "rage and mania" (49, 96, 125). The Curator feels the popular frenzy against the Consul is "insane" hysteria (67, 68).
Magnetic Effects
An attribute ascribed to cult figures like Pilger Tisman, contributing to their ability to attract followers (4).
Magnetic Man
One of the popular press designations for Pilgrim Dusmano (37), Pelion Tuscamondo (139), and Polder Dossman (203).
Maladroit
Pilgrim Dusmano's self-assessment of his clumsy, badly presented killing of Hut, which he feels needs to be revised for his cult's narrative (25).
Man-Tone
An alternative term for person-tone, specifically referring to Pilger Tisman's unique, powerful sonic signature (7).
Mania
The state possessing Wut, the "intelligent, calculating, canny, relentless, unforgetting, unforgiving man" encountered by the climbers in the Narrow Corner (125). Also the meaning of Wut's code name (49, 96, 112).
Manna
One of the substances, along with fishhooks, scattered by Polder Dossman's beneficent, dripping hands (170).
Mara, Jake
The name used for James Morey after Polder Dossman arrives in the stark, sharp-lined world (162). He is described as "wanwit," his brains having been scrambled (162). He accompanies Polder and Moira (162), locates the "umbrella merchant" Lorica (167), provides intelligence about the hecklers (202), and protests the planned "disassembly" of Polder (195).
Mara, Moira
The name used for Mary Morey after Polder Dossman arrives in the stark, sharp-lined world (162). She accompanies Polder and Jake (162), takes Polder's orders for investments and renting a grotto (164, 165, 166), attempts to manage Polder's cult affairs (172), asserts the necessity of belief in Polder's exaggerated status (198), gives Hector Bogus orders for Polder's glorification (192), critiques Polder's fear (208), and critiques the coin flip prank (209).
Margins
Defined by Pilgrim Dusmano as "spaces outside of accepted spaces"; he claims the apparent celestial locations of distant galaxies are notes written in these margins of sky maps due to lack of central space, requiring a new way of looking at them (15).
Marshal of Animations
The official responsible for ensuring live actors are used in the Cannes Perpetual Animation Festival (134). He is dragged before the elites after an automaton is used for Jezebel (137), confesses under duress that he substituted his own daughter due to a lack of other available actresses (138), and is subsequently beheaded and disarmed (139). A new Marshal is appointed (139).
Mask
Worn literally by Cyrus Evenhand when operating publicly (26, 49) and required for the office of Consul to ensure anonymity (69). The Consul's mask includes an eyepiece (69) and necessitates a "glottle" to disguise speech (69). Unmasking a Consul leads to certain destruction (70, 80). The term is used metaphorically by Judas Raffels, suggesting Pilgrim is a ruler masked by his followers (105) and that John Augustine (Doctor) has his own figurative mask (106). Pilgrim Dusmano eventually adopts a ritual mask instead of a face (69).
Masked-Consul System
The governmental structure preceding the narrative's main timeline, established after a period of assassinations, which relied on anonymous, masked Consuls making decisions from behind a veil (69).
Maugham
(Presumably W. Somerset Maugham) Cited as one of the projectors and shapers of the Narrow Corner afterlife (127).
Meat (of Walnut)
Pilgrim Dusmano is compared to a walnut containing only a "small and tasteless meat inside," implying a lack of substantial core despite his outward impact (31).
Media
The all-encompassing communication systems, linked by Og Scath to the Eidetic Lords (175) and the Media Lords (80). Polder claims expertise in modifying the "larger media flow" via his own unnamed medium (181). Noah Zontik asserts the Media represent the anti-intellect and anti-illumination (107). Defined by Bogus as including scatter-ray, focus-ray, ether-tinsel, and solid-light transmission, existing only in the "obscenity sort" (184). Responsible for the destruction of Consuls and predicted to destroy Pilgrim (108).
Media Club
An exclusive club where Pilgrim Dusmano holds honored membership (72). He dines there on mock-pizzle pie (75) and later consumes the roasted flesh of the henchman Blut (87). He interacts with various Lords Spiritual (Cordcutter, Fairfronter, Trenchant) within its premises (73–83) before fleeing from it near the narrative's end (110).
Media Lords
Figures who hold power through control of the Media (107). Associated with the Eidetic Lords (175). Considered by Noah Zontik to be the true Lords of Unreason and Darkness (107). They rule implicitly by election of the populace in the absence of formal officials (107). They attack purpose and hate authority (107), ritually destroy unmasked Consuls (108), and are predicted to destroy Pilgrim in the end (108). Their militia enforces their will (111, 114–115). Hector Bogus is identified as one (180, 185). Og Scath considers them allied with Polder (175). See also Lords, Media.
Media Lords and Eidolons
A linked group of themes concerning the manipulation of reality and identity through communication channels and artiﬁcial constructs. The Media Lords hold the real power in the postanarchic age, displacing formal government (107). Described by Noah Zontik as the "true Lords of Unreason and Darkness," representing the "anti-intellect" and "anti-illumination" (107), they derive power from collective projection rather than formal election (107). They attack purpose, hate authority (107), and ritually destroy ﬁgures of authority like the Consul when unmasked (108). Their tools include pervasive media (scatter-ray, focus-ray, ether-tinsel, solid-light transmission, all classiﬁed by Hector Bogus as "obscenity") (184) and armed Militia (111, 114). Closely allied are the Eidetic Lords (175, 181), seemingly involved in the creation and control of Eidolons, artiﬁcial beings or constructs often built on a human base (195, 196). Polder Dossman is repeatedly suggested or revealed to be such an eidolon (175, 183, 192). Hector Bogus, also an Eidolon Lord (180), demonstrates the power to create, animate, torture, and disanimate miniature eidolons (181–183) and links this to what Polder may be (182–183). The complex joins the novel's concerns with artiﬁciality, the manipulation of reality, the power that comes from controlling information and perception, and the possibility that central ﬁgures are manufactured.
Medici
Referenced as the family or individual who first perceived the Nine Worlds legacy (the rivière of jeweled worlds) in the Milky Way (133).
Medium
A system or channel of communication or influence. Hector Bogus discusses conventional media (181). Polder claims to have his own "unnamed medium," positioning himself as the "solar medium" to the conventional media's "planetaries" (181).
Meerschaum Cheese
A delicacy made from cetacean milk, eaten by Pilgrim Dusmano at the Media Club using special small-cupped, longhandled spoons (78).
Memory
Considered one of the primary "weighable" substances that can be carried forward after death, along with identity and consciousness (3). Its continuity requires attention during the death transition (17). Pilger Tisman successfully takes his memory with him (10). The knacker warns Pilgrim that his memory might not survive the transition to his new state (92). The Nine Worlds, existing outside time, leave no memory trace (160). Polder's own memory is depicted as unreliable or incomplete regarding past events (173) and details of contracts (161) or faces (175). The pan-morphic cultist in the Narrow Corner is described as being injured in mind and memory (123).
Memory Center
The physical locus of memory within the brain, specifically identified as the cerebral juglans or "remembering acorn," containing memory "abridgments and essences" (9). Pilger Tisman's is still intact immediately after death but is then "stolen" from (9).
Memory Failure
A condition that must be artificially introduced into routine processes, such as the dispatching of messengers, once the initial sense of urgency fades, in order to maintain the effectiveness of the ritual or procedure (52).
Menials
A class of servants or subordinates who, according to Palgrave Tacoman, must always be kept waiting (147).
Merope
Named as one of the Seven Sisters of the Pleiades (197). Also identified as one of the High Seven Dice Throwers, whose recent disappearance (nearly a decade prior) has created a vacancy in that group (197). Og Scath notes that within his "type-memory," Merope has manifested variously as female (seven times), hermaphrodite (seven times), and male (six times) (197). Merope's return to the sky is noted on the night Polder's cult peaks (198).
Message
Information conveyed between entities or worlds. Pilgrim sends a message to Supply via the Pym family (52), the words physically fading from the paper upon successful reception (55). Pilgrim intends his message to his followers across all worlds to be: "Don't think. Scintillate" (76). Polder believes the confusing message received by the Pym child must have been garbled (129).
Messenger(s)
Individuals dispatched, often ritually, to convey information or requests, particularly between Pilgrim Dusmano's operations and the entity known as Supply (33, 35). Pilgrim prefers "familied men" as messengers, considering their families "hostages" (34). The process involves a "grotesque act" (40), often with a stone knife (53), requires a specific mental state (39), and is shrouded in necessary haziness (40). Aubrey Pym and his family serve this role (38, 53–55). Spurgeon arrived as an "outre messenger" (36). Killing messengers is considered only a "technicality" by Pilgrim, not counted as a full kill (79).
Metacosmosis
Pilgrim Dusmano's term for the transmigration or travel between alternate worlds (16).
Metals, Screaming
Certain metals used in scientific instruments which, when subjected to great stress by torsion and heat, respond with wave patterns that seem to Polder Dossman like screams of agony (183).
Meteorological Manipulation
The technical term for phenomena like the Hand from Heaven, which Polder Dossman contracts for and activates (163, 168). Polder also attacks the hecklers using meteorological means (whirlwind, plasma explosion) (202).
Miasmic Fever
An atmospheric and physical condition attributed to Prime World (21). Prime people are likewise potentially "miasmic" (22).
Micromurder
Pilgrim Dusmano's term for the ritual drowning of the wooden statuette containing his former eyes, an act he views with "almost leprous interest" as a symbolic precursor or "sauce" for the grander destruction of the Consul (67). He prays never to weary of such pleasures (64).
Microscopes (Sophisticated)
Metaphorical tools used by the Media Lords to discern the "microscopic good" left in Pilgrim Dusmano, which paradoxically becomes the reason for his destruction (108).
Militia (of Media Lords)
The armed force serving the Media Lords. They battle the bravos of the Camel's Revenge (111). They enforce "Freedom of Entry" and "Freedom to Arrest" using a "flesh-and-blood warrant" (114). Led by a clear-voiced young commander (114), they pursue Pilgrim Dusmano based on Judas Raffels' betrayal (114), apprehend him (115), and execute him by trampling and dismemberment with horses (118). A sergeant from the militia interacts with Mary Morey and Noah Zontik regarding their desire to follow Pilgrim in death (119).
Milky Way
The galactic location where the "rivière or litany of jeweled worlds" constituting the Nine Lives legacy resides, visible to those with "jeweled eyes" (133).
Mind(s)
Frequently referenced as malleable, projectable, and interconnected. Pilgrim Dusmano manipulates the "plastic minds" of the young (31). Pilgrim's own mind is fragmented across thousands of others (103–104). Polder's mind becomes narrow and sterile (172) but holds superimposed outlines from past forms (130). The "group mind" of an audience can influence events in a drama (141, 142). The "underminds" of all creatures contain the "ocean" of the group unconscious (142, 144, 154). Minds can tire after nervous days (109).
Minutes, Weekly
The records of Pilgrim Dusmano's Commerce board meetings, which he insists on burning at the end of every week, claiming there is an undiscovered reason for doing so (35). This practice contributes to his associates' inability to recall recurring issues like adjustments to Supply (35).
Miracles
Actions beyond normal capabilities. Pilgrim Dusmano performs "small miracles" with his scarf (21, 23, 25) and Noah Zontik wonders if his "scruffy little handful of tricks and miracles" suffice to make him a cult figure (24). Polder Dossman performs massive public miracles (healing, blasting, withering, mind-blowing) during his evening gatherings (200).
Mirrored Image
Howard Praise expresses the fear that the "broken world" might become nothing more than a reflection of the "broken us and broken Pilgrim" (105).
Mistignette Mushrooms
A food item, eaten by Pilgrim Dusmano along with bleu cheese on the veranda at the Media Club (84).
Mock-Pizzle Pie
A prestigious and expensive dish eaten by Pilgrim Dusmano at the Media Club (75). Made from "clutter-buck" rather than bull, it is enjoyed by "current people" as a preference even when genuine pizzle is in season (75).
Mockery
A characteristic expression of Pilgrim Dusmano, described as "curling and pleasant" on his mouth (115, 203). Pilger Tisman's resurrected person-tone is also said to possess a "biting mockery" (9).
Model, Experimental
Hector Bogus's assessment of Polder Dossman, suspecting he is a flawed creation of some experimenter on another world (195). Doctors analyzing Polder's body also conclude he was likely an experimental model made by several experimenters (212).
Moloch
An archetype mentioned in a list including Hermes, Homunculus, and Fisherman (155).
Momentums
Powers; the Nine Worlds legacy (Nine Lives to La Spezia) is described as consisting of Nine Moments, defined as nine momentums or powers, existing outside of time (140).
Money Giants
Powerful, wealthy individuals who, unlike Pilgrim Dusmano, primarily lust after fortunes rather than the "flesh-meat bodies" of the deceased (95). They would normally contest Pilgrim's claim to Cyrus Evenhand's fortune through "gauged snarlings and bluffings" (95).
Monitors (Non-Human)
Entities assigned to enforce the rules governing travel and commerce on interworld routes (90).
Monkey Eyes
The type of small, brown, live eyes observed in the wooden statuette carved by Groben (63).
Monster
What Polder Dossman realizes he has become within the "many-monstered interior ocean" of the collective unconscious (170).
Monstrals
Extraordinary phenomena, along with spectacles, prodigies, and miraculi, demanded by Moira Morey as necessary elements for Polder Dossman's thriving cult (195).
Moonlight
The required illumination for performances of Jehu's Companions Finding the Remains of Jezebel on Cannes World; a real moon is used, its top half obscured by clouds (135).
Morey, James
The brother of Mary Morey (60). Often observed lingering in the shadows while Mary occupies the sunlight, leading to speculation that he is her shadow (60). Despite recognizing Pilgrim Dusmano's artificiality, he stays a leading member of the Dusmano cult (71). He acts as an assistant to Pilgrim, filling a crock with water to drown the statuette with Pilgrim's former eyes (63) and later operating the hoist and furnace during the ritual creation of the Holy Knacker statue (97, 99, 100). He is awed and frightened by the statue's unnatural glow (101). Afterward, James finds the "gold lust and the blood lust" drain out of him, leaving him sobbing silently in the shadows (101). He sometimes speaks "out of the shadows," offering observations on Dusmano's nature (62) or the state of the drowning statuette (67). He attends the final cult gathering (103) and affirms the belief in Pilgrim's eventual return in a parallel form (104). After his death alongside Mary, he manifests as the HOUND servitor in the afterlife (122). See also Mara, Jake.
Morey, Mary
A student and leading follower of Pilgrim Dusmano, sister of James Morey. She helps create the Holy Knacker, follows Pilgrim into death, and appears as the ariel in the Narrow Corner. In the later sharp-lined world she is Moira Mara. Her devotion includes clear recognition of Pilgrim's cruelty and artificiality (18–19, 60–71, 92–101, 112–129, 162–209).
Morning Students
The group Pilgrim Dusmano teaches or cultivates early each day at Rampart University (29), including Mary Morey and James Morey (60).
Mortal Coil
The phrase appears in the opening “World-Jumper's Ballad,” setting ordinary mortal existence against the possibility of jumping off a world (1).
Mottoes (of Jumpers)
Pilgrim Dusmano quotes one ("To be in the right frame of mind is a requirement for arriving at a new frame of existence") but immediately realizes he has never known any jumpers besides himself and so cannot know their mottoes (39).
Mountain-Moving
The "unfakable" proof of power demanded of Polder Dossman by the hecklers (204). Despite warnings and advice against it (204), Polder accepts the challenge and successfully moves Shining Mountain (205). The event is cataclysmic, involving earthquakes, airquakes, skyquakes, heat blasts, dust towers, decapitated fountains, unnatural lightning, roaring boulders, breaking roots, and flaming trees (205). The moving mountain kills the main heckler groups (205). This act destroys the Hand from Heaven, triggers destructive floods, dissolves Polder's cult (206), and leaves Polder psychically and physically "finished" (207).
Mountains
Pelion Tuscamondo orders various types (Gothic, Doré, menacing, Anti-Lebanon, Hermon, Hauran) as backdrops for his Resurrection of Lazarus animation (141). Polder Dossman claims the power to move mountains if public opinion is first manipulated (187). See Mountain-Moving and Shining Mountain.
Mourners of Durandarte
The subject of a Doré illustration used as the basis for a drama presented on Cannes World (140).
Muck
A defining characteristic of Prime World (21). Prime people are described as potentially "mucky" (22).
Muckman, Randal
A multimedia reporter contacted by Pilgrim Dusmano via voxo (57). Pilgrim gives him the information "Cyrus Evenhand is Consul" (58). Muckman attributes the information to a "high, wide. . . and handsome source" (knowing it to be the devious Pilgrim) and broadcasts it, triggering the main crisis (58). He is later present at the final cult gathering in the windowless room (103).
Mud
The characteristic substance of Prime World (21). Also part of the debris left of Pilgrim Dusmano after he is torn apart by horses (118). Polder Dossman, after achieving clarified form, wonders despairingly if he is still "made out of mud" (130).
Multi-Media Productions
The name appearing on a small advertisement attached to the pointing finger of the Hand From Heaven ("Sky-Signs and Prodigies by Multi-Media Productions. Call us!"); Polder finds this detail displeasing (170).
Multiplicity of Worlds
A core concept discussed extensively. Scientists initially posited billions scattered through space (13); "fringies" and "pseudos" conceived of them co-existing locally as "tree-worlds" or "branch-worlds" (14). Pilgrim Dusmano reconciles these, claiming billions exist simultaneously "right here right now" (15) and are the basis for his philosophy of amorality and worldjumping (16). Noah Zontik rejects the idea of multiple worlds (104).
Murder, Microcosmic
A term appearing in the epigraph for Chapter 5, Museum-Munchers' Daybook (57). Also used by Pilgrim Dusmano to describe the drowning of the statuette (67).
Murk
The defining atmospheric quality of Prime World (21). Prime people are likewise potentially "murky" (22). Moira Morey suggests filling the eyes of the watchers above the Narrow Corner with murk to render them invisible (122).
Murkiness
An aesthetic quality some might seek in art; the Daylight Museum forbids "second-hand murkiness" (59).
Murky Headquarters
The operational base from which Cyrus Evenhand operates and where he wrestles with his "dark intuition" regarding Pilgrim (25).
Museum
Several are mentioned: the Daylight Museum (59, 60, 61, 63, 65, 66, 106), the Dismal Den (59, 60), the Implosion House (59), Tom Fool's (59), and the Introspection Inn (59). Pilgrim Dusmano frequents museums as part of constructing his public image (59).
Museum-Munchers' Daybook
The source of the epigraph for Chapter 5 ("An idol-thing with jewel eyes. . .") (57).
Music, Clarence
The curator of the Daylight Museum (61, 103). He engages with Pilgrim Dusmano and the Moreys about art, shadows, sanity, and the nature of the Consul (61–63, 66–67, 69–71). He is present during the final cult gathering (103) and asks why the two Doctors Medical are drawn to Pilgrim (106).
Musk Ox
Its hair is noted for unequaled fineness, though camel hair was used first for brushes; its hide is also mentioned (165).
Mustard (Gas)
An "old ritual gas," also known as Yperite, used in executions designed to cause discomfort (2). Pilger Tisman is executed using this gas (2).
Mut
The code name for one of Cyrus Evenhand's eight henchmen, signifying "courage (but not, apparently, the carefulness)" (49). He is the powerful assailant who attacks Pilgrim Dusmano, performs a ritual bleeding, collects the blood in a five-pint tankard (45–47), but Pilgrim secretly takes his wallet (47–48). He later reports to Cyrus Evenhand, offers to procure tissue samples from Pilgrim Dusmano, drinks the collected blood (50–51), and is revealed to have the public identity of Satterfield ("Strength-in-Serenity," "Strength-in-Purity," "Mr. Holiness-through-Strength") (48, 74). His immense fortune and associated cult (Mut Cult) are subsequently plundered by Pilgrim and the knacker (90, 91, 92, 96). Pilgrim Dusmano plans to have Mut killed and his body turned into a gold-plated cult statue (91).
Mut's wallet
"My blood for drachmas" (48).
Mutational Jump
A sudden biological or metaphysical shift; Pilgrim Dusmano claims his acquisition of jewel eyes resulted from one occurring that day (77).
Mutilated
Jezebel's body is presented as such in the Cannes drama (135). The good man Longram is mutilated "in a dozen painful ways" by mobs before serving as Polder's proxy (211). Mary Morey mutilates the knacker's body while eviscerating it (97).
Narrow Corner
A location in the afterlife province known as the Iron Meadows or the Camel's Eye (121). It is depicted as a treacherous, pulsating, steep pass (124) formed not by hands but by the projected intuitions of countless bruised and dislocated souls (127), influenced by figures like Alighieri, Christ in Matthew, Maugham, Blake, Demetriades/Finnegan, and Ovyde (127). Legends describe it as a knife-edge precipice of glare ice (or molten rock) flanked by bottomless chasms where tooth-clattering spirits wait to devour souls and slake revenges (125). It is the setting for a chaotic battle involving the pan-morphic Pilgrim/Polder, the ariel, the dog, the Holy Knacker (body-smith), Wut (maniac), and the Pym child (fire-drake) (122–131). The body-smith attempts to trap Pilgrim there in a final form (126), and Polder falls into its chasm (132).
National Barley
A commodity sourced from Supply, subject to quality control concerns (e.g., being too bland or too sharp in taste) discussed by Pilgrim Dusmano's commerce board (36).
National Solidarity Acts
Pilgrim Dusmano's term for the ritual killing assaults on unmasked Consuls, viewing them as acts that renew the collective blood (71).
Neat's-Foot Oil
Compared unfavorably to the "old second-place camel oil" by the local lad in Camel Town (166).
Needle, Eye of the
Referenced in relation to the biblical edict concerning the rich, camels, and the kingdom of heaven (121, 133). The Narrow Corner is sometimes called "the Camel's Eye," linking it to this fable (124).
Neo-Creational Procedures File
The cited source of an epigraph comparing the creations of the god Electronus favorably to those of the "Old God" (13).
Nets
Metaphorical tools used by the death-monitors (Wilcove Funk; Austin, Jon; Jude Ravel; etc.) in their attempt to capture the escaping consciousness, memory, or identity of dying individuals like Pilger Tisman (7, 11). Tisman successfully evades or escapes these nets (7, 11).
Newest of the New Men
A designation applied to Pilgrim Dusmano for his role in the Media's production of "cultic and electronic personality" and the displacement of "uncultic and unelectronic persons" (73).
Nine Lives to La Spezia
The special Legacy of the rich: nine lives of intense pleasure in worlds outside time. The apparent promise of nine lives before hell is qualified by the insistence that nobody ever uses them up. Nine aspects continue in pleasure even while a tenth suffers elsewhere (133–146, 157, 208).
Nine Worlds to La Spezia
The collection of nine distinct locations or states (Cannes, Oraioi Polloi, Hy-Brasail, Smart Set, Savona, Delectable, Theleme, Luogo Perfetto, La Spezia) that constitute the Nine Lives legacy (134, 146). They exist outside of time and leave no memory (160). Death within them is a "pleasant coma" (157). Polder Dossman seeks confirmation of his presence within them (208). Hector Bogus confirms Polder is present nine times across the Nine Worlds (208). Polder is asked by Bogus if he seeks to return there from what he believes to be Prime World (207).
Nodule (Containing)
Refers to the cerebral juglans, which contains the memory patterns and seems "always on the nervous edge of explosion" (6).
Nonchromatic
Describes colors within Pilger Tisman's aura (specifically "a hundred nonchromatic colors") (7). Also used to describe an aspect of Tisman's call-tone, which is translated into audio (6).
Nonsuches
A category of people (along with fringies and pseudos) who correctly understood alternate worlds to occupy the same local space (14).
Not So Dead as All That
One of the special categories proposed by the coroner for classifying the state of deceased world-jumpers, acknowledging their potential for continued existence elsewhere (11). Pilger Tisman is buried regardless of whether he fits this description (12).
Notes (on Hand from Heaven)
Refers to the small advertisement ("Sky-Signs and Prodigies by Multi-Media Productions. Call us!") visible on the pointing finger of the Hand from Heaven activated by Polder Dossman; Polder finds the note displeasing and considers having it removed (170).
Numinous / Numinosity
A quality of supernatural presence and exceptional strength. The knacker gives Mary and James Morey a golden numinous glow and projected faces so they can collect the Mut cult's gold. The strength is temporary and fades during the assault on the knacker (92–100).
O'Basham
The family name displayed on Og Scath's giant-sized coat of arms; Og claims to be the only one titled "O'Basham" and that he originates from a place called Basham, unlocatable in modern geography (177).
Obscenity
According to Hector Bogus, the sole defining characteristic of all existing presses, Media publications, transmissions, art, argument, and ethics; he claims obscenity is necessary to loosen tongues that would otherwise be tied (184). Pilgrim Dusmano previously swore by "every obscenity" (188).
Ocean
A vast, underlying psychic medium or repository composed of the personal testaments of devils (143). It infuses every mind, memory, creature, and manifestation (142, 144). Pelion Tuscamondo pays to publish his "flame and image" into this ocean (142, 144). Polder Dossman becomes an archetype within this ocean (197), which is also described as the "many-monstered interior ocean" (170).
Ocean (Metaphorical)
The novel uses oceans both for unformed being and for the psychic medium underlying minds. See Amorphous Ocean, Ocean, and Group Unconscious / Folk Ocean.
Omega Pattern
A brain wave pattern humorously described as "zero per second," indicating brain death; Pilger Tisman's brain waves enter this state upon his physical death (9).
One Smooth Operation
The unexplained, seemingly effortless process by which vast quantities of supplies manifest at the commodity arrival floors of major worldwide wholesalers like Dusmano's Commercial Enterprises, Jones and Cloud, Chung and Ching, Ivanova and McCresh, Izzersted and Panenero (42–43). It does not involve visible transport or conventional teleportation receivers (42).
Oraioi Polloi
One of the nine worlds constituting the Nine Lives to La Spezia legacy (134, 146). It features the Atrium Theater where dramas like the Resurrection of Lazarus and the Adoration of the Boar are presented (147, 157). Death there is described as a "pleasant coma" (157). Palgrave Tacoman, Jeanie, Albrecht Fairbrow, and Lorica are present there (147).
Orbs, Corresponding
Parallel worlds which contain "correspondenceintegers" or parallel selves (30).
Out There / In Here
Pilgrim's juxtaposition of cosmic space with familiar local space. He contends that their measures are identical and says that neither contains nor extends beyond the other (15).
Overload
A technical failure cited by Hector Bogus as the reason for Polder Dossman's catastrophic breakdown during the mountainmoving incident; the overload mechanism failed to blow, causing "the creature" to blow instead (212).
Ovyde, Clerk
A figure cited as having constructed "sheer heights" of the Narrow Corner through the "strong impetus of his Lost Cantos," which were later burned as punishment for their "dangerous clarity" (127).
Pain
An element emphasized in punishments and experiences. Pilger Tisman is sentenced to die with discomfort and experiences "absolutely ghastly discomfort" (2), though Jude Ravel (Doctor) notes he "endured the pain well" (2). Hector Bogus finds "fun" in manufacturing small animations for the specific purpose of studying their "exquisite and intense response and appreciation of pain," which he deems eternal to the animation (182). The Polder-sliver experiences intense agony (214).
Paint-Picture Camel!
An insult shouted by local children at Polder Dossman, mocking his perceived artificiality (169).
Pallidness, Pulsating
One of the unusual visual effects noted in Pilger Tisman's complex aura (7).
Pan-Morphous
Descriptive term for the main character (Pilgrim/Polder) upon entering the afterlife realm leading to the Narrow Corner, indicating a nature expressed in multiple, superimposed, shifting outlines (ape, teras, troll, man, frog), seeming brittle yet manipulable (122). This pan-morphic cultist is injured, vulnerable, and battles various entities (123, 126).
Panenero
One of the great worldwide wholesaler firms mentioned as having its own "One Smooth Operation" for receiving world supplies (42).
Panic
An emotional state associated with disorientation and death. Pilgrim experiences "balanced panic" during Mut's attack (45). James Morey notes the wooden statuette is in panic while being drowned (67). Mary Morey predicts Pilgrim/Polder will panic if his followers are not present when he arrives in the afterlife (119).
Panther in the Desert, The
The title of a drama based on a Doré illustration, performed on Cannes World (140).
Paper Camel!
An insult shouted by local children at Polder Dossman, implying he is artificial or lacks substance (169).
Paraclete
A term used by Pilgrim Dusmano for the replacement or alternate self he can send after himself when he departs a world (77). Lord Fairfronter ironically questions if Pilgrim is a Christus to be sending a Paraclete (104).
Parallel
Used to describe worlds, actions, persons, selves, and bodies existing concurrently but usually separately across different dimensions or aspects (30, 55, 77, 104). Dunlunk's Fifth Law posits that actions inevitably create parallel actions (30). Pilgrim shapes "correspondence-integers" on parallel orbs (30). He considers his "sticks" to be parallel persons (77) and claims nothing of himself will be lost as he can be recognized in another parallel (78). Such existences may be linked by laws older than Dunlunk's (175). The concept explains shared or reflected memories between individuals like Dusmano and Noah Zontik, or Polder and Og Scath (32, 175).
Parchment
Fine split lambskin is considered paramount, but camel parchment has been used by holy prophets (166).
Parkland
A fine area maintained by Pilgrim Dusmano near his headquarters, where he walks to "pasture his always ravening mind" (37). Pilgrim Dusmano is later hiding in a thorn thicket along the parkway bordering this region (111, 114, 116).
Parting Cup
A ritual vessel, filled with quince wine, used in the Dusmano cult meeting ceremony (112). Judas Raffels (Doctor) drinks from it directly, bypassing the ritual serving (113).
Passageway (Smoky)
The approach to the Narrow Corner, lined with smoky stalactites that seem to intone verses (124). It is crumbly, slippery, and composed of lava-flow (124).
Passing (Selective)
An oddity noted about even good people, referring to their ability to easily pass large objects (like camels) through their systems while straining excessively over insignificant ones (gnats) (75, 72).
Pasteboard Pig!
An insult shouted by local children at Polder Dossman, identifying him with his secondary totem animal, the boar (169).
Patsy World
Polder Dossman's suspected assessment of the sharp-lined world where Polder arrives, anticipating easy exploitation ("patsy-picking time") (166).
Pattern
A term used in several contexts: 1. The underlying structure or template of memory contained within the cerebral juglans, holding power even when empty of detail (6). Taking these patterns is like stealing holes or tunnels (6). Pilger Tisman's memory deposit collapses when its pattern is removed (9). 2. The formative principle for commodities arriving at the trading floor; a student theorizes half the pattern must come from the ambient and half from another world via displacement (41–42). 3. The specific brainwave patterns (delta) emitted by Pilger Tisman during his death (8).
People-Grinder
Pilgrim Dusmano's apprehensive term for the large grinder-shredder machine that appears before the Pym family's dispatch (52). He subsequently uses it to dispose of their bodies (56).
Perilous Pass, The
Subject of a Doré illustration, elements of which are said to have influenced the depiction of the Narrow Corner (140). Basis for a drama performed on Cannes World (140).
Perpetual Animation Festival
See Cannes Perpetual Animation Festival.
Perplexity, Person-Formed
Description of the lingering influence or trace left by an individual, compared to a persistent odor in vacated premises (193).
Person
Defined circularly by Pilgrim Dusmano as one of the "persons of these wide-eyed groups" who believe in alternate worlds (14). Also used as a fundamental unit subject to limitation (the "prime count") in some beliefs (14). The nature of a person is questioned regarding the Tisman/Dusmano complex (146).
Person-Tone
The unique sonic signature of an individual, equivalent to call-tone (4, 6). Pilger Tisman's is powerful and complex (6). Its reappearance outside the body signifies successful world-jumping (7, 9).
Personal Baggage
Minimal items (memory, identity, consciousness) carried forward from death by some individuals, historically leading to harmless ghost appearances (3).
Personal Spectrum
The unique range of colors translated from an individual's aura; Pilger Tisman's is considered unprecedentedly complex and unique (7).
Personality
Considered a quality distinct from a mere physical presence or constructed image. Pilgrim Dusmano is described by the narrator as empty of real personality (73). The curator states that an unshaped block of stone or canvas showing personality is worthless to an artist, as it cannot accept art (64). Polder Dossman's intuitive personality is the strongest element projected across worlds (199). Polder Dossman is suspected of having only projected personalities (171).
Pilgrim Staff
A rare insignia, "smaller than a mote in the eye," worn by Lord Fairfronter (along with the Golden Shovel Pip), signifying his connection to the Dusmano cult and his dedication to establishing the Pilgrim image (75, 84).
Pilgrim, Peter (of Myth)
A legendary figure whom the spy Trenchant accuses Pilgrim Dusmano of not being, calling Dusmano a "falser Pilgrim" (82). This accusation strikes Dusmano, forcing him to confront his own authenticity in the "postreason era" (82). Hector Bogus also refers to this figure when challenging Polder's identity (185).
Pioneer of Pleasure
A title associated with Pilgrim Dusmano, acknowledging his status as a certified Lord Spiritual due to his "scatterfield philosophy," promotion of "dynamic rutting," and "kinetic taste" (73).
Pipe Clay Soup
An innovative food consumed by Pilgrim Dusmano at the Media Club, made from "vermicules that burrow into that white clay," flavored only with Holland onions and a salting of the clay itself (73).
Pit
A bottomless chasm flanking the Narrow Corner (125). Also, the "underlay" beneath the worlds, identified as a source of power and influence where Aurelion holds court (148). The flesh-smith threatens to throw Jump-No-More (Polder) into the pit that "has no way out" (130), but Polder defeats the knacker and throws him into it (131).
Plague-Rats Behind the Masks
The label used by the Media Lords to denounce Gut, Blut, and Flut, the unmasked associates of Consul Cyrus Evenhand (73).
Plastic
Descriptive term for the minds of the young, implying malleability, used by Pilgrim Dusmano (31). Also used for the "humpbacked flesh," a "less-than-human substratum" possibly composing part of Polder Dossman (195).
Plasticene-Gray Clay
Material, born of swamps and fired in Hell, used to make expensive, passionate, and powerful mood-piece crockery observed by Pilgrim in Sheol Shuckins or the Dismal Den (60).
Players
Participants in the confusing, experimental theater of the afterlife arena in the Narrow Corner (125).
Pleasure
The primary motivation for Pilgrim Dusmano (31) including his consumption of Blut's flesh (87). It encompasses manipulating minds (31), killing arrogant men (38), the "corporate murder-pleasure" of destroying a Consul (50, 67, 71), witnessing destruction (83), and consuming "abominations" (87). Pilgrim plans his pleasures, including scheduled insanity (61). He seeks the alternative (swift vs. slow death) that gives the most pleasure (69). Damnation is considered the "ultimate pleasure" (85). The Nine Lives legacy offers "almost hysterical" or "intolerable" pleasure (133, 146).
Pleasure Man
Pilgrim Dusmano is widely known as such, deriving enjoyment even from imaginative defamations (58).
Pleiades, Seven Sisters of the
Merope is identified as one of this group (197).
Plugs By Suggs
The stamp appearing on the bogus-gold plug Polder Dossman uses to fill a cured tooth, indicating the item came from a local dental supply house (200).
Pluralized
The state of having realized and enriched one's concentric aspects and personalities; the inhabitants of Camel Town's world have not pluralized themselves (163).
Polder-Sliver
The last remnant of Polder Dossman, a fluttering piece of his heart, kept animate and tortured by Hector Bogus in a cabinet before finally ceasing (214–215).
Police, Brigadier of
An official present at Pilger Tisman's deathweighing (1). He displays impatience (5), expresses personal hatred for Tisman possibly influenced by Tisman's powerful enemy (7), demands the silencing of Tisman's mocking post-mortem tone (7), and angrily denounces the proceedings as "bungled" when Tisman successfully world-jumps (10). Hector Bogus later holds this office during Polder Dossman's death (211).
Polloi, Oraioi
See Oraioi Polloi.
Poltergeists
Referenced metaphorically by Noah Zontik to describe the slow movement of objects on Prime World (23).
Post Age
Noah Zontik's term for the current era, following the period of full anarchy, characterized by the rejection of overt rule and the necessity for rulers (like the Consul) to be anonymous and masked (105).
Post Boy
A functionary on Oraioi Polloi carrying a brass horn that shows animated scenes. He alters a scene of Palgrave's death at great cost to his own strength. He later announces a newly synthesized element and blows the Giant Overture (150–154).
Postanarchic (Age/Era/World)
The time period or state of reality in which much of the narrative occurs (80, 94, 105, 175, 197). Characterized by the rejection of overt rule, the necessity of masked authority (Consul), the power of Media Lords, the rise of cults, and a pervasive "age of unreason" (81, 105). Thieves' honor is considered "patchy" in this era (97). Noah Zontik suggests it is a peculiar state, possibly not entered by most worlds (105). Pilgrim/Polder is considered potentially the "correct godlet" for this age (105).
Postreason Era
A time period mentioned by Pilgrim Dusmano, within which clear and simple unreason allows him to still identify as the authentic Peter Pilgrim of myth (82).
Power Reception
The point where transmitted force or influence is received; Noah Zontik questions whether evil originates in the transmitter (Pilgrim) or at the point of reception (the cult members) (103).
Praise, Howard
Initially a student hesitant about Pilgrim Dusmano's chaotic nature (16, 19), he is nonetheless compelled into the cult (19). He is still a member at the final events (103), stoutly defying the militia before Judas Raffels betrays Pilgrim's location (114), and mutters about "Heavy footsteps" approaching (113).
Precocious Children
Pilgrim Dusmano acknowledges he never knows how to talk to them (54), especially when they defy him, like the younger Pym child (54).
Prescience (Death)
A state prior to death where bruised and dislocated persons' intuitions and projections can influence or manufacture afterlife realities like the Narrow Corner (127).
Present World
The term used to distinguish the current reality from other worlds or aspects, such as Dongola (55).
Presses, Obscenity
According to Hector Bogus, the only kind of printing or media presses that exist, necessary because only obscenity can loosen tongues for art, argument, or ethics (184). Polder is warned against using them for his naive cult advertisements (184).
Pressmen Lords
One of the groups of Lords unable to find fault with Consul Cyrus Evenhand (80). Part of the coalition declaring permanent revolution against the people (81).
Prime Count
A hypothetical limit on the number of "prime souls" available in the universe, posited in some belief systems as around three and a half billion (14). This belief maintains that most souls are already embodied or that many apparent persons are merely reflections (14).
Prime People
The original, non-derivative individuals, contrasted with the multitudes of "derivative people" or "shadow souls" (14, 21). Pilgrim Dusmano allows "barely room" for them in his theory (22) and considers himself one (22). Noah Zontik hypothesizes they might be sordid, crabbed, fetishistic, logical, dull, narrow, murky, mucky, miasmic, possessing sinewy hands and delirious minds, like Prime World (22). He later identifies them with the inhabitants of the "uninfused world, the grubby world, the spiritualist world, the quack world, the Fortean world" (23).
Prime Souls
The original, limited number of souls (perhaps 3.5 billion) contrasted with "shadow souls" or "derivative persons" who lack true force (14).
Prime World
A hypothetical foundational reality (20). Described by Pilgrim Dusmano as the potential "narrow foul chance" or downside to world-jumping (20), the dullest possible world, where mythology is sordid reality, compensation is extracted, facts are hard without buoyancy, metaphors are material, and logic is absolute delirium (21). It is murk, mud, miasmic fever, featuring sinewy gripping hands and a low sky (21). Escape is impossible, with only two ways off: one being Hell (21). It's the anchor of eschatological things (21). Worrying about being on Prime World is a sign of its influence (183). Og Scath believes Polder thought he was on Prime World when he died (213). Polder fears he might fall into Hell from it (206, 208). Moira Morey argues probability proves their current world isn't Prime World (208).
Prismatic Room
A location within the Personage Club where Pilgrim Dusmano and Noah Zontik converse (20). Pilgrim departs directly through its walls in flight (24).
Private Conveyance
The means by which John Augustine (Doctor) makes his "way out of life" after the deaths of Noah Zontik and Judas Raffels (120).
Prodigies
Extraordinary beings or phenomena. When they meet "beyond life and time" (i.e., in the afterlife), they are like small boys bluffing murderously (123). Also used for spectacles Polder performs (200) and demanded by Moira for his cult (195).
Projection(s)
Emanations or creations stemming from an individual or group mind. Noah Zontik suggests Pilgrim Dusmano is a projection of a dull person (23), then of hundreds of bright persons, and ultimately of millions (103). He posits that the Media Lords are projections of the collective populace (105). He describes Pilgrim's origin as being in the "compensating imagination" of a prime person (23). The Narrow Corner is a projected image made solid by its own fire, an anthology of personal projections (127). Hypnotic projections, like the knacker's induced appearance change in the Moreys, wear off (94).
Prop Men
Derogatory term used by the head heckler for Polder Dossman's companions (Og Scath; Moira Morey; James Morey) (204).
Prophesied Guardians
The role the knacker assigns to Mary Morey and James Morey through fabricated documentation, making them appear as honored, deceased Mut Cult members returning from the grave to oversee the cult's gold, thus facilitating its transfer (93).
Prophetic Frightfulness
The quality of Anastasia Demetriades's recounting of the Narrow Corner, which Finnegan, Count then visualized and projected onto the place (127).
Protection (Flawed)
A recurring motif centered around designated guardians assigned to shield volatile protagonists, characterized by reluctance, ineffectiveness, and often shared destruction.
